- easy: 한 가지 명시적 개념·규칙만으로 푼다. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 추론은 한 단계 이하이다. 어휘·문장은 평이하다. 오답 3개는 해당 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 규칙을 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보이는 전형적 오개념이어야 한다(말도 안 되는 선택지 금지).
- 세부 기술 힌트: 두 문장 사이 관계(대조·추가·결과·예시)가 명시적 어휘 단서로 분명한 문제. 선택지는 서로 다른 관계를 나타내는 전환어 4개.
c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Wassily Kandinsky color-sound synesthesia theory and abstract expressionism emotional abstraction in early twentieth-century modernism

g.passage: The painter Wassily Kandinsky believed that colors could produce sounds in the mind, much as musical notes do. In his 1911 book Concerning the Spiritual in Art, he linked specific colors to specific instruments. ______ he described a bright yellow as resembling the sharp blast of a trumpet and a deep blue as sounding like a cello.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.design: 앞 문장의 일반 진술(특정 색과 특정 악기를 연결함)을 마지막 문장이 구체적 사례(노랑-트럼펫, 파랑-첼로)로 보여 주는 예시 관계 한 단계 추론으로 구성했다. 오답은 대조·결과·대체의 전형적 오개념이다.
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 칸딘스키가 특정 색을 특정 악기와 연결했다는 일반적 진술이고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 노란색을 트럼펫에, 파란색을 첼로에 비유한 구체적 사례이다. 따라서 예시를 이끄는 A가 정답이다. B는 대조를 나타내지만 두 문장은 서로 반대되지 않는다. C는 결과를 나타내지만 사례는 앞 진술의 결과가 아니라 그 진술을 보여 주는 예이다. D는 앞 내용을 대체한다는 뜻이지만 뒤 문장은 앞 내용을 이어서 구체화할 뿐이다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence makes a general claim: Kandinsky linked specific colors to specific instruments. The sentence after the blank gives concrete cases of this, comparing yellow to a trumpet and blue to a cello. A transition that introduces an example fits, so A is correct. B signals contrast, but the two sentences don't oppose each other. C signals a result, but the yellow and blue comparisons illustrate the claim rather than follow from it, and D signals a replacement, while the final sentence actually builds on the earlier idea.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Kintsugi Japanese pottery repair philosophy and gold-seam aesthetics celebrating imperfection in ceramic restoration tradition

g.passage: In many restoration traditions, the goal of repairing a broken bowl is to make the damage disappear, so that no one can tell the object was ever cracked. Kintsugi, a Japanese method of mending pottery, takes the opposite approach. ______ its practitioners join the broken pieces with lacquer mixed with powdered gold, leaving bright seams that draw the eye to exactly where the bowl once broke.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: As a result of hiding cracks,
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 대부분의 복원 전통이 손상을 감춘다고 하고, 킨츠기는 "정반대 방식(the opposite approach)"을 취한다고 명시한다. 빈칸 뒤 문장은 금빛 이음매로 균열을 오히려 드러내는 방법을 설명하므로, 감추는 대신 드러낸다는 대체·대조 관계인 B가 정답이다. A는 유사함을 나타내지만 두 방식은 반대이다. C는 균열을 감춘 결과로 금 이음매가 생긴다는 인과를 말해 논리에 맞지 않는다. D는 감추기에 더해 드러낸다는 추가 관계로, 킨츠기가 균열을 감추지 않는다는 내용과 모순된다.
g.explanation_en: The earlier sentences say most restoration traditions hide damage, and that kintsugi takes "the opposite approach." The sentence after the blank describes gold seams that make the cracks stand out, so you need a transition showing replacement or contrast, which makes B correct. A signals similarity, but the two approaches are opposites. C presents the gold seams as a result of hiding cracks, and that cause-and-effect link makes no sense. D signals addition, implying kintsugi hides cracks and also shows them, which contradicts the passage.
g.design: "the opposite approach"라는 명시적 대조 단서 하나로 풀리게 했다. 오답 C와 D는 정답과 같은 "~ hiding cracks," 틀을 쓰되 각각 인과와 추가 관계를 나타내고, A는 유사 관계를 나타낸다.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Isamu Noguchi sculptural integration with landscape and architectural space in modernist garden design philosophy

g.passage: Many sculptors of the twentieth century made objects meant to be placed on pedestals and viewed in galleries. Japanese American artist Isamu Noguchi took a different path. He believed that a sculpture could shape the space around it, not just sit inside that space. __For example, in his garden for the UNESCO headquarters in Paris, completed in 1958, he arranged stones, paths, and water so that visitors experienced the entire garden as one sculptural work.__ For Noguchi, the line between sculpture and landscape was meant to disappear.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a criticism that other artists made of Noguchi's approach to gallery sculpture.
It explains why most twentieth-century sculptors preferred to display their work on pedestals.
It offers a specific case that illustrates Noguchi's belief about how sculpture relates to space.
It describes a change in Noguchi's thinking that led him to abandon garden design.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 "For example"로 시작하며, 바로 앞 문장에서 말한 노구치의 믿음(조각이 주변 공간을 형성할 수 있다)을 유네스코 정원이라는 구체적 사례로 보여 준다. 따라서 정답은 C이다. A는 틀렸다. 다른 예술가들의 비판은 지문에 나오지 않는다. B도 틀렸다. 받침대 전시는 첫 문장에서 대비용으로만 언급되고, 밑줄 문장은 그 이유를 설명하지 않는다. D 역시 틀렸다. 밑줄 문장은 정원 작업을 그만둔 것이 아니라 정원 작업을 보여 준다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence begins with "For example." It gives the UNESCO garden as a concrete case of the belief stated just before it: that sculpture can shape the space around it. That makes C the answer. A is wrong because the text never mentions criticism from other artists. B is wrong because pedestals come up only in the first sentence, as a contrast, and the underlined sentence doesn't explain why sculptors used them. D is wrong because the sentence shows Noguchi doing garden design, not giving it up.
g.design: 쉬운 난이도이므로 "For example"이라는 명시적 신호어 하나로 사례 기능을 파악하게 했다. 오답은 모두 같은 "It + 동사" 문장 틀을 쓰며, 비판·이유 설명·입장 변화라는 흔한 오개념을 반영했다.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Toshiko Takaezu ceramic vessel forms and spontaneous glaze interaction exploring process-driven abstraction in studio pottery

g.passage: Ceramic artist Toshiko Takaezu (1922–2011) became known for her "closed forms," round stoneware vessels sealed at the top except for a tiny opening. Many potters plan every detail of a glaze before firing. Takaezu often worked differently. She poured and brushed glazes loosely over her forms and then let the heat of the kiln decide how the colors would run, pool, and blend. __For example, on one tall vessel a band of deep blue glaze slid down during firing and merged with a brown layer below, creating a soft streak she had not designed.__ For Takaezu, such unplanned effects were not mistakes but a central part of the finished artwork.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains how Takaezu sealed the tops of her closed forms.
It describes a problem that led Takaezu to stop using glazes.
It compares Takaezu's glazing method with that of potters who plan carefully.
It gives a specific case of the kind of glaze result described in the previous sentence.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 "For example"로 시작해, 앞 문장에서 말한 '가마의 열이 유약의 흐름과 섞임을 결정한다'는 내용을 실제 사례(파란 유약이 흘러내려 갈색 층과 섞인 것)로 보여 준다. 따라서 정답은 D이다. A는 봉인 방식을 설명하지 않으므로 틀렸다. B는 마지막 문장에서 그런 효과가 실수가 아니라 작품의 핵심이라고 했으므로 틀렸다. C의 비교는 밑줄 문장이 아니라 앞부분에서 나온다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence begins with "For example" and shows a real case of what the previous sentence describes: the kiln's heat deciding how glazes run and blend. A blue glaze sliding into a brown layer is exactly that kind of result, so D is correct. A is wrong because the sentence says nothing about how the vessels were sealed. B is wrong because the last sentence says such effects were central to her work, not a reason to quit glazing. C is wrong because the comparison with careful planners comes earlier in the text, not in the underlined sentence.
g.design: "For example" 신호어 하나로 일반 진술→사례 관계를 파악하는 한 단계 문항이고, 오답은 지문 속 다른 내용(봉인, 비교)을 가져오거나 결론을 뒤집은 흔한 오개념으로 만들었다.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Wangechi Mutu collage assemblage technique and postcolonial identity fragmentation in contemporary mixed-media art practice

g.passage: Kenyan-born artist Wangechi Mutu builds her collages from many separate sources: magazine clippings, paint, fabric, and even dirt. Rather than hiding the edges where these pieces meet, she leaves the seams plainly visible. Critics note that this choice is ______: by refusing to blend the fragments into one smooth surface, Mutu invites viewers to see identity itself as something pieced together from different histories.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 지문은 Mutu가 이음매를 숨기기보다(Rather than hiding) 일부러 드러내고, 이를 통해 관객에게 정체성을 조각들의 결합으로 보도록 이끈다고 설명한다. 따라서 이 선택은 의도적인 것이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 콜론 뒤에 설명된 분명한 목적과 맞지 않는다. C는 지문에 지속 기간에 관한 단서가 없다. D는 이음매가 '분명히 보인다'는 내용과 정반대이다.
g.explanation_en: The text says Mutu leaves the seams visible "rather than hiding" them, and the part after the colon explains the purpose behind that choice: she wants viewers to see identity as pieced together. A choice with a clear purpose is intentional, so A is correct. B doesn't fit, because something done for a stated purpose isn't an accident. C isn't supported, since the text says nothing about how long the effect lasts. D contradicts the text, which says the seams are plainly visible.
g.design: 쉬운 난이도에 맞게 단서를 하나만 두었다. 'Rather than hiding'과 콜론 뒤 목적 설명이 바로 정답을 가리키고, 오답은 같은 품사의 형용사로 맞췄다.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Jonathan Adagogo Green architectural intervention and community space activation in rural Nigerian village infrastructure design

g.passage: Jonathan Adagogo Green, a photographer who worked in the Niger Delta in the late 1800s, took many pictures of the open grounds at the center of local villages. His images show that these spaces were rarely ______: on most days, residents filled them with markets, meetings, ceremonies, and children at play, which made the grounds the busiest part of village life.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
g.explanation: 빈칸 뒤에 이 공간들이 시장, 모임, 의식, 노는 아이들로 늘 채워져 '가장 바쁜' 곳이었다고 나온다. 따라서 이 공간들이 '거의 ~하지 않았다'의 빈칸에는 '비어 있는, 쓰이지 않는'이라는 뜻의 B가 들어가야 한다. A, C, D는 모두 지문이 묘사하는 공간의 실제 모습(붐비고, 활기차고, 함께 쓰는 곳)이라 그럴듯해 보인다. 하지만 'rarely' 뒤에 넣으면 그런 모습이 '거의 없었다'는 뜻이 되어 뒤 문장과 모순된다.
g.explanation_en: After the blank, the text says residents filled these spaces with markets, meetings, ceremonies, and play, so they were the busiest part of village life. The blank comes after "rarely," so you need a word for the opposite of busy, meaning empty or unused. That points to B. A, C, and D are tempting because they describe what the grounds were really like (packed, energetic, used by everyone). But if you put any of them after "rarely," the sentence says the grounds were seldom like that, which contradicts the rest of the text.
g.design: 'rarely + 빈칸'과 바로 뒤 콜론 이하의 직접 단서 하나로 반의 관계만 파악하면 풀리게 했다. 오답은 지문 내용과 어울려 보이지만 부정어와 결합하면 모순되는 단어로 구성했다.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Ngozi Adebayo abstract bronze sculpture and gestural form language in contemporary African diaspora artistic expression

g.passage: Ngozi Adebayo, a London-based artist of Nigerian heritage, casts abstract bronze sculptures inspired by the hand gestures her grandmother used while telling stories. The polished texture of her sculptures ______ light unevenly, so that each curve seems to move as a viewer walks around it.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: "of her sculptures"라는 짧은 수식어가 단수 주어 texture와 동사 사이에 끼어 있는 주어-동사 수 일치 문제 하나만 묻는다. 오답은 모두 복수 동사로, 가까이 있는 sculptures에 동사를 맞추는 흔한 실수를 노린다.
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "texture"이고, "of her sculptures"는 주어를 꾸며 주는 전치사구일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 동사인 C "reflects"가 알맞다. A "reflect", B "are reflecting", D "have reflected"는 모두 복수 동사이다. 이 세 선택지는 동사 바로 앞에 있는 "sculptures"에 동사를 잘못 맞춘 것이다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "texture." The phrase "of her sculptures" just describes that subject. A singular subject needs a singular verb, so C, "reflects," is correct. A ("reflect"), B ("are reflecting"), and D ("have reflected") are all plural verb forms. They make the mistake of agreeing with "sculptures," the plural noun that sits right before the blank, instead of with the real subject.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Silbo Gomero whistled language phonemic structure and linguistic transmission in Canary Islands cultural heritage preservation

g.passage: On La Gomera, one of Spain's Canary Islands, residents have long communicated across deep ravines using Silbo Gomero, a whistled form of Spanish. Instead of spoken vowels and consonants, the whistles vary in pitch and length. The system of tones that whistlers use ______ only a small number of distinct sounds, yet listeners can understand full sentences. Since 1999, the language has been taught in the island's schools to help keep the tradition alive.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Aerial perspective atmospheric haze and distant landscape recession in landscape painting illusionistic depth representation

g.passage:
Long before scientists explained how particles in the air scatter light, painters had noticed that distant hills look paler, bluer, and less sharply outlined than nearby ones. Leonardo da Vinci wrote about this effect, and by the sixteenth century many European landscape painters were using it on purpose, softening the edges of far-off mountains and mixing cool blues into their colors. This technique, known as aerial perspective, lets a flat canvas suggest miles of open space without relying only on the converging lines of linear perspective.

Some art historians, however, point out that painters did not simply copy what they saw. Joachim Patinir, for example, often painted his far horizons a brighter blue than any real haze would produce, and he placed his bands of brown, green, and blue in a strict order from front to back. For these historians, Patinir's landscapes show that aerial perspective became a pictorial convention: a learned code that viewers read as distance, even when it departed from what the eye actually sees.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Aerial perspective was developed by Leonardo da Vinci to replace linear perspective, which painters had found unable to suggest great distances.
Painters such as Joachim Patinir abandoned aerial perspective because they preferred bright, unrealistic colors to accurate depictions of haze.
Aerial perspective succeeded because painters measured the effects of atmospheric haze more precisely than the scientists of their time could.
Aerial perspective began as an attempt to capture a real visual effect, but it came to function partly as an accepted method of signaling distance rather than a faithful record of it.
g.explanation: 지문은 화가들이 실제 대기 효과를 관찰해 공기 원근법을 썼지만, 일부 학자는 파티니르의 예를 들어 그것이 실제와 다른 '관습적 코드'가 되었다고 본다는 두 단락을 연결한다. D가 이 두 내용을 모두 담는다. A는 레오나르도와 선원근법을 언급하지만 지문은 대체가 아니라 '선원근법에만 의존하지 않는다'고 했고 레오나르도가 개발했다고도 하지 않는다. B는 파티니르의 밝은 파랑을 언급하지만 그는 기법을 버린 것이 아니라 관습적으로 사용했다. C는 과학 이전의 관찰을 과장해 정밀 측정으로 왜곡했다.
g.explanation_en: The text links two ideas: painters first used aerial perspective after observing real atmospheric effects, and some historians argue, using Patinir as an example, that it became a convention that departs from actual sight. D captures both parts. A mentions Leonardo and linear perspective, but the text says only that painters did not rely solely on linear perspective, and it never says Leonardo invented the technique. B misreads Patinir: his bright blues show him using aerial perspective as a convention, not abandoning it. C stretches the point that painters noticed the effect before scientists explained it into a claim about precise measurement, which the text never makes.
g.design: 훑어 읽으면 1단락(관찰 기반 기법)만 보고 답하게 되므로, 두 단락의 관계를 연결해야 하는 정답을 두었다. 오답 A·B는 지문의 세부(레오나르도, 파티니르의 색)를 부분적으로 활용하되 왜곡했다.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Tempera to oil painting medium transition and technical innovation in fifteenth-century Italian Renaissance artistic practice

g.passage: Art historians once described the arrival of oil paint in fifteenth-century Italy as a sudden replacement: painters, the story went, abandoned egg tempera once they learned the Flemish oil technique. Close study of panels from the period complicates that account. Technical analyses of works by artists such as Antonello da Messina and Giovanni Bellini show many paintings built in layers, with quick-drying tempera used for the underpainting and drawing and slow-drying oil glazes laid over it to deepen shadows and soften transitions between tones. Workshops seem to have treated the two media as complementary tools for decades, choosing each for what it did best, rather than as rivals in which one simply defeated the other.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Physical evidence from fifteenth-century paintings suggests that Italian painters combined tempera and oil over a long period instead of quickly switching from one to the other.
Physical evidence from fifteenth-century paintings suggests that Italian painters learned the oil technique from Flemish artists earlier than historians had believed.
Physical evidence from fifteenth-century paintings suggests that Italian painters preferred oil to tempera because oil dried more slowly and blended tones more smoothly.
Physical evidence from fifteenth-century paintings suggests that Antonello da Messina and Giovanni Bellini were the first Italian painters to abandon tempera entirely.
g.explanation: 지문은 오일이 템페라를 갑자기 대체했다는 옛 설명을 소개한 뒤, 기술 분석 결과 화가들이 수십 년 동안 두 매체를 층별로 함께 사용했다고 반박하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 플랑드르 기법을 언급하지만 전래 시기에 대한 주장은 지문에 없다. C는 오일의 느린 건조와 부드러운 톤 전환이라는 세부를 맞게 가져왔지만, 지문의 요점은 오일을 선호했다는 것이 아니라 두 매체를 상호 보완적으로 썼다는 것이다. D는 두 화가의 이름을 사용하지만, 지문에 따르면 그들의 작품은 오히려 템페라를 계속 썼다는 증거다.
g.explanation_en: The text sets out the old view that oil suddenly replaced tempera, then uses technical analysis to show that painters layered the two media together for decades, so A is correct. B mentions the Flemish technique, but the text never says when Italians learned it. C correctly picks up the detail that oil dries slowly and softens tones, but the text's point is that workshops used the two media as complements, not that they preferred oil. D uses the two painters' names, but the text says their works show tempera still in use, which is the opposite of abandoning it.
g.design: 오답 C·D는 지문의 실제 세부(오일의 특성, 화가 이름)를 빌려 훑어 읽기를 노렸다. 정답을 고르려면 옛 통념과 그 반박을 연결해 읽어야 한다.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Vermeer camera obscura optical projection theory and photorealistic light handling in northern European domestic interior scenes

g.passage: Since the 1890s, some scholars have argued that Johannes Vermeer used a camera obscura, a darkened box that projects an image through a lens, to compose his quiet Delft interiors. Supporters point to features that resemble optical effects: the soft, glowing dots of light on bread crusts and metal in The Milkmaid, and foreground objects that appear slightly blurred, as if out of focus. Art historian Ellen Marsh accepts that these effects look like lens artifacts but cautions against concluding that Vermeer traced projected images. No preparatory drawings or tracing marks have been found beneath his paint layers, she notes, and the blurred highlights are applied with deliberate, varied brushwork rather than copied mechanically. In Marsh's view, Vermeer may have studied how lenses render light and then reinvented those effects freely with his brush, making the device at most a source of visual ideas rather than a tool for reproducing scenes.
g.question: According to the text, how does Marsh interpret the lens-like effects in Vermeer's paintings?
options: She holds that the effects are evidence that Vermeer traced projected images, since they closely match the blur produced by early lenses.
She holds that the effects may reflect Vermeer's observation of optical images, though he likely produced them through his own inventive painting rather than by copying.
She holds that the effects have no connection to optics, since no camera obscura has been found among Vermeer's possessions.
She holds that the effects were added by later restorers, since they appear only in the foregrounds of his interior scenes.
g.explanation: Marsh는 효과가 렌즈 산물처럼 보인다는 점은 인정하지만, 밑그림이나 트레이싱 흔적이 없고 붓질이 의도적이라는 이유로 베르메르가 렌즈 효과를 연구한 뒤 붓으로 자유롭게 재창조했다고 보므로 B가 정답이다. A는 Marsh가 인정한 '렌즈와 닮음'에서 출발하지만, 그녀가 명시적으로 거부한 트레이싱 결론을 내세운다. C는 Marsh가 장치를 회의적으로 본다는 점에 기대지만, 그녀는 광학과의 연관을 완전히 부정하지 않으며 소유물에 대한 근거는 지문에 없다. D는 전경에 흐림이 있다는 세부를 이용하지만, 복원가에 대한 언급은 지문에 없다.
g.explanation_en: B is correct. Marsh grants that the effects look like lens artifacts, but because there are no tracing marks and the brushwork is deliberate, she suggests Vermeer studied how lenses render light and then recreated those effects freely. A starts from the resemblance she accepts, but it lands on the tracing conclusion she explicitly rejects. C picks up on her skepticism, but she never denies a link to optics, and the text says nothing about Vermeer's possessions. D borrows the detail about blurred foregrounds, but the text never mentions restorers.
g.design: To answer, students must connect Marsh's concession (the effects look lens-like) with her qualification (the brushwork was invented, not traced). A and C each take one half of her view and push it too far, while D misuses a real detail from the text. The question avoids the key words of the correct answer, such as "observation" and "inventive."

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Perugino workshop attribution methodology and master-apprentice production practices in Renaissance Florence artistic collaboration

g.passage:
For much of the twentieth century, connoisseurs judged paintings from Pietro Perugino's workshop by asking a single question: which panels did the master paint himself? Works with less refined faces or stiffer drapery were often set aside as "school pieces" and treated as lesser objects. Recent technical studies, however, have complicated this approach. Infrared imaging of several altarpieces shows that Perugino frequently drew the underlying design himself, while assistants carried out large areas of the painting, sometimes reusing the same cartoon for figures in different commissions.

Art historian Giulia Ferrante argues that these findings make the old question misleading. Because contracts of the period usually named Perugino as responsible for a work's overall design and quality rather than for every brushstroke, she contends, a panel painted largely by assistants could still be a fully legitimate "Perugino" by the standards of his clients. Scholars, in her view, should therefore study how tasks were divided within the workshop rather than sort paintings into authentic and inauthentic categories.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Infrared imaging has shown that Perugino painted far fewer of his altarpieces than twentieth-century connoisseurs believed, so many works should be removed from his body of work.
Perugino's habit of reusing cartoons across commissions suggests that his clients cared more about speed than about the quality of the finished paintings.
Evidence about how Perugino's workshop operated suggests that classifying paintings by whether the master personally executed them misrepresents how such works were understood in his time.
Ferrante argues that contracts from the period are more reliable than technical studies for determining which parts of a painting Perugino completed himself.
g.explanation: 지문은 기술 연구가 공방의 분업을 드러냈고, Ferrante가 당시 계약 기준상 조수가 그린 그림도 정당한 페루지노 작품이므로 진위 분류 대신 분업을 연구해야 한다고 주장한다는 내용이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 조수 참여라는 사실은 맞지만 작품을 목록에서 제외해야 한다는 결론은 지문의 주장과 정반대이다. B는 밑그림 재사용이라는 세부를 근거로 삼지만 고객이 속도를 중시했다는 내용은 지문에 없다. D는 계약을 언급하지만 Ferrante는 계약을 손길 판별 도구로 쓰지 않으며, 오히려 손길을 따지는 질문 자체를 문제 삼는다.
g.explanation_en: The text explains that technical studies revealed how work was divided in the workshop, and that Ferrante uses period contracts to argue that assistant-painted panels were still legitimate Perugino works. Scholars should therefore study the division of labor instead of sorting paintings as authentic or not, which makes C correct. A is right that assistants were involved, but its conclusion that works should be removed from his body of work is the opposite of Ferrante's point. B builds on the detail about reused cartoons, but the text never says clients cared more about speed. D mentions contracts, but Ferrante doesn't use them to find out which parts Perugino painted; she argues that this question itself is misleading.
g.design: To answer, students have to link the technical evidence to Ferrante's argument about contracts. Choices A, B, and D each use a real detail from the text (assistants, cartoons, contracts) but draw a wrong conclusion from it.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Pointillism color optical mixture and scientific divisionism in Georges Seurat post-impressionist painting technique development

g.passage: When Georges Seurat began placing small, separate touches of unmixed pigment side by side in the 1880s, he was drawing on color theorists such as Michel-Eugène Chevreul and Ogden Rood, who argued that colors seen next to each other could blend in the viewer's eye. Seurat hoped this "optical mixture" would produce hues more luminous than any mixed on the palette. Later studies of his canvases, however, suggest the effect rarely worked as the theory predicted: at ordinary viewing distances, many of his adjacent dots of complementary color blend into a somewhat grayish tone rather than a brighter one. Even so, art historians argue that the technique mattered for a different reason. The visible, evenly spaced dots give paintings such as A Sunday on La Grande Jatte a shimmering, deliberately constructed surface, and that quality, more than any gain in brightness, shaped how later painters approached the canvas.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Seurat's dot technique succeeded mainly because it made his colors more luminous than paint mixed on a palette, as Chevreul and Rood had predicted.
Seurat's dot technique was based so heavily on flawed color theory that it had little lasting effect on later painters.
Seurat's dot technique came out of his study of Chevreul and Rood, whose theories art historians now consider more important than his paintings.
Seurat's dot technique often failed to brighten colors as intended, but its distinctive surface effect gave it lasting importance.
g.explanation: 지문은 Seurat가 광학적 혼색으로 더 밝은 색을 기대했지만 실제로는 회색빛으로 섞이는 경우가 많았고, 그럼에도 점들이 만든 반짝이는 화면 질감 덕분에 이후 화가들에게 영향을 주었다고 말하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 Seurat의 의도와 이론은 맞게 담았지만, 그 효과가 실제로 성공했다고 해서 지문과 반대된다. B는 이론이 기대대로 작동하지 않았다는 점은 맞지만, 영향이 거의 없었다고 해서 결론과 모순된다. C는 이론적 배경은 맞게 언급하지만, 역사가들이 이론을 그림보다 더 중요하게 본다는 내용은 지문에 없다.
g.explanation_en: The text says Seurat expected optical mixture to make colors brighter, but his dots often blended into grayish tones instead. It then adds that the shimmering, constructed surface still gave the technique lasting influence, so D is correct. A gets Seurat's intent and sources right, but it claims the brightening effect worked, which is the opposite of what the text says. B is right that the theory fell short, but it says the technique had little influence, which contradicts the ending. C correctly mentions where the theory came from, but the text never says historians value the theories more than the paintings.
g.design: I used a "theory, then reversal, then different significance" structure, so a reader has to connect the failed brightening with the lasting surface effect. A and B each latch onto only half of the passage, and C is a plausible distortion built on the theorists.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Glassblowing apprenticeship tradition and furnace skill transmission in Murano Venice artisanal craft preservation

g.passage: For centuries, the glassmakers of Murano, an island in the Venetian lagoon, have passed on their craft through long apprenticeships in which a novice may spend years merely fetching tools and tending the furnace before being allowed to shape molten glass. Some observers have dismissed this slow progression as a holdover from guild customs that once restricted competition. Yet master glassblowers argue that the waiting period is itself the lesson: by watching the furnace for thousands of hours, apprentices learn to judge the temperature and workability of glass from its color and the way it moves on the pipe, knowledge that no written manual has managed to capture. Recently, several Murano workshops experimented with shortening apprenticeships by teaching techniques in classroom courses. Trainees from these programs mastered individual steps quickly, but masters reported that they struggled to adjust when a batch of glass behaved unexpectedly, a skill that apprentices trained in the traditional way seemed to develop almost without noticing.
g.question: Based on the text, what is the main point the author makes about Murano's lengthy apprenticeships?
options: The long years of observation build a kind of practical judgment that faster instruction has so far failed to reproduce.
The long years of observation survive mainly because guild customs once used them to limit competition among workshops.
The long years of observation could be replaced by classroom courses once masters write down their knowledge of glass temperature.
The long years of observation matter less than mastery of individual steps, which classroom trainees achieved more quickly.
g.explanation: 지문은 긴 견습 기간 동안 화로를 관찰하며 유리의 상태를 판단하는 감각이 길러지며, 교실식 단축 과정 수료생은 예상 밖 상황에 대처하지 못했다고 말하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 일부 관찰자의 견해일 뿐 저자는 'Yet'으로 이를 반박한다. C는 그 지식이 글로 담긴 적이 없다는 내용과 어긋나며, 교체 가능성을 주장하지도 않는다. D는 수료생이 개별 단계를 빨리 익혔다는 세부는 맞지만, 지문은 오히려 그것만으로는 부족하다고 결론짓는다.

B gives only the view of some observers, which the author pushes back on with "Yet." C goes against the text's statement that no manual has captured this knowledge, and the author never says the apprenticeships could be replaced. c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Salt-glazing pottery sodium vapor reaction and characteristic orange-peel surface texture in stoneware firing process

g.passage: In salt-glazing, potters do not coat stoneware with a prepared liquid glaze before firing. Instead, when the kiln reaches roughly 1,200°C, they throw ordinary salt into the firebox, where it vaporizes and the sodium reacts with silica in the clay surface to form a thin glassy layer. Because the vapor settles unevenly, beading in some places and thinning in others, the finished surface often shows a pitted, dimpled texture known as "orange peel." Many collectors prize this texture as a sign of authentic salt firing. ______ some contemporary potters deliberately avoid it, adjusting the amount and timing of the salt so that their pots come out with a smoother, more uniform sheen.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 수집가들이 오렌지 껍질 질감을 진품의 표시로 높이 평가한다고 말하고, 마지막 문장은 일부 도예가가 일부러 그 질감을 피한다고 말한다. 질감이 높이 평가되는데도 피하는 사람이 있다는 양보 후 반전 관계이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 수집가들의 선호가 질감을 피하는 이유가 된다는 뜻이 되어 인과 방향이 맞지 않는다. C는 마지막 문장을 앞 문장의 바꿔 말하기로 만들지만 두 문장은 내용이 반대이다. D는 두 문장이 비슷한 태도를 보인다는 뜻이지만 실제로는 대조되는 태도이다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank says collectors value the orange-peel texture as a sign of authentic salt firing. The final sentence says some potters avoid that texture on purpose. A trait is valued, yet some people reject it, so this is a concession followed by a contrast, and B is correct. A would mean the collectors' preference causes potters to avoid the texture, which gets the cause and effect backward. C would make the last sentence a restatement of the one before it, but the two sentences describe opposite attitudes. D says the attitudes are alike, when in fact they contrast.
g.design: There's no contrast word near the blank. To find the relationship, students have to compare how collectors value the texture with how some potters avoid it. A and D can look right if the passage is only skimmed.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Ladi Kwali pottery hand-building technique and Abuja Nigerian clay sculptural tradition in contemporary African ceramics

g.passage: Nigerian potter Ladi Kwali grew up in the Gbari village of Kwali, where women built large water jars by coiling ropes of clay and smoothing the surfaces by hand. In 1954 she joined the Abuja Pottery Training Centre, where she was trained to throw vessels on a potter's wheel and to fire them at high temperatures with glazes. ______ the pieces that made her internationally famous were not wheel-thrown: she kept coiling her jars by hand, bringing traditional Gbari forms into the new stoneware clay and carving them with images of lizards, fish, and scorpions.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 Kwali가 Abuja에서 물레 성형 기술을 배웠다고 말하고, 뒤 문장은 그런데도 그녀의 대표작이 물레가 아니라 손으로 코일을 쌓아 만든 것이었다고 말한다. 이는 앞의 내용에서 예상되는 결과를 뒤집는 양보 후 반전 관계이므로 C가 정답이다. B는 훈련이 명성으로 이어졌다는 인과로 읽힐 수 있지만, 뒤 문장은 훈련받은 기술을 쓰지 않았다는 내용이라 결과가 될 수 없다. A는 뒤 문장을 앞 문장의 사례로 만들지만 뒤 문장은 앞 내용과 대비된다. D는 단순 추가를 나타내므로 두 문장 사이의 대조를 놓친다.
g.explanation_en: The first sentence says that Kwali was trained at Abuja to throw pots on a wheel. The next sentence says that her most famous pieces were still coiled by hand instead. That reverses what the training would lead you to expect, so you need a contrast transition, and C is correct. B is tempting because her training might seem to explain her fame, but the second sentence describes her not using the wheel technique, so it can't be a result of learning it. A would make the second sentence an example of the first, but the two sentences actually contrast with each other. D just adds information and misses the contrast completely.
g.design: 빈칸 앞에 명시적인 역접 어휘를 두지 않았고, 대조 관계는 '물레를 배움'과 '손 성형을 고수함'이라는 내용에서만 읽어낼 수 있다. 오답 B는 훈련이 명성으로 이어졌다고 읽는 인과 독해를, A와 D는 정보를 덧붙이거나 구체화하는 독해를 노렸다.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Ruth Asawa wire sculpture spatial form and organic biomorphic abstraction in postwar Asian-American sculptural innovation

g.passage: Early critics often dismissed Ruth Asawa's looped-wire sculptures as decorative craft, linking the technique to basket weaving she had observed in Mexico rather than to the ambitions of postwar abstraction. Asawa herself acknowledged that she had learned the looping method from villagers in Toluca. ______ she used that humble technique to pursue a distinctly sculptural problem: by suspending interlocking lobes of wire within one another, she made forms whose inside and outside are visible at the same time, so that the surrounding space becomes part of the work.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 Asawa가 멕시코 마을 사람들에게서 기법을 배웠다고 인정했다는 내용으로, 비평가들의 '공예' 평가를 일부 받아들이는 양보에 해당한다. 뒤 문장은 그 소박한 기법으로 본격적인 조각적 문제를 탐구했다고 반전하므로 양보 후 대조를 나타내는 D가 정답이다. A는 기법을 배운 것이 원인처럼 보여 그럴듯하지만, 뒤 문장의 핵심은 비평가의 평가를 뒤집는 것이지 그 결과가 아니다. B는 두 문장이 같은 방향의 주장을 한다고 보지만 실제로는 방향이 반대이다. C는 뒤 문장이 기법 습득의 구체적 사례가 아니므로 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence is a concession: Asawa admitted she learned the looping method from villagers, which seems to support the critics' view that her work was craft. The next sentence reverses that impression by showing she used the technique to explore a serious sculptural problem, so a concession-then-contrast transition, D, is correct. A is tempting because learning the technique did make the sculptures possible, but the sentence's point is to push back against the critics, not to describe a simple consequence. B wrongly treats the two sentences as making parallel points when they actually pull in opposite directions. C doesn't work because the second sentence isn't an example of her learning the technique.
g.design: 별다른 어휘 단서 없이, 앞 문장이 비평가 쪽 견해를 인정하는 양보이고 뒤 문장이 이를 뒤집는다는 점을 파악해야 하도록 만들었다. 기법 습득에서 활용으로 이어지는 흐름 때문에 인과(A)가 그럴듯해 보이는 함정이 생긴다.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Casa Batlló Gaudí organic architecture and Art Nouveau curved surface design in Barcelona modernist architectural masterpiece

g.passage: Completed in 1906, Antoni Gaudí's renovation of Casa Batlló in Barcelona replaced a plain apartment block's flat walls with rippling stone, bone-shaped balcony supports, and a roof that curves like the back of a dragon. Many visitors take these flowing forms as pure ornamental fantasy, a showcase of Art Nouveau taste with little practical purpose. ______ several of the building's curves were carefully engineered: in the central light well, the tiles fade from deep cobalt near the skylight to pale blue lower down, and the windows get larger toward the ground floor, so daylight spreads evenly through all the stories.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 방문객들이 곡선을 실용적 목적 없는 장식으로 여긴다는 통념을 제시하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 곡선이 실제로는 채광을 위해 설계되었다고 그 통념을 뒤집으므로 통념과 실제를 대비하는 A가 정답이다. B는 뒤 문장에 구체적 세부(타일, 창문)가 나와 그럴듯하지만, 이 세부는 '순수 장식'이라는 견해의 예가 아니라 반박 근거다. C는 방문객의 인식이 공학적 설계의 원인이 될 수 없어 인과 방향이 맞지 않는다. D는 두 문장이 비슷한 내용이 아니라 상반된 내용이므로 틀리다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank gives a common belief: visitors see the curves as pure ornament with little practical purpose. The sentence after the blank overturns that belief by showing the curves were engineered to spread daylight evenly, so A, which sets a misconception against the actual facts, is correct. B looks tempting because specific details (tiles, windows) follow, but those details argue against the "pure ornament" view instead of illustrating it. C doesn't work because visitors' impressions can't have caused Gaudí's engineering, so the cause-and-effect direction is wrong. D is wrong because the two sentences contrast with each other instead of making similar points.
g.design: 빈칸 뒤 구체적 세부가 B(예시)를 유도하지만, 실제 관계는 통념에 대한 반박(양보 후 반전)이라 두 문장의 논리를 비교해야 풀린다.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Brutalist architecture concrete mass form and sculptural geometric monumentality in mid-twentieth-century institutional building design

g.passage: Brutalist buildings of the 1960s, such as Boston City Hall, are often dismissed as cold displays of raw concrete that ignore the people who use them. Many critics have assumed that their heavy, stepped masses were chosen mainly because poured concrete was cheap. __Yet the architects' own drawings show them repeatedly adjusting the depth of overhangs and the spacing of piers to control how shadow would fall across public plazas at different hours.__ Such revisions suggest that the buildings' sculptural geometry was a deliberate attempt to give civic institutions a readable, human-scaled rhythm, not simply a by-product of economical construction.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why poured concrete became the cheapest material available for institutional buildings in the 1960s.
It presents evidence that calls into question a common explanation for the form of Brutalist buildings.
It describes a feature of Boston City Hall that critics have praised as an exception to Brutalist coldness.
It gives a conclusion about the purpose of Brutalist geometry that the final sentence then qualifies.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해, 콘크리트 매스가 주로 비용 때문에 선택됐다는 비평가들의 가정에 반하는 증거(건축가들의 도면 수정)를 제시하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 비용을 언급하지만 밑줄 문장은 콘크리트가 저렴해진 이유를 설명하지 않는다. C는 Boston City Hall이 언급된 점은 맞지만 밑줄 문장은 비평가의 칭찬을 다루지 않는다. D는 순서를 거꾸로 본 것으로, 밑줄 문장은 결론이 아니라 증거이고 마지막 문장은 그 증거에서 결론을 끌어낼 뿐 결론을 약화하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet" and offers evidence, the architects' revisions to their drawings, that goes against the critics' assumption that the massive forms were chosen mainly to save money. That makes B correct. A brings up cost, but the sentence never explains why concrete was cheap. C mentions Boston City Hall, but the sentence doesn't describe anything critics praised. D gets the order backward: the underlined sentence is evidence, not a conclusion, and the final sentence draws the conclusion from that evidence instead of qualifying it.
g.design: Distractors reuse real passage elements (cost, Boston City Hall, the final conclusion), so students have to track how the sentence works in the argument: it gives evidence against an assumption. The question doesn't use the key words of the correct answer.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Hymn singing congregational vocal tradition and religious community participation in Protestant Christian worship musical practice

g.passage: In many Protestant churches of the eighteenth century, congregations sang psalms through a practice called "lining out": a leader would chant a single line, and the people would sing it back before the next line was given. Historians have often described the practice as a stopgap for congregations in which few people owned hymnals or could read music. __Yet in some Scottish Gaelic and African American congregations, lining out persisted long after printed hymnals became cheap and widely available.__ In these communities, the slow, ornamented responses—each singer bending the melody slightly differently—had become valued for their own sake, binding worshippers together through a shared sound that no printed page could prescribe. Lining out, in other words, was not merely a workaround for scarcity but a tradition of communal participation in its own right.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a historical detail that supports the explanation historians have often given for why the practice of lining out developed.
It presents an example of how printed hymnals gradually replaced older practices in congregations that had relied on lining out.
It presents an observation that complicates a common account of lining out and that the text goes on to explain.
It presents a contrast between Scottish Gaelic and African American congregations that the text then uses to describe their differing styles of singing.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 "Yet"으로 시작해, 앞에서 소개한 역사가들의 설명(찬송가 책이 부족해서 생긴 임시방편)과 맞지 않는 사실, 곧 책이 흔해진 뒤에도 lining out이 계속되었다는 점을 제시한다. 이어지는 문장들은 그 이유(공동체적 소리 자체를 소중히 여김)를 설명하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 이 문장이 통념을 뒷받침한다고 보아 방향이 반대이다. B는 인쇄 찬송가를 언급한다는 점만 보고 고른 것으로, 밑줄 문장은 오히려 대체되지 않았다는 내용이다. D는 두 공동체를 서로 대조하는 것으로 잘못 읽었는데, 지문은 두 공동체를 공통된 사례로 함께 묶어 다룬다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet," and it gives a fact that doesn't fit the historians' explanation from earlier in the text (that lining out was a stopgap because hymnals were scarce): the practice kept going even after hymnals were cheap. The sentences after it explain why, saying these communities valued the shared sound for its own sake, so C is correct. A gets the direction backward, because the sentence challenges the common account instead of supporting it. B may be tempting because the sentence mentions printed hymnals, but it actually says hymnals did not replace lining out in these congregations. D treats the two communities as a contrast, but the text groups them together as examples of the same thing.
g.design: To answer, students have to connect the "Yet" sentence to the historians' view before it and to the explanation after it. The wrong choices each grab a surface detail from the text (the historians' explanation, the hymnals, the two communities) and get its role wrong.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Ethnomusicology comparative music analysis and cultural rhythm pattern variation across global musical tradition documentation

g.passage: For much of the twentieth century, ethnomusicologists comparing rhythm across cultures relied on transcriptions in Western staff notation, which divides time into evenly spaced beats grouped into measures. Using such transcriptions, researchers often classified the drumming of West African ensembles as "polyrhythmic" layers of 3 against 2. __Yet when scholars began measuring recorded performances with timing software, they found that some of these supposedly even beats were systematically uneven, with certain strokes consistently arriving slightly early or late.__ These small, regular deviations, the researchers argued, are not errors but part of what performers and listeners recognize as the correct feel of a piece. The finding has led many in the field to treat staff transcriptions as a rough guide rather than as a dependable record of how rhythm is actually organized in a tradition.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that West African ensembles prefer a 3-against-2 rhythmic layering over other patterns.
It explains why performers in some traditions treat small timing deviations as mistakes to be avoided.

g.passage: Ekphrasis, the verbal description of a work of visual art, has long been praised for helping readers "see" paintings they have never encountered. Literary scholar Mireille Okonjo argues, however, that the vividness of an ekphrastic passage depends less on the number of visual details it supplies than on whether it describes the viewer's movement through the artwork, such as where the eye lands first, what it skips, and what it returns to. According to Okonjo, readers form clearer mental images when a description follows the path of looking than when it simply lists what the painting contains.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okonjo's argument?
options: Readers who received a long, detailed description of a painting reported clearer mental images than readers who received a short description of the same painting, whether or not either description followed the path of a viewer's eye.

Readers who received a short description that traced where a viewer's gaze moved across a painting reported clearer mental images than readers who received a longer description that listed the painting's contents without any sequence.

Readers who received a description that traced where a viewer's gaze moved across a painting were more likely to say they wanted to see the actual painting than readers who received a description that listed its contents.

Readers who received a description that listed a painting's contents recalled more of the painting's objects afterward than readers who received a description that traced where a viewer's gaze moved across it.
g.design: 정답은 디테일 양이 적은데도 시선 경로 묘사가 더 선명한 이미지를 낳았다는 두 요소(양 통제·결과 변수)를 연결해야 한다. 오답은 같은 문장 틀로 쓰되 경로를 다루지만 다른 결과(관람 욕구·회상)를 재거나 디테일 양이 중요하다는 결과를 제시한다.
g.explanation: Okonjo는 묘사의 선명함이 디테일의 양보다 시선의 이동 경로를 따르는지에 달려 있다고 주장한다. B는 디테일이 더 적은 경로형 묘사가 더 긴 목록형 묘사보다 선명한 심상을 낳았음을 보여 주므로 주장을 직접 지지한다. A는 디테일의 양이 선명함을 결정한다는 결과라서 오히려 주장을 약화한다. C는 경로형 묘사를 다루지만 심상의 선명함이 아니라 그림을 보고 싶은 마음을 측정한다. D는 사물 회상을 측정했는데 그 결과마저 목록형 묘사에 유리하므로 지지 근거가 되지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: Okonjo claims that how vivid an ekphrastic passage feels depends more on whether it follows the viewer's path of looking than on how many details it gives. B supports this directly: a shorter description that traces the gaze produced clearer mental images than a longer list, so the path mattered more than the amount of detail. A suggests that the amount of detail is what counts, which actually weakens her claim. C does involve a path-based description, but it measures readers' wish to see the painting, not how clear their mental images were. D measures how many objects readers recalled, and that result even favors the list, so it doesn't support her argument.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Tragicomedy genre hybridity and tonal oscillation between serious and comic dramatic register mixing

g.passage: Early modern critics often treated tragicomedy as a simple compromise: a play that begins in danger and ends happily, borrowing tragedy's plot and comedy's resolution. Theater historian Lena Marsh argues instead that the genre's defining feature is tonal oscillation—the rapid, repeated alternation between serious and comic registers within individual scenes. On her view, audiences of the period valued tragicomedy not for its happy endings but for the unsettling experience of being pulled back and forth between grief and laughter before any outcome was known.
g.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Marsh's argument?
options: Surviving playbills from the period advertise tragicomedies more often than tragedies, and ticket records show that tragicomedies drew larger audiences on average.
Most tragicomedies of the period follow a plot structure in which a serious threat to the protagonists is introduced early and then resolved happily in the final act.
Audience diaries from the period praise tragicomedies most often for scenes in which a jest abruptly interrupts a lament, and rarely mention how the plays end.
Several playwrights of the period revised tragedies into tragicomedies by rewriting only the final scene so that the hero survives.
g.explanation: Marsh의 주장은 두 부분으로 되어 있다: 이 장르의 핵심은 장면 안에서 진지함과 희극성이 오가는 것이고, 관객은 행복한 결말이 아니라 이런 오감 자체를 높이 샀다는 것이다. C는 관객이 탄식이 농담에 끊기는 장면을 칭찬했고 결말은 거의 언급하지 않았다고 하므로 두 부분을 모두 뒷받침한다. A는 인기를 보여 줄 뿐 관객이 무엇을 높이 샀는지는 보여 주지 않는다. B와 D는 결말 중심의 '타협' 관점에 더 맞으며, 특히 D는 마지막 장면만 바꿔도 장르가 바뀐다는 뜻이어서 Marsh의 주장을 오히려 약화한다.
g.explanation_en: Marsh's claim has two parts: the genre is defined by switching back and forth between serious and comic tones within scenes, and audiences valued that switching itself rather than the happy ending. C shows audiences praising scenes where a jest suddenly breaks into a lament while barely mentioning endings, so it supports both parts. A shows that tragicomedies were popular, but it doesn't tell you what audiences valued about them. B and D fit the older, ending-focused "compromise" view instead; D actually weakens Marsh, because it suggests that changing only the final scene was enough to change the genre.
g.design: To find the answer, students must link both parts of the claim (switching within scenes, and what audiences valued) to the evidence. The wrong answers deal with popularity or with the ending-based plot structure, so a student who reads quickly may pick them.

g.passage: In Hindustani classical music, a raga is not a fixed composition but a melodic framework: it prescribes ascending and descending note patterns, characteristic phrases, and even an associated time of day for performance. Having absorbed these constraints through years of study under a guru, ______ the alap, an unmetered opening section in which the notes of the raga are introduced one by one, freely yet without violating the framework.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the raga's characteristic phrases guide a sitarist improvising
Hindustani music allows a sitarist to improvise
the guru's teachings let a sitarist improvise
g.explanation: 분사구문 'Having absorbed these constraints through years of study under a guru'는 바로 뒤에 오는 주절의 주어를 수식한다. 구루 밑에서 수년간 공부하며 제약을 익힌 존재는 연주자뿐이므로 주어는 'a sitarist'여야 한다. 따라서 정답은 D이다. A는 수식어구와 가장 가까운 무생물 명사인 'phrases'를 주어로 삼아, 악구가 공부했다는 말이 된다. B는 지문 앞부분의 배경 명사인 'Hindustani music'을 주어로 삼아, 음악이 제약을 익혔다는 말이 된다. C는 사람과 관련된 'the guru's teachings'를 주어로 삼았다. 사람처럼 보이지만 이 경우 가르침이 '구루 밑에서' 공부한 셈이 되므로 논리에 맞지 않는다. A~C는 모두 행위자인 sitarist를 목적어 자리에 두어 수식어가 엉뚱한 대상을 가리키는 현수 수식어 오류이다.
g.explanation_en: The opening phrase "Having absorbed these constraints through years of study under a guru" modifies whatever comes right after it as the subject of the main clause. Only a performer could have studied under a guru and absorbed the raga's rules, so the subject has to be "a sitarist." That makes D correct. A makes "the raga's characteristic phrases" the subject. That's the closest inanimate noun, but phrases can't study anything. B uses "Hindustani music," the background noun from the start of the passage, and music doesn't absorb constraints either. C picks "the guru's teachings," which sounds connected to a person, but teachings can't study under a guru. In A, B, and C, the real agent (the sitarist) is pushed into an object position, so the modifier dangles.
g.design: A perfect participial phrase opens the sentence, and its real agent (the sitarist) is pushed back into the object position in the wrong answers. Each wrong answer uses a different false subject: the closest inanimate noun, the background noun, or a person-related noun that only looks like an agent.

c.instruction: 두 개의 절을 제시하되 그 사이의 논리 관계(대조/인과/단순나열 중 하나)가 접속사나 구두점 없이도 문맥상 명확히 드러나도록 구성하고, 학생이 먼저 그 관계를 파악한 뒤 알맞은 구두점·접속사 조합을 고르게 하라. 정답은 논리관계에 맞는 올바른 결합(세미콜론+접속부사, 종속접속사 등)이어야 하며, 오답 3개는 각각 (1) 콤마만으로 두 절을 이은 콤마 스플라이스, (2) 논리 관계가 반대인 접속사(대조인데 인과 접속사 사용 등) 사용, (3) 불필요한 접속사 중복(and+however 등 형태)을 사용하여 만들어라.
c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Acousmatic sound listening reduced ear auditory abstraction and musique concrète electroacoustic composition

g.passage: In the 1950s, French composer Pierre Schaeffer urged listeners of his musique concrète to practice what he called "reduced listening," attending to a recorded sound's texture, grain, and contour rather than to the object that produced it. A clattering train or a creaking door, he argued, could become pure sonic material once its source was mentally set aside. Many of his early audiences, ______ they kept naming the trains and doors they heard, treating the compositions less as abstract music than as puzzles of identification.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: however, struggled to listen this way;
however, struggled to listen this way,
therefore, struggled to listen this way;
however, struggled to listen this way, and yet
g.explanation:
먼저 논리 관계를 봐야 한다. 셰페르는 음원을 지우고 소리 자체를 들으라고 했지만, 청중은 그렇게 듣지 못했다. 그러니 두 내용은 대조 관계다. 빈칸 뒤의 'they kept naming…'은 독립절이므로, 앞의 독립절과 이으려면 세미콜론이 필요하다. 접속부사 however는 주어 뒤에 콤마로 끼워 넣을 수 있다. 따라서 정답은 A다.
B: 세미콜론 자리에 콤마만 써서 두 독립절을 이었으므로 콤마 스플라이스다.
C: 구두점 구조는 맞지만, therefore는 인과를 나타내므로 문맥의 대조 관계와 반대다.
D: 이미 however로 대조를 표시했는데 and yet을 또 써서 대조 표현이 중복된다.
g.explanation_en:
Start with the logic. Schaeffer wanted listeners to set aside a sound's source, but his audiences couldn't do that. That's a contrast. The words after the blank, "they kept naming…," form an independent clause, so you need a semicolon to join it to the clause before it. "However" is a conjunctive adverb, and it can sit after the subject, set off by commas. That makes A correct.
B: It joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice.
C: The punctuation works, but "therefore" signals cause and effect, which is the opposite of the contrast the passage needs.
D: "However" already marks the contrast, so adding "and yet" says the same thing twice.
g.design: 빈칸 앞뒤 내용의 대조 관계(이론과 청중 반응)는 문맥만으로 알 수 있게 썼다. 접속부사를 주어 뒤에 넣어 절의 경계를 덜 드러나게 했고, 오답은 콤마 스플라이스, 인과 접속부사, 대조어 중복의 세 가지로 구성했다.

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 정답 B: 'urged players' 뒤에 'to study ..., ______ ..., and to save ...'라는 부정사 세 개가 병렬로 이어지므로 빈칸도 'to reserve'가 와야 한다. A 'reserves'는 인용문 속 현재형 'smothers'에 시제를 맞춘 것이지만, 인용문은 별개의 문장이라 병렬 구조와 상관이 없고, 이렇게 되면 주어 없이 정형동사만 남는다. C 'reserving'은 세 항목 중 하나만 동명사/분사로 바꾸어 병렬 구조를 깬다. D 'reserved'는 주절의 과거형 'urged'와 시제는 맞지만, 'urged'와 병렬인 동사로 읽으면 'and to save'와 연결되지 않고, 앞의 'to study'와도 형태가 어긋난다.
g.explanation_en: B is correct. After "urged players," the sentence lists three parallel infinitives: "to study ..., ______ ..., and to save ...." So the blank needs the same form: "to reserve." A, "reserves," copies the present tense of "smothers" from the quotation. But the quotation is a separate clause and has nothing to do with this list, and "reserves" would leave a finite verb with no subject. C, "reserving," turns just one item of the list into an -ing form, which breaks the parallel structure. D, "reserved," matches the past tense of the main verb "urged." If you read it as a second past-tense verb alongside "urged," though, it doesn't fit with "to study" or "and to save," so the series falls apart.
g.design: I put a quotation in the present tense ("smothers") inside a past-tense main clause that contains a list of three infinitives. Each wrong answer follows one of the recipe's traps: A copies the quotation's tense, C changes the form of just one item in the list, and D matches only the tense of "urged."

Because the genre gives so much of its space to these warnings, Marcoux argues that ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

the lovers' grief at separation was likely a minor theme that medieval audiences of the aube hardly noticed.
the aube may have been as concerned with the social risks around a secret love as with the lovers' private feelings.
the aube was most likely written to warn real courtiers against forming secret attachments at court.

C draws the logical conclusion that the genre cared about these social risks as much as about the lovers' feelings, which adds to the traditional view without throwing it out. A claims the watchman was added later by copyists, but the passage says nothing about how the poems were copied. B goes too far by calling the lovers' grief a minor theme, since the evidence only shows that another concern shared the space. D claims the poems were written to warn real courtiers, but the passage describes what the poems contain, not any teaching purpose behind them.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Dadaism absurdist artistic resistance and anti-rational nonsense challenging World War One modernist cultural logic

g.passage: Many accounts describe the Dada performances staged at Zurich's Cabaret Voltaire in 1916 as pure nonsense: Hugo Ball chanting invented syllables, Tristan Tzara reading poems assembled from words drawn out of a hat. Art historian Lena Varga argues that this nonsense had a target. Before and during World War One, she notes, European governments and newspapers had praised the war as the rational result of progress, calling it efficient, scientific, and even necessary for civilization. In that setting, Dadaists treated orderly language and logical argument as tools that had been used to make mass slaughter seem reasonable. If Varga is right, then the movement's deliberate rejection of sense should be understood not as a retreat from public life but as ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: a retreat from the political arguments that had divided European artists in the years before the war began.
a move toward a new, more efficient artistic method meant to replace the chaotic styles that came before it.
an effort to show that the wartime governments had been unable to communicate their goals clearly to their own citizens.
an attack on the forms of reasoning that had been used to justify the war to the public.
g.explanation: Varga는 다다이스트들이 질서 있는 언어와 논리가 학살을 합리적으로 보이게 하는 데 쓰였다고 보았다고 말하므로, 의미의 거부는 바로 그 전쟁 정당화의 추론 방식을 공격하는 것으로 이해해야 한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 빈칸 앞의 '공적 삶으로부터의 후퇴가 아니라'와 모순된다. B는 다다가 오히려 거부한 '효율성'을 목표로 삼았다고 말하므로 틀렸다. C는 정부의 문제를 소통 실패로 보지만, 지문은 오히려 정부의 언어가 너무 설득력 있게 전쟁을 정당화했다고 말한다.
g.explanation_en: Varga says Dadaists saw orderly language and logic as tools that had made mass slaughter seem reasonable, so rejecting sense would be a way of attacking the reasoning used to justify the war. That makes D correct. A contradicts the blank's setup, which says the rejection was "not a retreat from public life." B claims Dada aimed for efficiency, but efficiency was part of the wartime rhetoric Dada opposed. C treats the governments' problem as a failure to communicate, yet the text suggests their language justified the war all too effectively.
g.design: To answer, students have to connect two ideas: language and logic were used to justify the war, and the blank contrasts Dada with a retreat from public life. Options B and C sound partly right because they mention efficiency and government language, but they turn the passage's logic around.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Abecedarian constraint narrative alphabetical ordering and textual puzzle structure in conceptual writing

g.passage:
Text 1
Abecedarian works, in which each successive sentence or word begins with the next letter of the alphabet, are often treated as mere puzzles. Critic Lena Moravec argues otherwise: because the constraint dictates order in advance, she claims, it strips the writer of any control over sequence, so such texts cannot build genuine narrative momentum and should be read only as displays of verbal ingenuity.

Text 2
Walter Abish's novel Alphabetical Africa is constrained so that its first chapter uses only words beginning with "a," the second adds "b," and so on before the process reverses. Readers have noticed that the expanding and shrinking vocabulary shapes the story itself: characters and events can appear only once their initial letters become available, and the gradual loss of letters in the second half creates a sense of mounting confinement. Here the constraint does not replace narrative design; it becomes one of its chief instruments.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Moravec's claim in Text 1?
options: By suggesting that an alphabetical constraint can itself generate the progression of a story rather than preventing it
By suggesting that an alphabetical constraint is valued by readers mainly for the verbal ingenuity it displays
By suggesting that an alphabetical constraint gives writers full control over sequence once the rule is reversed
By suggesting that an alphabetical constraint produces momentum only when it is abandoned partway through a work
g.explanation: Moravec는 알파벳 제약이 순서를 미리 정해 진정한 서사적 추진력을 만들 수 없다고 주장한다. Text 2는 Abish의 소설에서 어휘의 확장·축소가 인물 등장 시점과 점증하는 압박감을 만들어 제약이 서사의 도구가 된다고 말하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 Moravec의 입장을 반영할 뿐 Text 2의 요지가 아니다. C는 역전 구조를 언급하지만 Text 2는 작가가 순서를 완전히 통제한다고 하지 않으며 역전도 제약의 일부다. D는 제약이 후반에도 유지되어 오히려 압박감을 만든다는 Text 2 내용과 반대다.
g.explanation_en: Moravec claims that because an alphabetical constraint fixes order in advance, it cannot produce real narrative momentum. Text 2 shows Abish's expanding and shrinking vocabulary controlling when characters appear and building a sense of confinement, so the constraint drives the story; that makes A correct. B echoes Moravec's own view, not Text 2's point. C picks up the reversal detail, but Text 2 never says the writer gains full control; the reversal is still part of the rule. D contradicts Text 2, where the constraint stays in force in the second half and creates the confinement.
g.design: To answer, students must connect Moravec's claim that the constraint blocks momentum with Text 2's example of the constraint shaping the plot. Wrong answers C and D reuse the reversal and shrinking-letters details, and B repeats the "ingenuity" wording from Text 1.

c.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Orison Scottish devotional prayer form and religious sentiment expression in Reformation-era spiritual verse composition

g.passage:
Text 1
Scholars of sixteenth-century Scottish verse often treat the orison, a short devotional prayer-poem, as a casualty of the Reformation. Because Reformed preachers condemned prayers to saints and elaborate Latin liturgy, the argument goes, poets abandoned the orison altogether, and private religious feeling in Scottish verse largely fell silent until the following century.

Text 2
Manuscript miscellanies compiled in Scotland during the 1560s and 1570s tell a different story. Copyists kept writing orisons, but they stripped out invocations of the Virgin and the saints and addressed Christ directly in plain Scots. The intimate, first-person pleading that had defined the form survived; what changed was whom the speaker addressed and in what language.
g.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the scholars' view described in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that Reformed objections drove poets to stop composing orisons, while noting that the manuscripts show copyists preserving older Latin prayers
By arguing that the evidence from manuscript collections shows the form was reshaped to suit Reformed doctrine rather than given up
By contending that Reformed preachers in fact encouraged prayers to saints, so their objections could not have affected the form
By suggesting that private religious feeling disappeared from Scottish verse, though for reasons unrelated to the Reformation
g.explanation: Text 1의 학자들은 종교개혁 이후 오리즌이 버려졌고 개인적 신앙 감정이 침묵했다고 본다. Text 2는 필사본에서 성인 호칭을 빼고 그리스도에게 스코츠어로 직접 호소하는 오리즌이 계속 쓰였음을 보여 주므로, 형식이 사라진 것이 아니라 개혁 교리에 맞게 바뀌었다고 반박할 것이다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 오리즌 작성이 중단되었다는 데 동의하고 라틴어 기도가 보존되었다고 하는데, Text 2는 라틴어와 성인 호칭이 오히려 제거되었다고 말한다. C는 설교자들이 성인 기도를 장려했다고 하지만, 이는 두 지문 어디에도 근거가 없다. D는 신앙 감정이 사라졌다고 하는데, Text 2는 1인칭의 친밀한 호소가 살아남았다고 분명히 말한다.
g.explanation_en: The scholars in Text 1 claim that orisons were abandoned after the Reformation and that private religious feeling went silent. Text 2 points to manuscripts in which orisons kept being written, now addressed directly to Christ in Scots and without saints, so the form was adapted to Reformed doctrine rather than dropped. That makes B the answer. A agrees that composition stopped and says Latin prayers were preserved, but Text 2 says copyists removed the old invocations and wrote in Scots. C claims preachers encouraged prayers to saints, which neither text supports. D says private feeling disappeared, but Text 2 says the intimate first-person pleading survived.
g.design: To get this right, you have to link Text 2's manuscript evidence to Text 1's claim that the form was abandoned. A and D each partly agree with Text 1, so they look plausible on a quick read. The question doesn't use the key words of the correct answer, such as "reshaped."

By the end of the year, many of the selected students had improved more than their classmates. Later researchers wanted to know how teachers' beliefs could produce such a change. __Classroom observations showed that teachers gave the "promising" students more praise, called on them more often, and waited longer for their answers.__ These findings suggest that expectations shape student performance through everyday teacher behavior.

It presents evidence that the original study's results were caused by chance.
It provides details that help explain how teachers' beliefs led to student improvement.
It introduces a criticism of the researchers who carried out the original study.
g.explanation: 바로 앞 문장은 교사의 믿음이 어떻게 변화를 낳았는지라는 질문을 던지고, 밑줄 문장은 칭찬·발표 기회·기다림 시간이라는 구체적 행동으로 그 질문에 답한다. 마지막 문장도 기대가 교사 행동을 통해 작용한다고 정리하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 학생 선발 방식(무작위)을 말하는데, 이는 첫 문장의 내용이다. B는 결과가 우연이라고 하지만 밑줄 문장은 결과를 뒷받침하는 원인을 설명한다. D의 비판은 지문 어디에도 없다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence just before the underlined one asks how teachers' beliefs could cause the change, and the underlined sentence answers that question with specific behaviors: more praise, more chances to speak, and longer wait time. The final sentence then sums this up by saying expectations work through teacher behavior, so C is correct. A describes how students were chosen (at random), but that information is in the first sentence. B says the results happened by chance, but the underlined sentence explains a cause that supports the results. D is wrong because the text never criticizes the original researchers.
g.design: 쉬운 문항: 바로 앞의 '어떻게'라는 질문과 밑줄 문장의 답이 직접 이어진다. 오답은 같은 'It + 동사' 형식이고, 흔히 하는 오해(선발 방식, 우연, 비판)를 담았다.

c.seed: social science research — Bernstein language codes restricted versus elaborated speech patterns and social class educational achievement disparities

g.passage: In the 1960s and 1970s, British sociologist Basil Bernstein studied how children from different social classes used language. He described two patterns of speech. A "restricted code" relies on shared background knowledge and short, familiar phrases, so speakers often leave meanings unstated. An "elaborated code" spells meanings out in full, using more varied vocabulary and complex sentences. __Bernstein argued that schools mainly reward the elaborated code, which middle-class children were more likely to learn at home.__ In his view, this helped explain why working-class children, who were just as capable, often received lower marks in school.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It defines the restricted code by listing the features that make it different from the elaborated code.
It presents a criticism that later researchers raised against the two speech patterns Bernstein described.
It offers evidence that working-class children had less ability than middle-class children.
It states a claim that links the two speech patterns to the difference in school results described afterward.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 학교가 정교한 코드를 보상하며 중산층 아이들이 이를 집에서 배운다는 Bernstein의 주장으로, 앞서 소개된 두 언어 코드를 뒤 문장의 성적 격차 설명과 연결한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 제한된 코드의 정의가 밑줄 앞 문장에서 이미 제시되었으므로 틀리다. B는 밑줄 문장이 후대 연구자의 비판이 아니라 Bernstein 자신의 주장이므로 틀리다. C는 지문이 노동계급 아이들도 똑같이 능력이 있다고 말하므로 틀리다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence gives Bernstein's claim that schools reward the elaborated code, which middle-class children tend to learn at home. That claim connects the two speech patterns to the gap in school marks explained in the next sentence, so D is correct. A is wrong because the restricted code is already defined in an earlier sentence. B is wrong because the sentence is Bernstein's own argument, not a criticism from later researchers. C is wrong because the text says working-class children were just as capable.
g.design: 이 문항은 '주장이 앞의 정의와 뒤의 결과를 연결한다'는 한 단계 구조만 파악하면 풀 수 있다. 오답은 정의, 비판, 증거라는 흔한 오해를 노리게 만들었다.

c.seed: social science research — Reactance theory psychological resistance and motivation decrease when autonomy or choice perception becomes threatened

g.passage: Psychologist Jack Brehm proposed in 1966 that people experience an unpleasant motivational state, which he called reactance, whenever they sense that a freedom they value is being taken away. Later researchers tested the idea in everyday settings. In one study, participants were given a short public-health message urging them to cut back on sugary drinks. Half read a version full of commands such as "You must stop" and "There is no other option," while the other half read a version that gave the same facts but ended with "The choice is yours." Both groups judged the facts to be equally accurate. However, participants who read the commanding version reported more irritation toward the message and, a week later, said they intended to drink more sugary beverages than participants in the other group. The researchers concluded that the forceful tone made the request feel like a threat to readers' freedom to choose, and that this pushed readers away from the very behavior the message promoted.
g.question: According to the text, what did the researchers believe caused participants who read the commanding version to respond as they did?
options: Participants doubted the facts in the commanding version because its tone made the information seem exaggerated.
Participants felt that the wording of the message limited their own say in the matter, which made them resist its advice.
Participants were annoyed that the commanding version included fewer facts about sugary drinks than the other version did.
Participants already drank many sugary beverages, so they were less willing than others to accept advice about cutting back.

g.passage: Since the 1990s, psychologists have documented a phenomenon called stereotype threat: when people are reminded of a negative stereotype about a group they belong to, their performance on tasks related to that stereotype often declines. Early explanations held that the reminder simply lowered motivation, but later studies complicated that view. In one line of research, participants under threat reported trying just as hard as others, yet scored lower on a demanding math test. Measures taken during the test showed that these participants were spending mental effort monitoring their own performance and suppressing worried thoughts. This effort drew on working memory, the same limited resource needed to hold and manipulate numbers. When researchers gave participants a brief strategy for reframing their anxiety before the test, the gap shrank considerably, even though the stereotype had still been made salient.

Stereotype threat appears to impair performance largely by consuming mental resources that the task itself requires.
Stereotype threat affects performance on math tests more strongly than it affects performance on other demanding tasks.

c.seed: social science research — Bystander effect diffusion of responsibility and intervention inhibition as group size increases in emergency situations

g.passage: Early research on the bystander effect suggested a simple pattern: the more people who witness an emergency, the less likely any one of them is to help. Psychologists explained this through diffusion of responsibility, the idea that each witness feels less personally obligated when others are present. However, a 2019 analysis of hundreds of street surveillance recordings from several countries complicated this picture. In real public conflicts, at least one bystander intervened in roughly nine out of ten cases, and larger crowds were actually associated with a higher chance that someone would step in. The researchers noted that while each individual in a large group may indeed be less inclined to act, a bigger crowd also contains more potential helpers, so the group as a whole rarely fails to respond.

Video evidence from public conflicts shows that a reduced likelihood of helping per person need not mean that larger groups are less likely to provide help.

A is wrong because the researchers explicitly allow that individual willingness may indeed drop. B borrows the detail that recordings came from several countries, but the text never reports differences between countries. C reverses the finding that larger crowds were associated with a higher chance of intervention.

c.seed: social science research — Observational learning Bandura social modeling and aggressive behavior acquisition through vicarious reinforcement processes

g.passage: In his well-known Bobo doll studies of the early 1960s, psychologist Albert Bandura had children watch an adult hit and kick an inflatable doll. In a 1965 follow-up, he changed what happened to the adult afterward: some children saw the model praised, some saw the model scolded, and some saw no consequence at all. Children who had watched the scolded model later copied fewer of the aggressive acts on their own. When Bandura then offered every child a small reward for showing what the model had done, however, the differences between the groups mostly disappeared, and nearly all the children performed the aggressive acts accurately. Bandura concluded that seeing a model rewarded or punished mainly affects whether children choose to show a behavior, not whether they learn it in the first place.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Bandura's research suggested that children who see a model punished still pick up the model's actions, even if they are less willing to display them unprompted.
Bandura's research suggested that children who see a model punished learn fewer of the model's actions than children who see the model praised.
Bandura's research suggested that children copy aggressive actions only when they expect to be rewarded for doing so.
Bandura's research suggested that children are more likely to imitate an adult model than a model of their own age.
g.explanation: 지문의 핵심은 처벌받는 모델을 본 아이들이 스스로는 덜 따라 했지만, 보상을 제시하자 모든 집단이 공격 행동을 정확히 재현했다는 점이다. 즉 결과는 학습이 아니라 수행에 영향을 준다는 것이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 자발적 모방이 적었다는 부분만 보고 '학습'이 적었다고 잘못 해석한 것으로, Bandura의 결론과 정반대이다. C는 보상의 역할을 과장한 것으로, 아무 결과도 보지 못한 집단이나 칭찬받은 모델을 본 집단도 보상 없이 행동을 따라 했다. D는 지문이 비교하지 않은 모델의 나이 문제를 다룬다.
g.explanation_en: The text's key point is that children who saw the model scolded copied less on their own, but when offered a reward, children in every group reproduced the aggressive acts accurately. So consequences affected whether children performed the behavior, not whether they learned it, which makes A correct. B takes the fact that these children imitated less on their own and wrongly treats it as learning less, which is the opposite of Bandura's conclusion. C goes too far about rewards: children who saw the model praised or saw no consequence copied the acts without any reward offered to them. D brings up the model's age, which the text never compares.

c.seed: social science research — Authoritarian personality Adorno and fascism susceptibility through rigid thinking obedience to authority and intolerance

g.passage: In 1950, Theodor Adorno and his colleagues published The Authoritarian Personality, a study that sought to explain why some ordinary people might be drawn to fascist movements. Using questionnaires such as the F-scale, the researchers identified a cluster of traits—rigid, black-and-white thinking, deference to strong leaders, and hostility toward outsiders—that they argued formed a stable personality type rooted in strict childhood discipline. Later scholars, however, criticized the F-scale's design: because every item was worded so that agreeing indicated authoritarianism, respondents who simply tended to agree with statements could score high regardless of their actual views. Even so, many researchers have retained the study's core insight. Subsequent work using better-balanced measures has continued to find that rigid thinking, submission to authority, and intolerance tend to occur together, suggesting that Adorno's team identified a real pattern even if their original tools for detecting it were flawed.

options: Adorno's team showed that strict childhood discipline is the main cause of support for fascist movements, a conclusion later research has confirmed.

Because the F-scale's items were all worded in the same direction, later scholars concluded that the authoritarian personality was an artifact of flawed measurement.
Although later studies used better-balanced questionnaires, they found that rigid thinking and intolerance occur independently of submission to authority.
