c.seed: history and civics — Treaty of Brest-Litovsk 1918 Russian withdrawal and territorial concession World War One peace negotiation

g.passage: In March 1918, Soviet Russia signed the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk with Germany and its allies, formally leaving the First World War. The terms were severe: Russia gave up control over Poland, the Baltic territories, Finland, and Ukraine, regions that together held roughly a third of its population and much of its industry and farmland. Many historians have described the treaty as a humiliating surrender forced on a collapsing state. Yet Vladimir Lenin, who pushed the agreement through over fierce objections from within his own party, saw it differently. He argued that the new Bolshevik government could not survive if it kept fighting a war its exhausted army had already stopped waging. In his view, giving up territory was a temporary price for gaining the breathing space needed to secure power at home. Events partly supported this reasoning: when Germany was defeated later that year, the treaty was annulled, and the Bolsheviks, still in control, moved to reclaim several of the lost regions.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Although the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk imposed heavy losses on Russia, Lenin accepted it as a short-term sacrifice to preserve the Bolshevik government, a judgment later events partly bore out.
Although the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk was opposed within the Bolshevik party, Lenin's support for it was driven mainly by his confidence that Germany would soon lose the war.
Although the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk ended Russia's role in the war, its loss of farmland and industry caused the Bolshevik government's eventual collapse.
Although historians have called the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk a humiliation, its territorial terms were actually less severe than Russia's leaders had expected.
g.explanation: 지문은 조약의 가혹한 영토 손실을 제시한 뒤, 레닌이 이를 정권 유지를 위한 일시적 대가로 보았고 이후 사건이 그 판단을 부분적으로 뒷받침했다는 흐름이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 당내 반대는 맞지만, 레닌의 동기는 군대의 소진과 국내 권력 확보였지 독일의 패배 예측이 아니었다. C는 손실 내용은 맞으나 지문에서 볼셰비키는 오히려 권력을 유지했으므로 붕괴는 사실과 반대다. D는 조건이 '가혹했다'는 지문 내용과 모순되며, 지도자들의 예상에 대해서는 언급이 없다.
g.explanation_en: The text first lays out the treaty's harsh territorial losses, then explains that Lenin saw them as a temporary price for keeping the Bolsheviks in power, and finally notes that later events partly supported his view. That is why A is correct. B gets the opposition within the party right, but the text says Lenin acted because the army was exhausted and he needed to secure power at home, not because he predicted Germany's defeat. C correctly mentions the lost farmland and industry, but the text says the Bolsheviks stayed in control, which is the opposite of a collapse. D contradicts the text's description of the terms as severe, and the text never says what Russia's leaders expected.
g.design: B와 C는 실제 세부 사항(당내 반대, 산업·농지 손실)을 담고 있어서, 인과 관계나 결과를 확인해야만 배제할 수 있다. 정답은 지문 앞부분의 손실과 뒷부분의 레닌의 논리 및 결과를 연결해야 하는 두 단계 판단이 필요하다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — League of Nations 1920 international collective security organization and post-war dispute resolution mechanism

g.passage: When the League of Nations began operating in 1920, its founders hoped that collective security would make aggression too costly to attempt: member states pledged to treat an attack on one as a concern of all and to submit disputes to arbitration or to the League's Council before going to war. In practice, the League settled several smaller conflicts, such as the 1925 border clash between Greece and Bulgaria, by pressing both sides to withdraw. Yet its Covenant gave the Council no army of its own, and its decisions on serious disputes generally required unanimous agreement. When powerful members such as Japan in 1931 and Italy in 1935 used force, the League could respond only with condemnation or limited economic sanctions, which other members applied unevenly. Historians therefore often conclude that the League's design worked when disputing states were willing to be persuaded, but it depended on the cooperation of great powers it had no means to compel.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The League of Nations proved effective at resolving disputes because its members pledged to treat aggression against one state as a concern of all.
The League of Nations could resolve disputes among cooperative states, but its structure left it unable to restrain major powers that chose to use force.
The League of Nations failed mainly because its members refused to apply any economic sanctions against Japan and Italy.
The League of Nations was most successful in the 1920s because smaller conflicts, like the one between Greece and Bulgaria, required unanimous Council votes.
g.explanation: 이 글은 국제연맹이 작은 분쟁은 해결했지만(그리스-불가리아), 자체 군대가 없고 만장일치가 필요해 일본·이탈리아 같은 강대국은 막지 못했다는 두 정보를 연결하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 집단안보 서약이라는 일부만 보고 실효성을 과장하며 강대국 사례에서 실패한 점을 놓쳤다. C는 제재가 '고르지 않게' 적용되었다는 내용을 '전혀 적용하지 않았다'로 왜곡했고, 이를 실패의 주된 원인으로 삼는다. D는 만장일치 요건을 성공의 원인으로 잘못 연결하는데, 지문에서 만장일치는 한계로 제시된다.
g.explanation_en: The text links two points: the League settled smaller disputes like Greece–Bulgaria, but with no army and a unanimity requirement it couldn't stop powerful members like Japan and Italy. That combination makes B correct. A takes only the collective-security pledge and overstates how well the League worked, ignoring how it failed against the great powers. C distorts the text, which says sanctions were applied "unevenly," not that members refused to apply any, and it also treats this as the main reason for failure. D wrongly presents the unanimity requirement as a cause of success, when the text presents it as a weakness.
g.design: 정답을 고르려면 성공 사례와 구조적 한계를 연결해야 한다. A, C, D는 각각 지문 속 실제 세부(서약, 제재, 만장일치)를 쓰지만 이를 왜곡하거나 잘못 연결해서, 대충 읽으면 고르기 쉽다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Dawes Plan 1924 German war reparations restructuring and American financial intervention European stability

g.passage: By 1923, Germany's inability to meet its war reparations payments had brought French and Belgian troops into the Ruhr and pushed the German mark into hyperinflation. The plan drafted in 1924 by a committee chaired by American banker Charles Dawes did not reduce the total amount Germany owed. Instead, it lowered the annual payments for the first several years, tied later installments to the country's economic recovery, reorganized the German central bank, and arranged a large loan, much of it raised from American investors. Historians note that the plan's apparent success rested on a fragile foundation: Germany used borrowed American money to pay France and Britain, which in turn used those funds to repay their own war debts to the United States. When American lending dried up after 1929, the cycle collapsed, and the stability the plan had seemed to produce disappeared along with it.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The Dawes Plan ended the occupation of the Ruhr by significantly reducing the total reparations Germany was required to pay.
The Dawes Plan restored European stability mainly by reorganizing Germany's central bank, a reform that protected the German economy after 1929.
The Dawes Plan eased Germany's reparations burden for a time, but the stability it brought depended on a continuing flow of American loans.
The Dawes Plan failed immediately because American investors refused to lend money to Germany while its currency suffered from hyperinflation.
g.explanation: 이 글은 도스 플랜이 초기 연간 지불액을 줄여 부담을 덜어 주었다는 점과, 그로 인한 안정이 미국 차관의 순환에 의존해 1929년 이후 무너졌다는 점을 함께 서술하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 루르 점령이라는 배경을 언급하지만, 지문은 계획이 총 배상액을 줄이지 않았다고 명시하므로 틀렸다. B는 중앙은행 개편이라는 실제 세부 사항을 쓰지만, 그것을 안정의 주된 원인으로 보고 1929년 이후에도 경제를 지켰다고 주장해 지문의 붕괴 서술과 모순된다. D는 미국 대출을 언급하지만, 지문에서 미국 투자자들은 실제로 대출을 해 주었고 계획은 한동안 성공한 것처럼 보였으므로 틀렸다.
g.explanation_en: C is correct because the text makes two connected points: the Dawes Plan lowered Germany's early annual payments, and the stability that followed depended on a cycle of American lending that fell apart after 1929. A brings up the real background of the Ruhr occupation, but the text says outright that the plan did not reduce the total amount Germany owed. B uses a real detail, the reorganization of the central bank, but it treats that change as the main source of stability and says it protected the economy after 1929, which contradicts the text's account of the collapse. D mentions American loans, but in the text American investors did lend money, and the plan appeared to succeed for several years.
g.design: To get this right, you have to connect the plan's short-term relief with its dependence on loans. Choices A and B each use a real detail from the text but distort it, and D is a plausible-sounding claim that the text contradicts.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: history and civics — Indian Independence movement Gandhi nonviolent resistance and British colonial rule termination 1947

g.passage: Many popular accounts credit Mohandas Gandhi's campaigns of nonviolent resistance, such as the 1930 Salt March, with single-handedly ending British rule in India in 1947. Historians generally agree that these campaigns eroded the moral legitimacy of colonial rule, both in India and abroad. ______ many scholars also point to factors Gandhi did not control: the financial strain Britain suffered during the Second World War, the 1946 mutiny of sailors in the Royal Indian Navy, and growing doubts in London about whether the empire could still be governed at all.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.design: 빈칸 앞은 비폭력 운동의 영향을 인정하는 양보이고, 빈칸 뒤는 '단독으로 끝냈다'는 통념을 약화하는 다른 요인으로 넘어간다. 이 관계를 알려 주는 어휘 단서는 없다. 원인/결과로 읽거나 예시로 읽으면 오답이 그럴듯해 보이도록 설계했다.
g.explanation: 정답은 D이다. 앞 문장은 간디의 운동이 식민 통치의 정당성을 약화했다고 인정하고, 뒤 문장은 간디가 통제하지 못한 다른 요인들을 제시한다. 그래서 '단독으로 끝냈다'는 통념에 단서를 다는 양보 후 반전 관계가 된다. A는 정당성 약화가 전쟁 비용이나 해군 반란을 낳은 것처럼 인과 관계를 만드는데, 지문은 이 요인들을 간디와 무관하다고 밝힌다. B는 뒤 문장이 앞 문장의 사례인 것처럼 연결하지만, 뒤 문장의 요인들은 도덕적 정당성 약화의 예가 아니다. C는 같은 내용을 다르게 말하는 관계인데, 뒤 문장은 새로운 요인을 더하는 대조적 내용이다.
g.explanation_en: D is correct. The previous sentence admits that Gandhi's campaigns weakened the legitimacy of colonial rule. The next sentence lists factors outside his control, which pushes back on the claim that he ended British rule "single-handedly." That is a concession followed by a qualification. A suggests the campaigns caused the war costs and the mutiny, but the passage says Gandhi did not control these factors. B treats the next sentence as an example of the previous one, but those factors are not examples of moral delegitimization. C signals a restatement, but the next sentence adds new and contrasting information.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 관계가 어휘 단서 없이 두 문장의 논리(양보 후 반전, 일반화 후 구체화, 원인 vs 결과 방향)에서 도출되는 문제. 오답 전환어도 일부 관계는 말이 된다.
c.seed: history and civics — Spanish Inquisition 1478-1834 religious heresy prosecution and forced conversion Muslim Jewish populations

g.passage: Established in 1478, the Spanish Inquisition had authority only over baptized Christians; Jews and Muslims who had never been baptized lay outside its reach. When the monarchs Ferdinand and Isabella issued the Alhambra Decree in 1492, ordering Spain's Jews to accept baptism or leave the kingdom, tens of thousands chose conversion rather than exile. ______ the tribunal suddenly found a vast new population of converts, whose private religious practices it could now investigate as possible heresy.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 첫 문장은 종교재판소가 세례받은 기독교인만 관할했다는 점을, 둘째 문장은 1492년 칙령으로 많은 유대인이 개종(세례)했다는 점을 말한다. 이 두 정보를 연결하면 개종의 결과로 재판소가 새로운 대규모 집단을 조사할 수 있게 되었다는 인과 관계가 성립하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 대조를 나타내지만 관할권 확대는 개종에서 예상되는 결과이지 그와 상반되는 내용이 아니다. C는 앞 내용의 구체적 사례를 제시할 때 쓰는데, 마지막 문장은 개종의 사례가 아니라 그 결과이다. D는 비슷한 사건을 하나 더 덧붙일 때 쓰지만, 마지막 문장은 앞 사건과 나란한 별개의 사건이 아니다.
g.explanation_en: The first sentence says the Inquisition had authority only over baptized Christians, and the second says that many Jews accepted baptism after the 1492 decree. If you put those two facts together, the final sentence describes what followed from them: the tribunal now had a large new group it could investigate. That makes it a cause-and-effect relationship, so A is correct. B signals contrast, but this new reach is exactly what you'd expect from the conversions, not something that goes against them. C would introduce an example, but the last sentence is a consequence of the conversions, not an instance of them. D would add a similar, separate event, and the last sentence doesn't do that either.
g.design: There's no cause-and-effect word in the passage. To see the relationship, students have to link the jurisdiction rule (baptized Christians only) with the mass conversions. Readers who skim may pick contrast (the decree reads as something forced on people) or example.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Gutenberg printing press 1440 movable type technology and mass book production information revolution

g.passage: Accounts of Johannes Gutenberg's work in Mainz around 1440 often credit his movable type press with launching an immediate information revolution. Historian Elena Varga argues that this picture compresses decades of change into a single moment. Gutenberg's metal type certainly made it possible to produce identical pages far faster than scribes could copy them, but early printers faced steep costs for paper, metal, and labor, and many went bankrupt before selling their stock. __For much of the fifteenth century, printers favored Latin religious and legal texts that already had dependable buyers among clergy and universities, rather than new kinds of writing for broad audiences.__ In Varga's view, the transformation that later observers celebrate depended less on the press alone than on the slow growth of distribution networks, vernacular markets, and literate readers over the following century.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains how Gutenberg's metal type allowed printers to reproduce pages faster than scribes, which the text presents as the main source of early printing's success.
It gives evidence that early printing reinforced existing patterns of reading, which supports Varga's claim that the press did not by itself cause rapid change.
It identifies the financial losses that drove many early printers out of business, which the text treats as the reason vernacular markets never developed.
It describes a common view of Gutenberg's achievement, which Varga accepts before adding details about later distribution networks.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 초기 인쇄업자들이 이미 고정 수요가 있던 라틴어 종교·법률 문헌을 주로 찍었다는 사실로, 인쇄술이 즉각적 혁명을 일으키지 않았다는 Varga의 주장을 뒷받침하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 인쇄 속도를 다룬 것은 앞 문장이며 지문은 그것을 성공의 주원인으로 보지 않는다. C는 비용·파산 내용이 앞 문장에 있어 부분적으로 관련되지만, 밑줄 문장은 손실을 다루지 않고 지문은 자국어 시장이 나중에 성장했다고 말한다. D의 통념은 첫 문장이 소개하며 Varga는 이를 받아들이지 않고 반박한다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence shows that early printers mostly produced Latin religious and legal texts that already had reliable buyers. That evidence supports Varga's argument that the press did not create an instant revolution, so B is correct. A is wrong because the point about printing speed comes in the previous sentence, and the text doesn't treat speed as the main reason for success. C ties in partly to the earlier mention of bankruptcy, but the underlined sentence isn't about financial losses, and the text actually says vernacular markets grew later. D is wrong because the common view appears in the first sentence, and Varga disputes it instead of accepting it.
g.design: To answer, students have to link the sentence's content (conservative printing choices) to Varga's thesis. Wrong options borrow material from nearby sentences, such as speed, bankruptcy, and the common view, so a student skimming the passage could pick one.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: history and civics — Papal Schism 1378-1417 multiple popes competing authority and ecclesiastical legitimacy crisis medieval Christianity

g.passage: Between 1378 and 1417, Latin Christendom was divided by rival claimants to the papacy, first two and eventually three, each with cardinals, courts, and royal supporters of his own. Many historians have treated the Great Schism as a pure catastrophe that drained the Church's moral authority and opened the way for later reformers. __Yet the crisis also forced theologians and canon lawyers to ask a question that had long seemed unthinkable: whether a general council of the Church might hold authority even over a pope.__ Writers such as Jean Gerson argued that it could, and the Council of Constance (1414–1418) put that argument into practice by deposing or accepting the resignation of all three claimants and electing Martin V. For this reason, some scholars now see the Schism not only as a breakdown but also as the source of a lasting debate about where legitimate authority in an institution ultimately lies.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It names a reformer whose later criticism of the Church is said to have grown directly out of the damage the Schism caused.
It gives evidence that backs up the claim that the Schism mainly weakened the Church's moral standing.
It brings in a consequence of the Schism that complicates the view just mentioned and leads into the text's example of a council.
It explains how the rival claimants tried to justify their separate claims to the papacy in front of royal supporters.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해, 분열을 순전한 재앙으로만 보는 앞 문장의 시각과 대비되는 결과(공의회가 교황보다 위에 있을 수 있는가라는 물음)를 제시하고, 이어지는 Gerson과 콘스탄츠 공의회 사례로 연결되므로 C가 정답이다. A는 '후대 개혁가'가 앞 문장에 나오지만 밑줄 문장은 특정 개혁가를 언급하지 않으며, Gerson은 비판자가 아니라 공의회 권위를 옹호한 인물이다. B는 밑줄 문장이 그 견해를 뒷받침하는 것이 아니라 오히려 복잡하게 만든다는 점에서 틀렸다. D는 경쟁 교황과 왕실 지지자가 지문에 나오기는 하지만, 밑줄 문장은 교황 측의 정당화가 아니라 신학자·교회법학자들의 물음을 다룬다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence starts with "Yet," so it pushes back against the view that the Schism was a pure catastrophe. It does this by pointing to another result: scholars began asking whether a council could hold authority over a pope. That question leads straight into the examples of Gerson and the Council of Constance, so C is correct. A is wrong because later reformers are mentioned in the sentence before, but the underlined sentence names no reformer, and Gerson defended a council's authority rather than criticizing the Church. B is wrong because the sentence complicates the catastrophe view instead of supporting it. D is wrong because the rival claimants and their royal supporters do appear in the text, but the underlined sentence is about questions raised by theologians and canon lawyers, not about how the claimants justified themselves.
g.design: To answer, students have to connect the turn signaled by "Yet" with the council example that comes after it. Each wrong answer reuses a detail from the text (reformers, the catastrophe view, the claimants), so students can only rule them out by comparing them with what the underlined sentence actually does.

c.instruction:

c.seed: history and civics — Hundred Years War 1337-1453 English French territorial conflict and feudal succession dispute resolution

g.passage: The Hundred Years' War (1337–1453) is often presented as a simple contest between two nations, England and France, fighting over territory. Historian Anne Curry and others have pointed out, however, that the conflict began as a feudal succession dispute: Edward III of England claimed the French crown through his mother, while the French nobility backed Philip VI, a cousin descended through the male line. __Because many of the lords who fought were tied to both crowns by land and oath, a knight in Gascony or Brittany could reasonably see himself as defending a rightful lord rather than a homeland.__ For this reason, these historians argue, the national loyalties that later chroniclers projected onto the war's early decades mostly took shape as the fighting went on, rather than causing it.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces the territorial claims that the text goes on to describe as the war's main cause.
It raises a challenge to the historians' view that the conflict began as a succession dispute.
It describes the specific regions where the war's earliest battles were fought.
It shows how the war's feudal origins shaped participants' allegiances, supporting the text's final claim.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 앞 문장에서 말한 봉건적 계승 분쟁이라는 기원이 실제 참전자들의 충성 대상(조국이 아닌 정당한 영주)에 어떤 영향을 주었는지 보여 주고, 마지막 문장의 '민족적 충성은 전쟁 중에 형성되었다'는 결론을 뒷받침하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 영토가 언급되지만 글은 영토를 주된 원인으로 보지 않으므로 틀리다. B는 밑줄 문장이 역사가들의 견해에 반박하는 것이 아니라 오히려 지지하므로 틀리다. C는 가스코뉴와 브르타뉴가 언급되지만 전투 장소를 설명하려는 것이 아니라 충성 관계를 보여 주는 예시이므로 틀리다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence shows how the war's origin as a feudal succession dispute affected the people who fought: they were loyal to a rightful lord, not a homeland. That point supports the final sentence's claim that national loyalties developed during the war, so D is correct. A is wrong because the text mentions land but doesn't treat territory as the main cause. In fact, the text argues against that view. B is wrong because the sentence supports the historians' view instead of challenging it. C is wrong because Gascony and Brittany are mentioned to show divided loyalties, not to identify where the first battles took place.
g.design: To get this right, students have to connect the underlined sentence to both the sentence before it (feudal origins) and the final claim. The distractors each pick up something from the passage on the surface, like territory, the historians' view, or place names.

c.seed: history and civics — Zheng He treasure voyages 1405-1433 Ming Dynasty maritime exploration and tributary system expansion Indian Ocean

g.passage: Between 1405 and 1433, the Ming admiral Zheng He led seven fleets across the Indian Ocean, reaching ports from Java to the Swahili coast. Many popular accounts describe these voyages as missions of discovery, comparable to later European expeditions. __Yet the routes Zheng He followed had been sailed by Arab, Persian, and Gujarati merchants for centuries, and his pilots relied on charts and navigational knowledge already circulating in those trading networks.__ Historian Geoff Wade and others therefore argue that the fleets are better understood as instruments of the Ming tributary system: by displaying overwhelming naval power and distributing lavish gifts, the court persuaded distant rulers to send envoys acknowledging the emperor's supremacy.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a fact that undermines a common characterization of the voyages, setting up an alternative interpretation of their purpose.
It presents a fact that explains how the Ming court was able to persuade distant rulers to send envoys acknowledging the emperor.
It presents a fact that supports the comparison between Zheng He's voyages and later European expeditions described earlier.
It presents a fact that illustrates the extensive reach of the fleets across ports from Java to the Swahili coast.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해, 항로가 이미 수 세기 동안 알려져 있었다는 사실을 제시하며 항해를 '발견'의 임무로 보는 대중적 시각을 약화시킨다. 이어서 'therefore'로 조공 체제의 도구라는 대안적 해석이 제시되므로 A가 정답이다. B는 마지막 문장의 설득 방식(해군력과 선물)과 연결되지만, 밑줄 문장은 그 방법을 설명하지 않는다. C는 유럽 탐험과의 비교를 언급하지만, 밑줄 문장은 그 비교를 지지하는 것이 아니라 반박한다. D는 첫 문장의 항해 범위와 관련 있어 보이지만, 밑줄 문장의 초점은 항로가 새롭지 않았다는 점이다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet" and points out that the routes had been sailed for centuries. That fact weakens the popular view of the voyages as missions of discovery, and the next sentence ("therefore") offers another reading: the fleets were tools of the tributary system. So A is correct. B ties into the final sentence about persuading rulers, but the underlined sentence never explains how persuasion worked; that sentence names naval power and gifts instead. C mentions the comparison to European expeditions, but the underlined sentence argues against that comparison rather than supporting it. D picks up on the fleets' reach, but the underlined sentence is about the routes already being known, not about how far the fleets went.
g.design: Distractors B, C, and D each pick up real details from the passage (persuading envoys, the European comparison, how far the fleets reached), so a quick skim makes them tempting. To rule them out, the student has to see what "Yet" and "therefore" do: the sentence contrasts with the popular view and leads into the new interpretation.

c.seed: history and civics — Ottoman millet system religious communities autonomy and non-Muslim subject administrative framework

g.passage: Historians once described the Ottoman millet system as a fixed arrangement, established in the fifteenth century, under which each recognized non-Muslim community—Greek Orthodox, Armenian, and Jewish—governed its own religious, educational, and family affairs through its own leaders. Scholar Benjamin Braude has complicated this picture. He notes that the word "millet" rarely appears in this administrative sense in Ottoman documents before the late eighteenth century, and that earlier arrangements with community leaders were often local, negotiated, and inconsistent from one province to another. __Rather than a single framework imposed from the capital, then, the system may have been a patchwork of ad hoc agreements that later officials and historians reorganized into a tidy, uniform structure.__ This view does not deny that non-Muslim communities had real autonomy; it suggests instead that the shape of that autonomy varied far more than the traditional account allows.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence from Ottoman documents that the traditional view of the millet system had overlooked.
It draws a conclusion from the details about the term's late appearance and the local variation in earlier arrangements.
It brings up an objection to Braude's argument that the final sentence then sets out to answer.
It restates the traditional account of the millet system so that the text can then question it.
g.design: 이전 문장의 근거(용어 등장 시기·지역 차이)와 밑줄 문장의 추론 관계를 연결해야 하는 두 단계 판단이다. A·C는 지문 요소(문서, 마지막 문장의 단서)를 부분적으로 활용한 오답이다.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'then'으로 시작하며, 앞에서 제시한 두 근거(그 용어가 18세기 후반 이전에는 드물게 쓰였다는 점, 초기 합의가 지역마다 달랐다는 점)를 바탕으로 이 제도가 즉흥적 합의들의 모음이었을 수 있다는 결론을 내리므로 B가 정답이다. A는 틀렸다. 문서 관련 근거는 바로 앞 문장에 나오고, 밑줄 문장은 새로운 근거를 내놓지 않고 그 근거를 해석할 뿐이다. C도 틀렸다. 마지막 문장은 Braude의 견해를 한정하며 명확히 하는 것이지 반론에 답하는 것이 아니고, 밑줄 문장은 반론이 아니라 Braude 쪽의 결론이다. D는 전통적 설명이 첫 문장에서 소개되고 밑줄 문장은 그것에 반대하는 내용이므로 오답이다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence begins with "then," and it draws a conclusion from the two points just before it: the term rarely appeared before the late 1700s, and earlier arrangements differed from place to place. From these, it concludes that the system may have been a patchwork of ad hoc agreements, so B is correct. A is wrong because the evidence from the documents comes in the sentence before; the underlined sentence doesn't add new evidence, it interprets what came earlier. C is wrong because the final sentence narrows and clarifies Braude's view rather than answering an objection, and the underlined sentence supports Braude instead of challenging him. D is wrong because the traditional account is given in the first sentence, and the underlined sentence argues against it.

c.seed: history and civics — Columbian Exchange 1492 onward plants animals diseases transfer and demographic consequences Americas Europe

g.passage: Historians often describe the Columbian Exchange, the transfer of plants, animals, and pathogens between the Americas and Afro-Eurasia after 1492, as a story of loss for the Americas, where smallpox and measles killed a large share of Indigenous peoples. Historian Rebecca Earle complicates this picture by noting that some American crops changed population patterns far beyond the Atlantic world. __Maize and potatoes, for instance, grew well in soils and climates where wheat and rice failed, and by the eighteenth century they were supporting rapid population growth in places as distant as northern Europe and highland China.__ Earle argues, therefore, that the Exchange should be understood not only as a demographic catastrophe in one hemisphere but also as a demographic engine in others.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that the deaths caused by smallpox and measles in the Americas were smaller than historians commonly assume.
It explains why Earle believes that wheat and rice were less important to world history than the crops introduced from the Americas.
It offers examples supporting the claim that American crops reshaped populations in regions far from where they originated.
It describes a consequence of the Columbian Exchange that Earle regards as more significant than its effects in the Americas.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 바로 앞 문장의 주장, 즉 일부 아메리카 작물이 대서양 세계 너머의 인구 양상을 바꾸었다는 주장을 옥수수·감자의 구체적 사례로 뒷받침하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 질병 피해를 축소하는 근거로 읽었지만, 지문은 피해를 부정하지 않고 다른 측면을 덧붙일 뿐이다. B는 밀과 쌀이 언급되긴 하나, 그 작물들의 역사적 중요도를 비교하는 것이 문장의 목적은 아니다. D는 마지막 문장의 '~뿐 아니라 ~도'를 놓친 것으로, Earle는 두 효과를 함께 인정할 뿐 어느 쪽이 더 중요하다고 순위를 매기지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: C is correct because the underlined sentence gives concrete examples, maize and potatoes, to back up the sentence right before it: some American crops changed populations far beyond the Atlantic world. A is wrong because the text never says the death toll from disease was overestimated. It adds another side to the story without denying the losses. B is wrong because wheat and rice show up only to explain where the American crops did well. The sentence isn't ranking them by historical importance. D misses the "not only... but also" in the last sentence: Earle accepts both effects and never says one matters more than the other.
g.design: Distractors reuse real details from the passage (disease deaths, wheat and rice, Earle's revisionist view), so you can only rule them out by tracing the sentence back to the claim it supports and noticing that the conclusion doesn't rank the two effects.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: history and civics — Triangular trade transatlantic slavery system and merchant capitalism colonial commerce networks

g.passage: In his 1944 book Capitalism and Slavery, historian Eric Williams, a Trinidadian scholar who later led his country to independence, argued that profits from the triangular trade—in which ships carried manufactured goods to West Africa, enslaved people to the Caribbean, and sugar back to Britain—helped finance British industrialization ______ later economic historians have questioned whether those profits were large enough to have played such a decisive role.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 긴 동격구와 대시 삽입구를 걷어 내면 'Williams argued that ... helped finance British industrialization'과 'later economic historians have questioned ...'라는 독립절 두 개가 남는다. 두 독립절 사이에 접속부사 however가 오면 앞에는 세미콜론, 뒤에는 쉼표를 두어야 하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 however 뒤 쉼표는 맞지만 앞이 쉼표뿐이라 comma splice가 된다. B는 두 절을 아무 부호 없이 이어 run-on이 된다. C는 세미콜론으로 절 경계는 맞게 표시했지만 접속부사 however 뒤에 필요한 쉼표가 빠졌다.
g.explanation_en: If you strip away the long appositive and the dash interruption, you're left with two independent clauses: "Williams argued that ... helped finance British industrialization" and "later economic historians have questioned ...". When the conjunctive adverb "however" joins two independent clauses, it takes a semicolon before it and a comma after it, so D is correct. A puts the right comma after "however," but it has only a comma before it, which makes a comma splice. B runs the two clauses together with no punctuation at all, so it's a run-on. C marks the boundary between the clauses correctly with a semicolon but leaves out the comma that has to follow "however."
g.design: The two clauses are pushed far apart by a long appositive and a dash insertion, so you have to find the clause boundary before handling the punctuation around "however." A and C each get one part right, which means you have to check both sides of "however" to rule them out.

g.passage: Historians of economics often note that Adam Smith's 1759 treatise The Theory of Moral Sentiments, a book that rooted ethics in the human capacity for sympathy and drew heavily on Smith's long conversations with his friend David Hume______ was overshadowed for generations by his later and more famous study of commerce, The Wealth of Nations.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: "a book that ... David Hume"는 주어 The Theory of Moral Sentiments를 설명하는 비필수 동격어구로, 쉼표로 시작했으므로 쉼표로 닫아야 하며 그 뒤에 동사 was가 이어진다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 세미콜론으로 주어와 동사 was를 갈라놓아 앞뒤가 모두 독립절이 아니게 된다. C는 동격어구를 닫는 문장부호가 없어 어디까지가 삽입인지 불분명해진다. D의 대시는 삽입을 닫는 기능은 있지만, 쉼표로 열었던 삽입을 대시로 닫으면 짝이 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "a book that ... David Hume" is a nonessential appositive describing the subject, The Theory of Moral Sentiments. Because it opens with a comma, it has to close with a comma before the verb "was," so A is correct. B puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, and neither side of it is an independent clause. C leaves the appositive with nothing closing it, so you can't tell where the interruption ends. D uses a dash, which can close an interruption, but a dash can't close one that opened with a comma, because the punctuation has to match.
g.design: 긴 동격어구가 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어, 수험생은 앞쪽의 여는 쉼표를 확인하고 그에 맞는 닫는 부호를 골라야 한다. 이 과정에서 대시 오답(D)과 부호 없음 오답(C)을 비교해 배제해야 한다.

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Pennsylvania's constitution ... was among the most radical of these early frameworks"는 삽입구가 있지만 그 자체로 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "it abolished ..."도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 아무 문장부호 없이 이어 run-on 문장이 된다. D는 등위접속사 and가 있어 그럴듯해 보이지만 두 독립절을 잇는 and 앞에 쉼표가 빠져 있어 표준 규칙에 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Even with its long interrupting phrase, the part before the blank ("Pennsylvania's constitution ... was among the most radical of these early frameworks") is a complete independent clause, and "it abolished ..." after the blank is another one. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so B is correct. A joins them with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C uses no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D looks reasonable because it has the conjunction "and," but when "and" joins two independent clauses, it needs a comma before it, and D leaves that comma out.
g.design: The interrupting phrase about the convention puts distance between the subject and the verb, so readers have to check that the first part is still a complete clause. The answer choices compare a comma splice, a run-on, and an "and" without its comma against the semicolon.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.

g.passage: When Haiti enacted its Civil Code in 1825, legislators borrowed much of its structure from France's Napoleonic Code of 1804, the legal framework of the very empire that had tried to restore slavery on the island only two decades earlier______ Haitian jurists adapted key provisions to the needs of a nation founded by formerly enslaved people.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 긴 동격구("the legal framework of ... earlier")로 끝나는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "Haitian jurists adapted ..."도 독립절이다. 접속부사 however로 두 독립절을 이으려면 앞에 세미콜론, 뒤에 쉼표를 써야 하므로 C가 정답이다. A와 D는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 무종지문(comma splice)이 되며, D는 however 양쪽 쉼표가 삽입구처럼 보여 그럴듯하지만 여전히 틀리다. B는 세미콜론은 맞지만 문장 첫머리 접속부사 however 뒤에 필요한 쉼표가 빠졌다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank is an independent clause that ends with a long appositive ("the legal framework of ... earlier"), and "Haitian jurists adapted ..." after the blank is also an independent clause. To join two independent clauses with the conjunctive adverb "however," you put a semicolon before it and a comma after it, so C is correct. A and D link the two clauses with only commas, which makes a comma splice. D can look right because the commas around "however" make it read like an aside, but it's still a splice. B gets the semicolon right but leaves out the comma that has to follow "however" when it opens a clause.
g.design: A long appositive hides where the first independent clause ends. The distractors each get part of the rule right (B has the semicolon, D has the paired commas), so you have to compare all four choices to rule them out.

g.passage: John Snow, a young surgeon's apprentice who treated stricken coal miners when cholera swept through northern England in 1831 and 1832, came to doubt the popular belief that the disease was carried by foul-smelling air ______ 1849, he published an essay arguing that cholera spread through water contaminated with the waste of infected people.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 긴 동격 삽입구(a young surgeon's apprentice ... 1832)를 건너뛰면 주절은 "John Snow ... came to doubt the popular belief ... air"이고, 빈칸 뒤 "in 1849, he published ..."도 주어 he가 있는 독립절이다. 독립절 두 개는 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 되고, B는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. C는 관계사 which를 넣지만 뒤 절에 이미 주어 he가 있어 which가 문장 안에서 할 역할이 없으므로 비문이 된다.
g.explanation_en: If you skip over the long appositive (a young surgeon's apprentice ... 1832), the main clause is "John Snow ... came to doubt the popular belief ... air," and what follows the blank, "in 1849, he published ...," is also an independent clause with its own subject, he. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so D is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice, and B puts them together with no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. C adds the relative pronoun which, but the clause after it already has a subject (he), so which has no job to do in the sentence and the result is ungrammatical.
g.design: 긴 동격 삽입구 때문에 주절의 동사를 바로 찾기 어렵게 했다. 그래서 학생은 두 독립절이 맞닿는 경계를 먼저 찾은 다음, 쉼표 오용·무종지문·관계절 오답과 비교해 알맞은 부호를 골라야 한다.

g.passage: Hong Xiuquan, a failed civil service candidate who came to believe after reading Christian missionary tracts that he was the younger brother of Jesus, founded the God Worshipping Society in Guangxi Province in the 1840s______ his followers had captured the city of Nanjing, which they renamed Tianjing, or "Heavenly Capital," and made the seat of their rebel kingdom.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 긴 동격구(a failed ... Jesus)를 걷어내면 주절은 'Hong Xiuquan ... founded the God Worshipping Society ... in the 1840s'이고, 빈칸 뒤 'his followers had captured ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결해야 하므로 정답은 A이다. B는 'by 1853' 뒤 쉼표는 맞지만 두 절을 쉼표만으로 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 which가 관계절을 만드는 듯 보이지만 관계절 안에 his followers라는 주어가 따로 있고 which가 맡을 역할이 없어 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: If you set aside the long appositive (a failed ... Jesus), the main clause is "Hong Xiuquan ... founded the God Worshipping Society ... in the 1840s," and the words after the blank, "his followers had captured ...," form another independent clause with its own subject and verb. Two independent clauses can be joined with a semicolon, so A is correct. B puts a comma correctly after "by 1853," but joining two clauses with only a comma creates a comma splice. C joins the clauses with no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D looks like it starts a relative clause, but that clause already has its own subject, "his followers," so "which" has no job to do and the sentence doesn't work.
g.design: 긴 동격 삽입구 뒤에서 두 독립절의 경계를 판단하게 했고, 오답은 모두 같은 'by 1853,' 틀을 공유하면서 쉼표 스플라이스·무종지문·잘못된 관계사로 함정을 만들었다.

g.passage: Signed in 1842 aboard a British warship anchored on the Yangtze River, the Treaty of Nanjing—the first of what Chinese historians would later call the "unequal treaties" ______ the Qing government to open five coastal cities, including Shanghai and Guangzhou, to British merchants and to cede the island of Hong Kong.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: "the first of ... 'unequal treaties'"는 주어 the Treaty of Nanjing을 설명하는 동격 삽입구로, 앞에서 대시로 열렸으므로 같은 대시로 닫아야 하고 그 뒤에 동사 forced가 와야 한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표를 써서 삽입구를 닫으려 하지만 대시로 연 삽입구를 쉼표로 닫으면 문장부호가 짝이 맞지 않는다. C의 세미콜론은 주어와 동사를 갈라놓아 앞부분이 동사 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다. D는 닫는 문장부호가 없어서 삽입구가 끝나는 지점이 표시되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "the first of ... 'unequal treaties'" is an appositive that describes the subject, the Treaty of Nanjing. It opens with a dash, so it has to close with a dash too, and then the verb "forced" follows. That makes B correct. A tries to close the appositive with a comma, but a phrase opened with a dash can't be closed with a comma because the punctuation doesn't match. C puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, which leaves the first part as an incomplete sentence with no verb. D has no closing punctuation at all, so nothing shows where the appositive ends.
g.design: 긴 도입 분사구와 대시로 열린 동격 삽입구가 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있다. 학생은 삽입구가 대시로 열렸다는 점과, 빈칸 뒤 단어가 주절의 동사라는 점을 함께 확인해야 한다. A의 쉼표와 D의 무부호는 얼핏 그럴듯해 보인다.

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Tanzimat ("reorganization") was a period of reform in the Ottoman Empire lasting from 1839 to 1876.
- The 1839 Edict of Gülhane promised security of life and property to all subjects and called for regular, fair taxation.
- The 1856 Reform Edict went further, declaring Muslim and non-Muslim subjects equal before the law.
- In 1850, the empire adopted a commercial code modeled closely on the French Commercial Code.
- In 1876, a group of reformers known as the Young Ottomans helped bring about the empire's first constitution, which created an elected parliament.
- The 1876 constitution was suspended by Sultan Abdülhamid II in 1878.
g.question: The student wants to emphasize how far the reforms of 1856 extended beyond those of 1839. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The Tanzimat began with the 1839 Edict of Gülhane and ended in 1876, when reformers helped bring about the empire's first constitution.
Like the 1850 commercial code, which was modeled on French law, the 1856 Reform Edict reflected the Tanzimat's interest in European legal systems.
Whereas the 1839 Edict of Gülhane had promised all subjects security of life and property, the 1856 Reform Edict declared Muslims and non-Muslims equal before the law.
The 1839 Edict of Gülhane promised fair taxation, and the 1876 constitution, though suspended two years later, created an elected parliament.
g.explanation: 목표는 1856년 개혁이 1839년 개혁보다 얼마나 더 나아갔는지 강조하는 것이다. C는 1839년 칙령의 생명·재산 보장과 1856년 칙령의 종교 간 법적 평등을 대조해 확장된 범위를 보여 준다. A는 탄지마트의 시작과 끝을 말할 뿐 1856년 칙령을 언급하지 않는다. B는 1856년 칙령을 다루지만 1850년 상법과의 공통점을 말할 뿐 1839년과 비교하지 않는다. D는 1839년과 1876년을 연결해 1856년이 빠져 있다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to show how much further the 1856 reforms went than the 1839 ones. C does this by contrasting the 1839 edict's promise of security of life and property with the 1856 edict's declaration that Muslims and non-Muslims were legally equal. A only gives the start and end of the Tanzimat and never mentions the 1856 edict. B does discuss the 1856 edict, but it links it to the 1850 commercial code instead of comparing it with 1839. D pairs 1839 with 1876 and leaves 1856 out completely.
g.design: To answer, students have to pick the 1839 and 1856 notes and present them as a contrast. Two wrong choices (B and D) each mention one of the right edicts, so a student who skims could be drawn to them. The question's wording doesn't repeat key words from C, such as "equal" or "security."

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Suez Canal, connecting the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea, opened in November 1869.
- Before the canal, ships traveling between Britain and India typically sailed around Africa's Cape of Good Hope.
- The canal shortened the sea voyage from London to Bombay (now Mumbai) by roughly 4,500 miles.
- The project was led by French diplomat Ferdinand de Lesseps and financed largely by French investors and Egypt's ruler, Khedive Ismail.
- In 1875, facing heavy debts, Ismail sold Egypt's shares in the canal company to the British government.
g.question: The student wants to explain how control over the canal shifted after it opened. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Opened in 1869, the Suez Canal let ships traveling between London and Bombay avoid the long route around Africa's Cape of Good Hope.
Led by French diplomat Ferdinand de Lesseps, the Suez Canal was financed largely by French investors and Egypt's ruler, Khedive Ismail.
Opened in 1869, the Suez Canal shortened the sea voyage from London to Bombay by roughly 4,500 miles, a change of great value to Britain.
Financed largely by French investors and Khedive Ismail, the Suez Canal gained a major new stakeholder in 1875, when the debt-burdened Ismail sold Egypt's shares to Britain.
g.explanation: 목표는 개통 이후 운하에 대한 지배권(소유)이 어떻게 바뀌었는지 설명하는 것이다. D는 처음의 재정 주체(프랑스 투자자와 이스마일)와 1875년 영국으로의 지분 매각을 연결해 변화를 보여 준다. B는 초기 소유·재정 구조만 제시할 뿐 이후의 변화가 없다. A와 C는 항로 단축이라는 운하의 무역상 효과를 다루며 C가 영국을 언급하지만 지배권 이동은 설명하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to explain how control of the canal changed after it opened. D does this by linking the original backers (French investors and Ismail) to the 1875 sale of Egypt's shares to Britain, so you can see the shift. B only tells you who first paid for the canal and leaves out any later change. A and C are about the shorter trade route. C mentions Britain, but it never says that control moved to Britain.
g.design: To get this right, you have to connect two notes: the original financing and the 1875 sale. B uses only half of that pair. C mentions Britain, which may tempt a student who reads quickly, but it is about the trade route, not ownership. The question avoids the words "shares" and "sold."

g.passage: The 1854 Treaty of Kanagawa, signed after Commodore Matthew Perry arrived in Edo Bay with armed American warships, is often described as the moment Japan's sakoku policy of isolation ended. Yet the treaty's actual terms were narrow: it opened only two remote ports, Shimoda and Hakodate, to American ships for supplies and shelter, guaranteed fair treatment of shipwrecked sailors, and allowed a U.S. consul to live at Shimoda. It said nothing about general trade, which Japanese negotiators had specifically refused. That kind of commerce came only with the 1858 Harris Treaty, which opened additional ports to merchants and set tariff rates. Historian Mitani Hiroshi therefore argues that Kanagawa should be seen as a limited concession that Japanese officials accepted to avoid a conflict, not as the full reversal of sakoku. If Mitani is correct, then accounts that credit Perry's 1854 visit alone with opening Japan to the world ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: give too little weight to the later agreement that actually allowed foreign merchants to do business in Japan.
give too little weight to how Perry's warships forced Japanese officials to sign the 1854 agreement.
give too little weight to how the 1854 agreement completely ended Japan's policy of isolation.
give too little weight to how much Japanese negotiators wanted to expand foreign trade in 1854.
g.explanation: 미타니는 가나가와 조약이 보급·피난용 항구 두 곳만 연 제한적 양보였고, 실제 통상은 1858년 해리스 조약에서야 가능해졌다고 본다. 따라서 페리 방문만으로 일본이 개방되었다고 보는 서술은 후속 조약의 역할을 과소평가한다는 결론이 나오므로 A가 정답이다. B는 지문에 나온 군함 압박을 언급해 그럴듯하지만, 그런 서술은 오히려 페리의 압박을 강조하는 쪽이며 미타니의 논점(조약의 제한성)과 연결되지 않는다. C는 미타니의 주장과 정반대이다. D는 일본 협상단이 일반 통상을 거부했다는 지문 내용과 모순된다.
g.explanation_en: Mitani argues that the Treaty of Kanagawa was a limited concession that opened just two ports for supplies and shelter, and that real trade began only with the 1858 Harris Treaty. So any account that gives Perry's 1854 visit all the credit for opening Japan overlooks that later treaty, which is why A is correct. B sounds reasonable because the passage does mention the warships, but accounts that credit Perry already stress his pressure, and Mitani's point is about how limited the treaty was. C says the opposite of what Mitani argues. D contradicts the passage, which says Japanese negotiators refused general trade.
g.design: To answer, you have to connect the treaty's narrow terms with the trade that came later under the Harris Treaty. B and C use real details from the passage or the popular view, and only careful reading rules them out.

c.seed: history and civics — Serfdom abolition Russia 1861 Alexander II emancipation decree and peasant land redistribution reform consequences

g.passage: Russia's 1861 emancipation decree, issued by Alexander II, freed roughly 23 million privately owned serfs from personal bondage. The land they had farmed, however, did not simply become theirs. Former serfs received allotments that were often smaller than the plots they had worked before, and they had to pay for that land through "redemption payments" spread over 49 years. In most regions, these allotments were also assigned to the village commune rather than to individual households, and the commune was collectively responsible for the debt; a peasant who wished to leave the village permanently generally needed the commune's permission. Historians who examine the reform's economic effects therefore argue that, although emancipation ended serfs' legal ownership by landlords, ______
g.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: it did little to change the size of the plots that most peasant households farmed, since allotments generally matched the land serfs had worked before.
it left many former serfs tied to their villages by obligations that limited their freedom to move or to farm on their own terms.
it removed the commune's authority over peasants by transferring responsibility for land debts to individual households.
it immediately made former serfs wealthier than before, since the redemption payments were spread over several decades.
g.explanation: 지문은 소유권 해방(양보)과 대비해, 49년 상환 부담, 코뮌의 공동 책임, 마을을 떠나려면 허가가 필요했다는 점을 함께 제시하므로, 농민이 여전히 의무에 묶여 있었다는 B가 논리적 결론이다. A는 토지 문제를 다루지만 할당지가 이전보다 작았다는 지문 내용과 모순된다. C는 코뮌과 부채를 언급하지만 부채가 개별 가구가 아니라 코뮌에 귀속되었다는 사실을 뒤집는다. D는 장기 분할 상환이라는 사실을 근거로 삼지만, 더 작은 땅과 수십 년의 부채는 즉각적인 부를 뒷받침하지 않으며 'although' 대비 구조에도 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The passage contrasts legal freedom with the reform's continuing burdens: 49 years of payments, collective debt held by the commune, and the need for the commune's permission to leave. Choice B pulls these details together into the logical conclusion. Choice A deals with land but contradicts the passage, which says allotments were often smaller than before. Choice C mentions the commune and debt but reverses the facts, since the debt belonged to the commune, not to individual households. Choice D builds on the long repayment period, but smaller plots and decades of debt don't suggest instant wealth, and D also doesn't fit the contrast set up by "although."
g.design: To get this right, students have to link two details (the commune's collective debt and the permission needed to leave) to the "although" contrast. Choices A, C, and D each reuse a real detail from the passage (plot size, the commune and debt, the payment schedule) but distort it.

c.seed: economics and business — Consignment inventory system supplier-managed stock and risk transfer in automotive parts supply chain logistics

g.passage: Under a consignment inventory system, an automotive parts supplier keeps its own brake pads and filters on the shelves of a car manufacturer's warehouse. The manufacturer does not pay for a part until it is pulled from the shelf for use on the assembly line ______ the supplier carries the financial risk of any stock that sits unused.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The manufacturer does not pay ... line"과 빈칸 뒤 "the supplier carries ... unused"는 각각 독립절이므로 마침표 같은 적절한 경계가 필요하다. C는 마침표로 두 절을 분리하고 "Until then,"을 둘째 문장의 도입구로 붙여 올바르다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 아무 부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D도 쉼표만으로 독립절을 연결해 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("The manufacturer does not pay ... line") and the text after it ("the supplier carries ... unused") are both independent clauses, so they need a proper boundary like a period. C works because it ends the first sentence with a period and starts the second with the introductory phrase "Until then,". A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B puts no punctuation between them at all, so it's a run-on sentence. D still uses only commas to join the clauses, so it's also a comma splice.
g.design: Easy: two clearly independent clauses with a single boundary rule (no comma splice/run-on); distractors are the typical comma splice and run-on errors.

c.seed: economics and business — Hedge fund quantitative arbitrage strategy statistical price divergence exploitation across correlated security markets

g.passage: Some hedge funds use a quantitative strategy called statistical arbitrage. Analysts track pairs of securities whose prices usually move together, such as the stocks of two similar oil companies. When the prices of a pair suddenly drift apart, the fund buys the cheaper security and sells the more expensive ______ if the prices return to their normal relationship, the fund profits from the gap closing.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "the fund buys ... more expensive one"과 뒤 "if the prices return ..., the fund profits ..."는 각각 독립절이다. 접속사 없이 두 독립절을 잇는 데는 세미콜론이 적절하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 잇는 쉼표 스플라이스이다. B는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. C는 "and" 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표가 들어가 문장 흐름을 부적절하게 끊는다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("the fund buys ... the more expensive one") and the text after it ("if the prices return ..., the fund profits ...") are both independent clauses. A semicolon is the right way to join two independent clauses when there's no conjunction, so D is correct. A creates a comma splice, because a comma alone can't join two independent clauses. B creates a run-on sentence, because the two clauses are joined with no punctuation at all. C puts an unnecessary comma after "and," which wrongly breaks up the sentence.
g.design: 독립절 두 개가 한눈에 보이는 경계에 세미콜론/쉼표 스플라이스/무종지문/잘못된 쉼표 위치를 대비해 한 가지 규칙만으로 풀게 했다.

c.seed: economics and business — Franchise fee structure and royalty percentage optimization balancing franchisor profitability with franchisee viability

g.passage: When franchisors set royalty rates, they face a delicate trade-off. A higher percentage of each outlet's sales increases the franchisor's revenue in the short term, but it can squeeze franchisees' margins so tightly that struggling owners close their locations. Economist Francine Lafontaine's studies of franchise contracts suggest that the most durable systems, rather than maximizing upfront fees, ______ royalties modest enough that the typical franchisee can still earn a reasonable return.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸은 that절의 주어 'the most durable systems'의 정동사 자리이며, 삽입구 'rather than maximizing upfront fees'를 건너뛰어야 구조가 보인다. 복수 주어에 맞는 현재형 정동사 A(keep)가 정답이다. B는 삽입구의 'maximizing'과 병렬처럼 보이지만 분사라 that절에 정동사가 없게 된다. C의 to부정사, D의 완료분사도 정동사가 아니므로 절이 불완전하다.
g.explanation_en: The blank needs the main verb of the that-clause, whose subject is "the most durable systems"; you have to skip over the interrupting phrase "rather than maximizing upfront fees" to see this. Choice A, "keep," is a finite present-tense verb that agrees with the plural subject, so it's correct. Choice B may look parallel to "maximizing," but a participle can't serve as the clause's main verb. Choices C (an infinitive) and D (a perfect participle) also aren't finite verbs, so they leave the clause incomplete.
g.design: 주어와 빈칸 사이에 -ing 삽입구를 넣어, 훑어 읽으면 병렬형(keeping)이나 비정형 동사를 고르도록 유도했다. 정동사가 필요하다는 구조 판단을 하고 주어와의 일치까지 확인해야 하는 두 단계 판단이다.

c.seed: economics and business — Spot market price volatility versus futures contract hedging in agricultural commodity farmer revenue stabilization

g.passage: Wheat growers who sell their harvest on the spot market face prices that can swing sharply within a single season. To limit this exposure, many farmers lock in a sale price months before harvest by selling futures contracts. The practice of hedging a portion of expected output with such contracts, according to agricultural economists who have tracked farm incomes across several decades, ______ year-to-year revenue considerably, though it also caps the gains farmers can capture when spot prices surge.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'The practice'이며, 'of hedging ... contracts'와 'according to ... decades'는 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 수식어구일 뿐이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 단수 주어에 맞는 정동사가 필요하므로 B가 정답이다. A와 D는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사(contracts, economists, decades)에 맞춘 복수형이어서 주어와 수가 일치하지 않는다. C는 분사라서 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 완전한 문장이 되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The practice." The phrases "of hedging ... contracts" and "according to ... decades" are just modifiers that come between the subject and its verb. So the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, which makes B correct. A and D are finite verbs, but they're plural forms that match the nearby plural nouns (contracts, economists, decades) instead of the actual subject. C is a participle, so it would leave the sentence without a main verb, and it wouldn't be a complete sentence.
g.design: 긴 전치사구와 삽입구 안에 복수 명사를 여러 개 넣어 훑어 읽으면 복수 동사를 고르게 했고, 분사 오답으로 정동사가 필요하다는 점도 함께 판단하게 했다.

c.seed: economics and business — Vertical integration backward control and transaction cost reduction in petroleum refining industry consolidation

g.passage: In the late nineteenth century, many American petroleum refiners began acquiring the pipelines, storage tanks, and crude-oil fields that supplied their plants. Economists have often explained this backward integration as a bid for market power: a firm that owned its suppliers could squeeze out rivals. Economic historian Lena Marsh argues that this account misses a more ordinary motive. Refiners that bought crude on the open market had to bargain repeatedly with independent producers and pipeline operators, and they often faced sudden price demands when supplies ran short. Writing and enforcing contracts to guard against such behavior was costly and frequently failed. By owning the supply chain, Marsh contends, refiners replaced these uncertain negotiations with internal coordination, lowering the everyday expense of keeping their refineries running. Monopoly ambitions, in her view, were sometimes present but were not what made integration attractive to most firms.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Marsh argues that refiners integrated backward mainly because owning crude-oil fields allowed them to drive independent producers out of the market.
Marsh argues that refiners integrated backward mainly because contracts with pipeline operators were illegal to enforce in the late nineteenth century.
Marsh argues that refiners integrated backward mainly because bringing suppliers under their ownership reduced the costs and risks of repeatedly dealing with outside parties.
Marsh argues that refiners integrated backward mainly because crude oil was scarce, so owning fields guaranteed higher profits than refining did.
g.explanation: 지문의 핵심은 Marsh가 후방 통합을 시장 지배력 때문이 아니라, 외부 공급자와 반복 협상하고 계약을 집행하는 데 드는 비용을 내부 조정으로 줄이려는 일상적 동기로 설명한다는 것이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 Marsh가 반박하는 기존 경제학자들의 설명(경쟁자 축출)이다. B는 계약이 비용이 많이 들고 자주 실패했다는 내용을 '불법'으로 왜곡했다. D는 공급 부족이라는 세부 사항을 빌려 왔지만, 정제보다 유전 소유가 더 큰 이익을 냈다는 주장은 지문에 없다.
g.explanation_en: The text's central point is that Marsh explains backward integration not by market power but by an ordinary motive: owning suppliers swapped costly, repeated bargaining and unreliable contracts for internal coordination. That makes C correct. A gives the market-power explanation that Marsh is arguing against. B distorts the text, which says contracts were costly and often failed, not that they were illegal. D borrows the detail about supply shortages, but the text never claims that owning fields was more profitable than refining.
g.design: 오답 A·D는 지문 속 실제 요소(기존 설명, 공급 부족)를 가져와 일부만 맞게 만들었다. 그래서 반박 대상과 Marsh의 주장을 구분해야 풀리는 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. 질문은 일반형으로 써서 정답의 핵심어가 드러나지 않게 했다.

g.passage:
Economists have long assumed that a shopper's willingness to pay for a product reflects a stable, internal sense of its value. Studies of anchoring complicate that assumption. In one experiment, participants first wrote down the last two digits of an arbitrary number and then bid on items such as wireless keyboards and bottles of wine. Those whose digits were high consistently bid more than those whose digits were low, even though everyone understood that the number had nothing to do with the products.

Researchers who followed up on this finding noticed something further. Once an anchor had set a buyer's initial valuation, later price changes were judged relative to that starting point rather than in absolute terms. A buyer anchored high tended to treat a moderate price increase as tolerable, while a buyer anchored low reacted to the same increase by sharply cutting the quantity purchased. The anchor, in other words, shaped not only how much people were willing to pay at first but also how sensitive their demand was to subsequent changes in price.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Arbitrary numbers influence what buyers will pay for inexpensive goods but have little effect on their bids for costly items such as wine.
Buyers who receive a high anchor will pay more at first, but their demand eventually becomes more sensitive to price than that of buyers given a low anchor.
Economists have abandoned the view that willingness to pay reflects internal value, since buyers no longer judge price changes in absolute terms.
An irrelevant reference point can affect both a buyer's starting valuation of a product and how strongly that buyer responds when the price later changes.
g.explanation: 지문은 첫 단락에서 무관한 숫자(앵커)가 초기 입찰가에 영향을 준다고 하고, 둘째 단락에서 그 앵커가 이후 가격 변화에 대한 수요 민감도까지 좌우한다고 말한다. D는 이 두 가지를 모두 담고 있으므로 정답이다. A는 저가품과 고가품을 구분하지만, 지문에서 와인도 영향을 받았으므로 틀렸다. B는 높은 앵커가 초기 지불액을 높인다는 점은 맞지만, 오히려 높은 앵커를 받은 구매자가 가격 인상에 덜 민감했으므로 민감도 비교를 거꾸로 서술했다. C는 지문이 기존 가정을 '복잡하게 만든다'고만 했을 뿐 경제학자들이 이를 버렸다고 하지 않았고, 단정적 표현도 지나치다.
g.explanation_en: The first paragraph shows that an arbitrary number (an anchor) affects buyers' initial bids, and the second shows that the same anchor also shapes how sensitive their demand is to later price changes. D captures both points, so it is correct. A splits cheap goods from expensive ones, but the text says bids on wine were affected too. B is right that a high anchor raises the initial amount buyers will pay, but it reverses the sensitivity comparison: buyers anchored high were actually less responsive to a price increase. C overstates the text, which says anchoring studies "complicate" the old assumption, not that economists have abandoned it.
g.design: To pick the answer, students have to connect both paragraphs. Each of B and C uses one true detail but gets the details wrong or goes too far, and A misreads the examples. All four choices follow the same sentence pattern.

c.seed: economics and business — Spatial price discrimination market segmentation and delivery cost variation across geographic regions

g.passage: Economists have long assumed that when a cement producer charges distant customers more than nearby ones, the gap simply reflects the added cost of trucking heavy loads over longer distances. Studying delivered prices across several regional markets, economist Lena Okafor found a more complicated pattern. Customers located near a rival plant often paid less than the extra trucking cost would predict, while customers with no nearby alternative supplier paid noticeably more than that cost alone could explain. Okafor concluded that producers set delivered prices partly according to how much competition each location faces, so a buyer's distance from the plant explains only part of the price that buyer pays.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Research suggests that differences in what cement buyers in different places pay are shaped not only by shipping expenses but also by how many other suppliers can reach those buyers.
Research suggests that cement buyers located far from a plant generally pay higher prices than nearby buyers because trucking heavy loads over long distances is costly.
Research suggests that cement producers lower their prices for every customer whenever a rival plant opens anywhere in the same regional market.
Research suggests that cement producers should charge all customers the same price regardless of location in order to avoid losing buyers to rival plants.
g.design: 정답을 질문과 다른 표현(경쟁 공급자 수)으로 바꿔 말하고, 오답은 같은 'Research suggests that…' 틀로 기존 가정(B), 과잉일반화(C), 지문에 없는 처방(D)을 넣어 두 정보(거리+경쟁)의 연결을 요구했다.
g.explanation: 지문은 기존 가정(가격 차이=운송비)을 소개한 뒤, Okafor가 경쟁 업체 근처 고객은 더 적게, 대안이 없는 고객은 더 많이 낸다는 것을 발견해 가격이 경쟁 정도에도 좌우된다고 결론짓는다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 지문이 불완전하다고 본 기존 가정만 다시 말한다. C는 '모든 고객'에게 가격을 내린다고 과잉일반화하는데, 지문에서는 경쟁 업체 근처 고객만 해당한다. D는 지문에 나오지 않는 처방이다.
g.explanation_en: The text first describes the old assumption that price gaps simply reflect trucking costs. Then Okafor finds that buyers near rival plants pay less, while buyers with no alternative supplier pay more, so prices also depend on competition. That makes A the answer. B only restates the old assumption that the text calls incomplete. C overgeneralizes by saying prices drop for every customer, when only buyers near rivals pay less. D offers advice that the text never gives.

c.seed: economics and business — Tournament compensation structure relative performance ranking and incentive intensity in sales force management

g.passage: Many companies pay their sales representatives through tournament-style schemes, in which bonuses depend not on how much each person sells but on how each person ranks against colleagues. Economists have long argued that such schemes sharpen effort, since a modest gain in sales can lift a worker past a rival and into a much larger prize. Yet a 2021 field study of a regional insurance firm by economist Laila Haddad complicates this view. When the firm widened the gap between first- and second-place bonuses, top-ranked and bottom-ranked agents changed little, while agents in the middle of the rankings sharply increased the number of client calls they made. Haddad concluded that steeper prizes do raise effort, but mostly among workers who believe a single strong month could realistically change their position; those far ahead or far behind see little reason to respond.
g.question: Based on the text, what did Haddad's study suggest about the firm's agents?
options: Larger differences between bonus levels raised effort fairly evenly across all agents, confirming the long-standing argument of economists.
Larger differences between bonus levels mattered chiefly to agents whose rank seemed open to change in the near term.
Larger differences between bonus levels discouraged bottom-ranked agents so much that their client calls declined below earlier levels.
Larger differences between bonus levels mattered chiefly to top-ranked agents, who worked harder to protect their first-place prizes.
g.explanation: 지문에 따르면 상금 격차를 키웠을 때 순위 중간에 있는 직원들만 고객 전화를 크게 늘렸습니다. Haddad는 그 이유를 이들이 한 달만 잘해도 순위를 바꿀 수 있다고 믿기 때문이라고 결론지었으므로 B가 정답입니다. A는 노력이 높아졌다는 부분은 맞지만, 노력이 고르게 늘었다고 말해 상위와 하위 직원의 변화가 적었다는 내용과 모순됩니다. C는 하위 직원이 반응하지 않았다는 부분은 맞지만, 전화 수가 줄었다는 내용은 지문에 없습니다. D는 실제로 거의 변화가 없었던 상위 직원에게 효과를 돌리고 있으므로 오답입니다.
g.explanation_en: The text says that when the bonus gap grew, only the agents in the middle of the rankings made many more client calls. Haddad explained this by saying these agents believed one strong month could change their rank, so B is correct. A gets it right that effort rose, but it says the rise was even across all agents, which contradicts the text's point that top and bottom agents changed little. C is right that bottom agents didn't respond, but the text never says their calls dropped. D gives the effect to top-ranked agents, who actually changed little, so it is wrong.
g.design: 독자는 두 정보를 연결해야 한다. 하나는 중간 순위 직원만 반응했다는 결과이고, 다른 하나는 그 이유가 순위를 바꿀 수 있다는 믿음이라는 결론이다. 정답 B는 '중간 순위'를 '단기간에 순위가 바뀔 수 있어 보이는 직원'으로 바꿔 말한다. 오답 A와 C는 각각 일부가 맞는 근거를 담고 있다.

c.seed: economics and business — Matching markets two-sided platform design and preference heterogeneity in labor recruitment intermediation

g.passage: Online recruitment platforms that connect employers with job seekers are often assumed to work best when they maximize the number of applications each posting receives, since more applicants should give firms more chances to find a good fit. Economist Peter Coles and colleagues found that this assumption breaks down when workers and employers differ widely in what they value: as applications multiply, employers struggle to tell which candidates are genuinely interested and which are applying indiscriminately. ______ platforms that limited how many "priority signals" each job seeker could send, forcing applicants to reveal their strongest preferences, produced more interviews and more accepted offers than platforms that allowed unlimited applications.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.design: 빈칸 앞에서 무제한 지원이 고용주의 판단을 어렵게 만든다는 문제(원인)를 제시하고, 뒤에서는 그 문제에 맞춘 해결책이 거둔 성과(결과)를 제시했다. 'For instance'는 구체화로, 'Nevertheless'는 첫 문장의 통념과 대조되는 것으로 착각하게 만드는 함정으로 설계했다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 문장은 지원서가 늘어날수록 고용주가 진짜 관심 있는 지원자를 가려내기 어려워진다는 문제를 설명한다. 빈칸 뒤 문장은 지원자가 선호를 드러내게 만든 플랫폼이 더 좋은 결과를 냈다고 하므로, 앞서 밝힌 문제에서 자연스럽게 따라 나오는 결과이다. 그래서 C가 정답이다. A는 '최대화' 통념과 대조된다는 점에서 그럴듯해 보이지만, 바로 앞 문장과는 반전 관계가 아니라 앞 내용을 이어 가는 관계이다. B는 비슷한 사례를 하나 더 드는 표현인데, 뒤 문장은 비슷한 문제가 아니라 그 문제의 해결책을 다룬다. D는 뒤 문장을 앞 문장의 예시로 보는 것인데, 신호 제한 플랫폼은 고용주가 겪는 어려움의 예가 아니라 그 어려움에 대한 대응이다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank describes a problem: as applications pile up, employers can't easily tell which candidates are really interested. The sentence after the blank reports that platforms that made applicants reveal their preferences got better results, which follows logically from that problem. That makes C the answer. A may seem tempting because the findings contrast with the "maximize applications" assumption, but the sentence right before the blank isn't being reversed; it's being built on. B would introduce a parallel case, but the final sentence describes a solution to the problem, not a similar problem. D would treat the final sentence as an example of the employers' difficulty, but the signal-limiting platforms are a response to that difficulty, not an example of it.

c.seed: economics and business — Slack resources excess capacity and organizational resilience buffer in manufacturing inventory management strategy

g.passage: For decades, many manufacturers treated surplus inventory and idle machine capacity as pure waste, and lean production methods aimed to strip such "slack" from factories to cut storage and maintenance costs. Management researchers studying supply disruptions have reached a less flattering verdict on that approach. Plants that kept modest reserves of parts and spare production lines often absorbed shortages with little loss of output, while their leaner competitors were forced to halt assembly for weeks. ______ the extra resources that once looked like inefficiency on a balance sheet can work as a buffer that keeps a firm running when conditions suddenly change.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 문장은 여유 재고를 가진 공장이 공급 차질을 잘 견뎠다는 구체적 결과를 제시하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 결과의 의미를 '비효율처럼 보이던 자원이 완충 장치 역할을 한다'고 다시 풀어 말하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 지문 앞부분의 린 생산 관점과 대비되는 느낌 때문에 끌리지만, 바로 앞 문장과 빈칸 뒤 문장은 서로 반대되지 않고 같은 방향이다. B는 구체적 사례를 이끄는 말인데, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 사례가 아니라 앞 사례를 일반화한 내용이다. C는 새로운 유사 사례를 덧붙일 때 쓰는 말이지만, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 다른 사례가 아니라 앞 내용의 요약이다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank gives a specific finding: plants with spare parts and spare lines handled shortages well. The sentence after the blank restates what that finding means in general terms, saying that "wasteful" slack actually works as a buffer. So D is correct. A may look tempting because the passage contrasts the lean view with the research, but the two sentences around the blank point the same way and don't contradict each other. B would introduce an example, but the final sentence is a generalization, not an example. C would add a parallel case, but the final sentence sums up the earlier point instead of adding a new one.
g.design: The passage opens with a contrast (lean view vs. research), so a quick reader may pick A. Choosing D takes two steps: noticing that the sentences right around the blank agree with each other, then seeing that the last sentence generalizes the evidence rather than giving another case.

c.seed: economics and business — Dual labor market segmentation primary sector stability versus secondary sector precarity wage inequality persistence

g.passage: Standard labor economics predicts that wage gaps between similar workers should shrink over time: if two people have comparable skills, employers competing for talent will bid their pay toward the same level. Economists Peter Doeringer and Michael Piore argued in the early 1970s that this prediction fails because the labor market is divided into two largely separate sectors. Jobs in the primary sector offer stable employment, internal promotion ladders, and rising wages, while jobs in the secondary sector are short-term, poorly paid, and offer little training. __Crucially, employers in the primary sector often read a history of frequent job changes as a sign of unreliability, even when those changes were caused by layoffs rather than by the worker.__ As a result, workers who begin in the secondary sector can find themselves locked out of better jobs regardless of their abilities, and wage inequality persists rather than fading.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It identifies a way that hiring practices keep workers from moving between sectors, which explains why the expected narrowing of wage gaps does not occur.
It identifies a difference in training between the two sectors, which explains why primary-sector workers have greater skills than secondary-sector workers.
It identifies a flaw in Doeringer and Piore's model, which explains why some economists still accept the standard prediction about wages.
It identifies a cause of layoffs in the secondary sector, which explains why secondary-sector jobs tend to be short-term.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 1차 부문 고용주가 잦은 이직 경력을 불신의 신호로 읽는다는 점을 들어, 2차 부문 노동자가 더 나은 일자리로 이동하지 못하는 장벽을 제시한다. 이것이 다음 문장의 "As a result"로 이어져 임금 격차가 줄지 않는 이유를 설명하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 지문에 훈련 차이가 언급되긴 하지만 밑줄 문장의 내용은 훈련이 아니라 채용 시 판단이며, 지문은 오히려 능력과 무관하다고 말한다. C는 밑줄 문장이 모델을 비판하지 않고 뒷받침한다는 점에서 틀린다. D는 해고가 언급되지만 해고의 원인을 설명하는 문장이 아니다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence explains that primary-sector employers treat frequent job changes as a red flag, which creates a barrier stopping secondary-sector workers from moving up. The next sentence, beginning "As a result," uses this barrier to explain why wage inequality persists instead of shrinking, so A is correct. B is wrong because, although the text does mention training differences, the underlined sentence is about hiring judgments, and the text actually says workers are shut out regardless of their abilities. C is wrong because the sentence supports Doeringer and Piore's model rather than criticizing it. D is wrong because the sentence mentions layoffs but doesn't explain what causes them.
g.design: To get this right, students must link the hiring-signal detail to the "As a result" conclusion about wage gaps that don't close. Choices B and D reuse real details from the text (training, layoffs) but describe the wrong function.
