c.seed: economics and business — Markdown markdown optimization timing and seasonal demand forecasting in retail inventory markdown management

g.passage: Retailers that sell seasonal goods, such as winter coats or patio furniture, face a recurring dilemma: when to cut prices on unsold stock. Traditionally, many chains marked items down on a fixed calendar, applying discounts to all stores in the same week. Analysts at several apparel companies have argued that this approach ignores local variation in demand, since a cold spell in one region can keep coats selling at full price while stores elsewhere are already overstocked. __Yet when one chain tested store-by-store markdown timing based on weekly sales forecasts, it found that the forecasts were reliable only in stores with several years of sales history, while newer locations saw no improvement over the fixed calendar.__ The result suggests that flexible markdown timing may be most useful where enough past data exist to predict how local demand will change over a season.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that fully overturns the analysts' criticism of applying the same markdown schedule to every store.
It reports a finding that limits how widely the analysts' proposed alternative can be expected to succeed.
It offers an example illustrating how a cold spell can keep regional coat sales at full price.
It reports a finding explaining why retailers first adopted a fixed markdown calendar for all stores.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해, 매장별 할인 시점 조정이 판매 이력이 긴 매장에서만 효과가 있었다는 결과를 제시하며 분석가들의 대안이 적용될 수 있는 범위를 제한한다. 마지막 문장도 '데이터가 충분한 곳에서 가장 유용하다'고 정리하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 반박의 방향은 일부 맞지만, 기존 매장에서는 개선이 있었으므로 비판을 '완전히 뒤집는' 것은 아니다. C는 한파 사례가 앞 문장에 나오지만 밑줄 문장은 그 사례를 보여주는 문장이 아니다. D는 고정 달력과 비교한 내용이 있어 그럴듯하지만, 소매업체들이 처음 그 방식을 채택한 이유는 다루지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence starts with "Yet" and reports that store-by-store markdown timing helped only in stores with long sales histories, so it limits how widely the analysts' proposed alternative can be expected to work. The final sentence backs this up by concluding that flexible timing works best where there is enough data, so B is correct. A gets the direction partly right, but the test did not fully overturn the criticism, because established stores did improve. C refers back to the cold-spell example in the previous sentence, but the underlined sentence does not illustrate that example. D sounds plausible because the sentence compares results to the fixed calendar, but it never explains why retailers adopted that calendar in the first place.
g.design: 이 문항은 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. 먼저 'Yet'이 만드는 대조를 파악하고, 그다음 마지막 문장의 결론과 연결해 밑줄 문장이 대안을 '제한'한다는 점을 확인해야 한다. A는 반박의 정도를 과장했고, C와 D는 지문과 표면적으로 겹치는 내용을 이용한 오답이다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: economics and business — Premium pricing quality signal and brand reputation asymmetric information reduction in luxury goods markets

g.passage: Economists have long puzzled over why some shoppers seem to prefer a handbag or watch precisely because it costs more. One explanation draws on the problem of asymmetric information: a seller knows far more about a product's materials and craftsmanship than a buyer can learn in a store. When quality is hard to verify, a high price can act as a signal, since only a firm confident that its goods will satisfy customers can afford to charge a premium and still earn repeat business. __Yet a price alone is cheap to set, and a new firm could simply copy a luxury label's price tag without matching its stitching or leather.__ What makes the signal credible, researchers argue, is the brand reputation built over decades: a firm with a long record has much to lose if a single disappointing product damages trust, so its premium price is backed by that accumulated reputation in a way a newcomer's price is not.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that luxury shoppers routinely misjudge quality, showing that the signaling explanation should be abandoned.
It describes a strategy commonly used by new firms, illustrating how premium pricing helps unfamiliar brands enter luxury markets.
It raises a weakness in the explanation just described, setting up the claim about what allows a high price to convey quality reliably.
It restates the problem of asymmetric information, emphasizing that buyers cannot learn about materials before purchase.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 "가격만으로 신호가 된다"는 앞의 설명에 대해, 가격은 누구나 흉내 낼 수 있다는 한계를 지적한다. 이어지는 문장은 그 한계를 브랜드 평판으로 해결하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 한계를 지적한 것은 맞지만 지문은 신호 이론을 버리지 않고 보완한다. B는 신생 기업이 언급되지만 그것은 가설적 모방 사례일 뿐 시장 진입에 도움이 된다는 내용이 아니다. D는 정보 비대칭과 관련은 있으나 밑줄 문장은 문제를 재진술하는 것이 아니라 가격 신호의 약점을 제기한다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence points out a flaw in the idea that price alone signals quality: anyone can copy a price tag. The next sentence then answers that flaw by explaining that brand reputation makes the signal credible, so C is correct. A is wrong because, although the sentence raises a problem, the text refines the signaling explanation rather than abandoning it. B is wrong because the new firm appears only as a hypothetical copycat, not as an example of pricing helping entry. D is wrong because the sentence doesn't restate the information gap; it challenges whether price can bridge it.
g.design: Distractors A and D partly fit (a problem is raised; asymmetric information is relevant), and B misreads the newcomer mention; correct answer requires linking the sentence to both the prior claim and the following resolution.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 해당 skill 의 전형적 SAT 문항 형식을 따른다.
c.seed: economics and business — Options contract asymmetric payoff structure and upside capture in commodity price risk management

g.passage: Many farmers protect themselves against falling crop prices by locking in a sale price months before harvest through a forward contract. This approach removes the danger of a price collapse, but it also removes any benefit if prices rise. A grain producer who agreed to sell at $5 per bushel must accept $5 even if the market later reaches $7. Some agricultural economists therefore favor put options, which give a producer the right, but not the obligation, to sell at a set price. __If prices fall below that set price, the producer exercises the option; if prices climb, the producer simply lets it expire and sells at the higher market rate.__ The option costs an upfront fee, yet for producers who expect volatile markets, that fee buys protection without giving up potential gains.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why forward contracts eliminate the risk of a sudden collapse in crop prices.
It points out a cost of put options that makes them less attractive than forward contracts for most producers.
It gives an example of a producer who lost potential earnings by committing to a fixed sale price.
It shows how a put option lets a producer avoid losses from falling prices while still benefiting from rising ones.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 가격이 하락하면 옵션을 행사하고 상승하면 만료시켜 시장가로 판다는 내용으로, 풋옵션이 하락 위험을 막으면서 상승 이익도 누리게 하는 방식을 보여주므로 D가 정답이다. A는 선도계약의 하락 위험 제거를 다루지만, 그 내용은 앞 문장에 나오고 밑줄 문장은 옵션을 설명한다. B의 비용(선불 수수료)은 마지막 문장에 나오며, 지문은 옵션을 덜 매력적이라고 평가하지 않는다. C의 $5/$7 사례는 밑줄 문장이 아니라 셋째 문장의 역할이다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence says the producer uses the option when prices fall and lets it expire when prices rise, so it shows how a put option protects against losses while keeping the upside. That makes D correct. A is about forward contracts, which come up in earlier sentences, but the underlined sentence describes options. B points to the upfront fee, which appears only in the last sentence, and the text never says this cost makes options less attractive. C describes the $5/$7 example, but that example is in the third sentence, not the underlined one.
g.design: 오답 A·C는 지문의 다른 문장 내용을 정확히 담아 위치를 혼동하면 고르게 했고, B는 마지막 문장의 비용을 왜곡했다. 정답을 고르려면 밑줄 문장이 옵션의 비대칭 손익을 설명한다는 점을 앞뒤 문맥과 연결해야 한다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: economics and business — Monopsony buyer market power concentration and wage suppression in single-industry rural labor towns

g.passage: Economists studying single-industry rural towns, where one poultry processor or sawmill may employ most of the local workforce, describe such employers as monopsonists: buyers of labor facing little competition from other firms. Because workers in these towns often cannot easily relocate, the dominant employer can set wages below what a competitive market would ______ economist Alan Manning has argued that this kind of buyer power, rather than low worker productivity, explains much of the wage gap between isolated and diversified labor markets.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Because ... produce"는 종속절과 주절로 이루어진 완전한 문장이고, 뒤의 "economist Alan Manning has argued ..."도 독립절이므로 두 절 사이에는 세미콜론 같은 강한 경계가 필요하며, 접속부사 indeed는 두 번째 절을 시작하므로 세미콜론 뒤에 쉼표와 함께 와야 한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 이음(comma splice)이 된다. C는 세미콜론을 indeed 뒤에 두어 indeed가 앞 절에 붙어 버리므로 의미상 두 번째 절을 강조하는 기능과 맞지 않는다. D는 경계 부호 없이 두 독립절을 이어 run-on 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("Because ... produce") make a complete sentence, and "economist Alan Manning has argued ..." is also an independent clause, so you need a strong boundary such as a semicolon between them. The conjunctive adverb "indeed" introduces the second clause, so it goes after the semicolon and is followed by a comma, which makes A correct. B joins two independent clauses with only commas, creating a comma splice. C puts the semicolon after "indeed," which attaches it to the first clause, but its job is to introduce and emphasize Manning's claim in the second clause. D has no boundary punctuation at all between the clauses, so it is a run-on.
g.design: The long dependent clause and the appositive-like definition earlier make it hard to see where the clause boundary falls. Students also have to decide whether "indeed" belongs to the clause before it or the one after it.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: economics and business — Cross-subsidization pricing internal transfer and profitable segment offsetting unprofitable service provision

g.passage: Postal systems in many countries rely on cross-subsidization, a pricing arrangement in which revenue from a profitable segment of a business covers the losses of an unprofitable one. Urban mail delivery, dense and inexpensive to provide on a per-letter basis, typically generates steady surpluses ______ those surpluses pay for delivery to remote rural addresses, where carrying a single letter may cost several times the uniform stamp price.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 긴 동격 수식어 뒤 주절 경계를 파악하고, 두 독립절 사이에 전환어구가 올 때 세미콜론이 필요함을 판단하게 했다. A·D는 전환어구 쉼표가 부분적으로 맞지만 절 경계 처리를 못 하고, C는 관계사로 그럴듯해 보이지만 뒤 절이 이미 완전하다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Urban mail delivery ... generates steady surpluses"와 빈칸 뒤 "those surpluses pay for ..."는 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절을 잇고 전환어구 in effect를 뒤 절 앞에 두려면 세미콜론과 쉼표가 필요하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 전환어구를 쉼표로만 감싸 두 독립절을 이어서 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C의 which는 관계절을 만들지만 뒤에 이미 주어 those surpluses가 있어 문장 구조가 무너진다. D는 두 절 사이에 아무 경계 부호가 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("Urban mail delivery ... generates steady surpluses") and the text after it ("those surpluses pay for ...") are both independent clauses, each with its own subject and verb. To join them and put the transition "in effect" at the start of the second clause, you need a semicolon followed by a comma, so B is correct. A sets off the transition with commas only, so it joins two independent clauses with just a comma, which is a comma splice. C uses "which" to start a relative clause, but the words after it already have their own subject ("those surpluses"), so the sentence breaks down. D has no punctuation at all between the clauses, which makes it a run-on sentence.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: economics and business — Inventory pooling risk pooling centralization and demand variance reduction across distributed warehouse networks

g.passage: When a retailer replaces several regional warehouses with one central facility, the random swings in demand at each location tend to offset one another, a phenomenon operations researchers call risk pooling. The practical payoff, according to supply-chain analyst Maren Okafor, can be substantial. A firm that consolidates four warehouses, each previously holding its own buffer against unexpected orders, may need far less total safety ______ high demand in one region is often balanced by low demand in another.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 뒤 "unexpectedly high demand ... is often balanced"는 완전한 독립절이고, 의미상 재고가 덜 필요한 '이유'를 설명한다. C는 쉼표 뒤에 종속접속사 since를 써서 이유를 나타내는 종속절로 만들어 문법과 논리가 모두 맞다. A는 접속사 없이 두 독립절을 쉼표로만 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. B의 so는 문법적으로는 두 절을 이을 수 있지만 '그래서'라는 결과 관계를 만들어, 재고 감소의 원인을 결과처럼 뒤집는다. D는 unexpectedly를 앞 절에 붙여 "stock unexpectedly"라는 어색한 수식이 되고, 뒷절의 "high demand"에서 수식어가 떨어져 나가 의미가 왜곡된다.
g.explanation_en: The words after the blank, "unexpectedly high demand ... is often balanced by low demand in another," form a complete independent clause, and in context they explain why the firm needs less safety stock. Choice C uses a comma plus the subordinating conjunction "since," which turns that clause into a reason and links it correctly to the main clause. Choice A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, so it creates a comma splice. Choice B is grammatical, but "so" signals a result, which flips the logic: offsetting demand is the cause of needing less stock, not a result of it. Choice D attaches "unexpectedly" to the first clause, producing the odd phrase "need far less total safety stock unexpectedly" and separating the modifier from "high demand," so the meaning is distorted.
g.design: There are two steps: first spot the independent clause hidden after the long modifier, then pick the connector whose logic fits the context. B is grammatically fine but gets the logic wrong, and A looks natural if you only skim, so you have to compare the choices to rule them out.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: economics and business — Signaling wage education credential and productivity sorting in asymmetric information job market screening

g.passage: In his 1973 model of job-market signaling, economist Michael Spence argued that a college degree can be valuable to employers even if coursework adds nothing to a worker's skills. Because employers cannot directly observe productivity before hiring, they rely on credentials that are costlier for less able applicants to ______ the degree sorts candidates simply because only those who expect to finish it with relative ease find it worth pursuing.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Because employers ... to obtain"은 독립절(they rely ...)을 포함한 완전한 문장이고, 뒤 "the degree sorts candidates ..."도 독립절이므로 두 절 사이에 강한 경계가 필요하다. D는 세미콜론으로 절을 나누고 삽입구 "in this view"를 뒤 절 앞에 쉼표로 붙여 정답이다. A는 삽입구를 쉼표 두 개로 감싸서 맞아 보이지만 결국 두 독립절이 쉼표로만 이어진 comma splice이다. B와 C도 쉼표만 쓰거나 아예 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 이어 붙여 각각 comma splice와 run-on이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "Because employers ... to obtain," is a complete sentence because it contains the main clause "they rely ...," and "the degree sorts candidates ..." after the blank is also an independent clause. That means you need a strong boundary between them. D works because the semicolon separates the two clauses and the comma after "in this view" sets off the introductory phrase of the second clause. A looks right because it puts commas around "in this view," but the two independent clauses are still joined only by commas, which is a comma splice. B and C also connect the clauses with just a comma or with no punctuation at all, so they create a comma splice and a run-on, respectively.
g.design: The adverbial phrase "in this view" can look like it belongs to either clause, so a student who just checks that the phrase is set off by commas will pick A. To get it right, you have to notice that the clause boundary needs a semicolon. All four options follow the same pattern.

c.instruction:

c.seed: economics and business — Defect rate quality control variation reduction and production process standardization in manufacturing quality assurance

g.passage: In the 1920s, physicist Walter Shewhart drew a distinction that still shapes quality assurance in manufacturing. Some variation in a production process, he argued, arises from countless small, unavoidable fluctuations, the kind no worker can trace to a single source______ other variation stems from identifiable problems, such as a worn cutting tool or a miscalibrated gauge, and can therefore be eliminated to reduce defect rates.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 빈칸 앞에 동격 수식어(the kind ... source)가 있어 절 경계를 놓치기 쉽게 했고, 세미콜론+접속부사 뒤 쉼표까지 두 단계 판단을 요구한다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Some variation ... arises ... source"와 빈칸 뒤 "other variation stems ..."는 각각 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 이어야 하고, 접속부사 "by contrast"는 뒤에 쉼표를 붙여 다음 절과 구분하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 세미콜론은 맞지만 접속부사 뒤에 필요한 쉼표가 빠졌다. D는 첫 절과 둘째 절 사이에 아무 문장부호도 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("Some variation ... arises ... single source") and the text after it ("other variation stems ...") are both independent clauses. Two independent clauses can be joined with a semicolon, and the transitional phrase "by contrast" needs a comma after it to set it off from the clause that follows, so A is correct. B links the two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C uses the semicolon correctly but leaves out the comma needed after the transitional phrase. D puts no punctuation at all between the two clauses, which makes a run-on sentence.

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 빈칸 앞에 긴 관계절이 이어져 절 경계가 흐려지게 했고, 접속부사 'in contrast'를 쉼표로만 감싼 선택지가 그럴듯해 보이게 했다. 두 개의 독립절이 있는지 확인하고, 접속부사는 절을 잇지 못한다는 규칙까지 적용해야 풀 수 있다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 'Affiliate marketing reverses ... result'는 완전한 독립절이고, 뒤의 'an affiliate ... earns nothing ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 접속부사 'in contrast'는 두 절을 이어 줄 수 없으므로 앞에 세미콜론이 있어야 하고, 뒤에는 쉼표를 둔다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 접속부사를 쉼표로만 감싸서 쉼표 접합 오류가 생기고, C도 쉼표 접합인 데다 'in contrast' 뒤에 쉼표까지 빠졌다. D는 두 독립절을 아무 문장부호 없이 붙여 쓴 무종지문이다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank, "Affiliate marketing reverses ... result," form a complete independent clause, and the words after it, "an affiliate ... earns nothing ...," form another one with its own subject and verb. "In contrast" is a conjunctive adverb, so it can't join two clauses by itself: it needs a semicolon in front and a comma after. That makes B the correct answer. A puts commas around the adverb, which still creates a comma splice. C is also a comma splice, and it leaves out the comma after "in contrast." D runs the two independent clauses together with no punctuation at all.

g.passage: Tardigrades, tiny animals often called "water bears," can survive conditions that would kill most living things. When their surroundings dry out, they curl into a ball, lose nearly all the water in their bodies, and enter a state called anhydrobiosis, in which their metabolism almost stops. __Without water, however, the proteins inside an animal's cells usually lose their shape and stop working.__ Researchers have found that tardigrades solve this problem by producing special proteins that form a glass-like gel around other cell parts, holding them in place until water returns. Thanks to this protection, a dried tardigrade can revive and move again within hours of being rehydrated.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes a result of the research that the text goes on to question.
It offers an example of how tardigrades behave when their surroundings dry out.
It presents a difficulty that the text then explains how tardigrades overcome.
It gives a reason why scientists first became interested in studying tardigrades.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 물이 없으면 단백질이 형태를 잃고 기능을 멈춘다는 어려움을 제시하고, 바로 다음 문장이 "this problem"을 언급하며 완보동물이 특수 단백질로 이를 해결하는 방식을 설명하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 오답인데, 밑줄 문장은 연구 결과가 아니며 지문은 아무것도 반박하지 않는다. B는 오답인데, 몸을 마는 행동은 앞 문장에 나오고 밑줄 문장은 세포 일반의 문제를 다룬다. D는 오답인데, 과학자들이 처음 관심을 갖게 된 계기는 지문에 나오지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence points out a problem: without water, proteins in cells usually lose their shape and stop working. The very next sentence calls this "this problem" and explains how tardigrades solve it with special gel-forming proteins, so C is correct. A is wrong because the sentence isn't a research result, and the text never questions anything. B is wrong because the curling behavior comes in the sentence before; the underlined sentence describes a general problem for cells, not something tardigrades do. D is wrong because the text never says why scientists first started studying tardigrades.
g.design: "however"와 다음 문장의 "this problem"이 직접 단서여서 문제-해결 구조 하나만 알아보면 풀린다. 오답은 모두 "It + 동사 + 명사구" 틀로 맞췄고, 각각 반박, 예시, 동기를 내세운 그럴듯한 오개념이다.

When a lamprey finds a larger fish, it presses this disc against the host's side and holds on tightly. __Once attached, the lamprey releases saliva containing chemicals that stop the host's blood from clotting.__ Because the wound stays open, the lamprey can keep feeding on blood and body fluids for days before letting go.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

It presents a claim about lamprey saliva that the following sentence goes on to question.
It explains why a lamprey must choose a host larger than itself.
It describes a step in the feeding process that accounts for the result mentioned in the next sentence.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 숙주의 피가 굳지 않게 하는 침을 분비한다는 섭식 과정의 한 단계를 설명하고, 다음 문장은 'Because the wound stays open'으로 그 결과(며칠간 섭식)를 제시하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 다른 무턱 어류와의 비교가 지문에 없으므로 틀렸다. B는 다음 문장이 밑줄 내용을 의심하는 것이 아니라 그 결과를 이어서 말하므로 틀렸다. C는 숙주가 더 커야 하는 이유는 밑줄 문장에서 설명되지 않으므로 틀렸다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence describes one step in feeding: the lamprey releases saliva that keeps the host's blood from clotting. The next sentence begins "Because the wound stays open," showing the result of that step, so D is correct. A is wrong because the text never compares lampreys with other jawless fish. B is wrong because the next sentence builds on the sentence instead of questioning it. C is wrong because the underlined sentence says nothing about why the host must be larger.

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'Because pikas ... between peaks'와 뒤 'as a result, each mountaintop population ... rise'는 각각 독립절이므로, 둘 사이에는 세미콜론 같은 강한 경계가 필요하다. A는 세미콜론으로 두 독립절을 바르게 연결한다. B는 쉼표만으로 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 'and' 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표가 들어가고, 'as a result' 앞의 구두점도 어색하게 만들어 표준 영어 규칙에 맞지 않는다.

Choice C has no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. Choice D puts an unnecessary comma after "and" and leaves awkward punctuation before "as a result," so it doesn't follow standard conventions.
g.design: Two clearly visible independent clauses separated by a transitional phrase; tests only the semicolon-vs-comma-splice rule with typical distractors.

- 세부 기술 힌트: 긴 수식어구/도치 뒤의 주어-동사 일치, 병렬 구조, 수식어 위치(dangling modifier), 정동사 vs 분사/부정사 선택처럼 구조 파악이 필요한 문제.
c.seed: life science — Naked mole rat eusocial colony structure reproductive suppression and painless tactile discrimination adaptation

g.passage: In a naked mole rat colony, which can contain more than two hundred individuals, only a single queen and one to three males breed. The other members, though physically capable of reproducing, ______ in a suppressed state for years, a condition that researchers once attributed to hormonal cues in the queen's urine but now link more strongly to stress from her frequent shoving.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "The other members"이고, 삽입된 양보 수식어구 "though physically capable of reproducing" 뒤에는 정동사가 와야 한다. D의 "remain"은 복수 주어와 수가 일치하는 현재형 정동사이며, 첫 문장의 현재 시제("contain," "breed")와도 맞는다. A의 "remaining"은 분사라서 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다. B의 "to remain"은 부정사이고 C의 "having remained"는 완료 분사로, 둘 다 정동사 역할을 할 수 없다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "The other members," and after the inserted concessive phrase "though physically capable of reproducing," the sentence still needs a main verb. D, "remain," is a finite present-tense verb that agrees with the plural subject and fits the present tense of the first sentence ("contain," "breed"). A, "remaining," is a participle, so it would leave the sentence with no main verb. B, "to remain," is an infinitive, and C, "having remained," is a perfect participle, so neither one can act as the main verb.
g.design: 삽입된 양보 수식어구가 주어와 동사 사이를 끊어 놓아서 정동사가 빠졌다는 사실을 알아차리기 어렵다. 분사와 부정사 오답은 수식어구를 이어 가는 것처럼 보이기 때문에 그럴듯하게 느껴진다.

c.seed: life science — Chickadee winter energy conservation torpor-like state hypothermia tolerance and survival in freezing conditions

g.passage: To get through winter nights that often fall well below freezing, black-capped chickadees rely on more than their dense feathers. Studies of wild birds in Alaska show that these songbirds, each of which weighs only about eleven grams and stores barely enough fat to last a single long night, ______ their body temperature by as much as 10°C after dark, entering a controlled hypothermic state that sharply cuts the energy they burn before dawn.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸은 that절의 주어 'these songbirds' 뒤에 나오는 정동사 자리이며, 그 사이의 관계절(each of which ... night)은 삽입 수식어일 뿐이다. 주어가 복수이므로 복수 정동사 A가 맞다. B는 정동사 형태지만 관계절 속 'each'나 'a single long night'에 맞춘 단수형이라 주어와 일치하지 않는다. C와 D는 분사 형태라 that절에 정동사가 없어 절이 완성되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The blank is the main verb of the that-clause, whose subject is "these songbirds"; the relative clause "each of which ... night" is just an interrupting modifier. Since the subject is plural, it needs the plural finite verb in A. B is a finite verb, but it's singular, so it agrees with "each" or "a single long night" inside the modifier, not with the real subject. C and D are participles, which would leave the that-clause without a main verb.
g.design: I put a long relative clause containing singular nouns ("each," "night") between the plural subject and the blank. That way students have to find the real subject and also see that the clause needs a finite verb.

c.seed: life science — Cuckoo bumblebee social parasitism host colony infiltration and reproductive usurpation behavior in bumble bee nests

g.passage: Cuckoo bumblebees, members of the subgenus Psithyrus, have no worker caste and cannot collect pollen for their own young. Instead, a female enters the nest of a host bumblebee species in spring, after the host queen has already produced her first workers. It was long assumed that the intruder simply overpowers the colony by force, since she has a thicker exoskeleton and a stronger sting than the host. Yet field observations by entomologists show that many invaders spend hours or even days hiding in the nest debris before acting, gradually acquiring the colony's scent. Once chemically disguised, the cuckoo female often kills or subdues the host queen and then lays her own eggs, which the host workers rear as if they were their own sisters. The intruder also suppresses egg laying by the workers, ensuring that the colony's labor goes almost entirely to raising her offspring.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Cuckoo bumblebees succeed in host nests mainly because their thick exoskeletons and strong stings let them defeat the host queen quickly.
Rather than relying on strength alone, cuckoo bumblebees often take over host colonies through a gradual chemical disguise that lets them redirect the workers' labor to their own brood.
Cuckoo bumblebees invade host nests in spring because host workers are too young at that time to recognize unfamiliar scents.
Host bumblebee workers eventually detect cuckoo females but continue to rear their eggs because the workers are unable to lay eggs of their own.
g.explanation: 지문은 침입자가 힘으로 군락을 제압한다는 기존 가정을 소개한 뒤, 실제로는 숨어서 군락의 냄새를 서서히 얻고 이후 숙주의 일벌 노동을 자기 새끼 양육에 돌린다는 점을 보여 주므로 B가 정답이다. A는 지문이 반박하는 기존 가정을 그대로 결론으로 제시한다. C는 봄에 침입한다는 세부 내용은 맞지만, 일벌이 어려서 냄새를 알아보지 못한다는 이유는 지문에 없다. D는 일벌이 침입자를 알아챈다고 하고 일벌이 알을 낳지 못한다고 하는데, 지문에서는 일벌이 자매처럼 여겨 키우며 침입자가 일벌의 산란을 억제한다고 했으므로 틀리다.
g.explanation_en: The text brings up the old belief that invaders win by force. It then shows that many of them actually hide, slowly pick up the colony's scent, and then get the host workers to raise their brood, so B is correct. A repeats the old assumption that the text argues against. C gets the spring timing right, but the text never says young workers can't recognize scents. D says the workers notice the intruder and can't lay eggs. In the text, though, the workers raise the eggs as if they were their sisters, and the intruder has to stop the workers from laying, which means they are able to lay eggs.
g.design: 오답 A와 C는 지문의 세부 내용(외골격·침, 봄 침입)에 기대도록 만들어서, 기존 가정이 반박되는 흐름과 연결해 읽어야만 배제되게 했다.

c.seed: life science — Tidepool sculpin homing behavior territorial fidelity chemical gradient detection and sensory navigation in tide pools

g.passage: Tidepool sculpins (Oligocottus maculosus) are small fish that spend low tide confined to rocky pools along the Pacific coast of North America. When researchers move a sculpin to a pool tens of meters away, it often returns to its original pool within a few tides, even across stretches of unfamiliar shoreline. Early investigators assumed the fish relied mainly on vision, memorizing the shapes of nearby rocks. That explanation, however, could not account for later experiments: sculpins whose eyes were covered still homed successfully, while those whose olfactory organs were blocked wandered at random. Further work showed that each pool carries a slightly distinct chemical signature, shaped by its resident algae and invertebrates, and that sculpins can distinguish water from their home pool from water drawn from neighboring pools. The researchers concluded that as the incoming tide connects the pools, the fish follow faint chemical traces back toward familiar water, using visual cues only once they are close.
g.question: According to the text, what did researchers conclude about how tidepool sculpins find their way back after being displaced?
options: The sculpins rely chiefly on memorized rock shapes, using chemical cues only when visibility is poor during high tide.
The sculpins return to whichever pool contains the most algae and invertebrates, regardless of where they lived before.
The sculpins track chemical traces of their home pool's water during high tide, turning to sight mainly at the end of the trip.
The sculpins wander at random until tidal currents happen to carry them close enough to recognize their home pool by sight.
g.explanation: 지문 마지막 문장은 밀물로 웅덩이가 연결될 때 물고기가 희미한 화학적 흔적을 따라 익숙한 물로 돌아가고, 가까워지면 시각 단서를 쓴다고 결론짓므로 C가 정답이다. A는 초기 연구자들의 가설(시각 중심)을 결론으로 착각한 것으로, 주된 수단과 보조 수단을 뒤바꿨다. B는 조류·무척추동물이 화학적 특징을 만든다는 세부를 왜곡해 '가장 많은' 웅덩이로 간다고 했으나, 지문은 고유한 집 웅덩이를 구별한다고 한다. D는 후각이 차단된 개체가 무작위로 헤맸다는 내용을 정상 개체의 행동으로 잘못 적용했다.
g.explanation_en: The last sentence says that when the rising tide connects the pools, the fish follow faint chemical traces back to familiar water and use visual cues only once they're close, so C is correct. A takes the early investigators' vision-based idea and treats it as the conclusion, flipping which cue is primary and which is backup. B twists the detail that algae and invertebrates shape each pool's chemical signature: the fish recognize their own home pool, not whichever pool has the most life. D takes the random wandering seen only in fish whose sense of smell was blocked and wrongly applies it to normal fish.
g.design: To answer, you have to connect the rejected early hypothesis, the experimental results, and the final conclusion. Each wrong choice misapplies a real detail from the text: the old hypothesis, the source of the chemical signature, or the result for fish with blocked smell.

c.seed: life science — Mimic octopus rapid morphological change and behavioral mimicry of multiple species predator avoidance strategy

g.passage: The mimic octopus (Thaumoctopus mimicus), found in the shallow, sandy waters of Indonesia, is known for imitating a range of other animals. By flattening its body and arms and swimming close to the seafloor, it can resemble a toxic flatfish; by burying six arms and waving the remaining two in opposite directions, it can look like a venomous sea snake. Early observers assumed the octopus simply shifted among these disguises at random. Researchers who have filmed the animal over many hours, however, report a different pattern: the octopus seems to choose its imitation based on the threat it faces. When damselfish harass it, for example, it often takes on the sea snake form, an animal that hunts damselfish. Because open sand offers few places to hide, this ability to match a disguise to a particular attacker may be what allows the octopus to forage in daylight.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The mimic octopus can resemble both a flatfish and a sea snake, which makes it more versatile than any other octopus species living in Indonesian waters.
The mimic octopus switches among its disguises at random, an approach that keeps damselfish and other attackers from learning to recognize it.
The mimic octopus forages mainly in daylight because open sand offers it few hiding places, so it must stay in plain sight of predators.
The mimic octopus appears to pick a disguise suited to the specific threat it meets, a skill that may help it survive while feeding in exposed habitats.
g.explanation: 지문의 중심은 초기의 '무작위 변신' 가정과 달리 문어가 위협에 맞춰 흉내 대상을 고르는 것으로 보이며, 이 능력 덕분에 숨을 곳 없는 모래밭에서 낮에 먹이를 찾을 수 있다는 점이다. D는 두 가지를 모두 담고 있어 정답이다. A는 흉내 대상이 여러 개라는 세부 정보는 맞지만, 다른 문어와의 비교는 지문에 없다. B는 연구자들이 반박한 초기 관찰자의 가정을 그대로 가져온 것이다. C는 모래밭과 낮 시간이라는 세부 정보는 맞지만, 인과관계가 뒤집혀 있고 맞춤형 위장이라는 핵심 내용이 빠져 있다.
g.explanation_en: The text's main point is that the mimic octopus does not switch disguises at random, as early observers thought. Instead, it seems to choose a disguise based on the threat it faces, and this ability may be what lets it forage in daylight on open sand. Choice D captures both of these ideas, so it is the answer. Choice A gets one detail right, since the octopus does imitate several animals, but the text never compares it with other octopus species. Choice B repeats the early assumption that the researchers rejected. Choice C uses real details about sand and daylight, but it flips the cause-and-effect relationship and leaves out the key idea of matching a disguise to a threat.
g.design: 이 문항은 가정이 반박되는 구조를 활용해, 초기 가정을 그대로 담은 B로 대충 훑어 읽는 학생을 유도한다. A와 C는 지문의 세부 정보는 맞지만 근거 없는 비교를 하거나 인과관계를 뒤집은 오답이다. 네 선택지 모두 "The mimic octopus..."로 시작하는 같은 문장 틀로 썼다.

c.seed: life science — Mantis shrimp triadic color vision photoreceptor types and complex light polarization perception visual system

g.passage: Mantis shrimp are often described as having the most sophisticated eyes in the animal kingdom: whereas humans rely on three types of color photoreceptors, some mantis shrimp species possess twelve. For years, researchers assumed that this abundance must allow the animals to distinguish between colors with extraordinary precision. However, when biologist Hanne Thoen and colleagues trained mantis shrimp to choose between pairs of closely matched colors, the animals performed worse than many species with far fewer receptor types, often failing to tell apart hues that humans separate easily. The researchers proposed that mantis shrimp do not compare signals across receptors, as human brains do, but instead recognize colors directly by which receptor fires, a system that sacrifices fine discrimination for speed. Notably, the same eyes also detect circularly polarized light, a capacity that appears to serve signaling between individuals rather than precise color judgment.
g.question: According to the text, what did the trained-choice experiments suggest about mantis shrimp?
options: Their many receptor types appear to support rapid identification of hues rather than fine distinctions between similar ones.
Their many receptor types appear to support fine distinctions between similar hues rather than rapid identification of them.
Their many receptor types appear to support detection of polarized light rather than identification of hues.
Their many receptor types appear to support comparison of signals across receptors in the way human brains do.
g.design: 실험 결과(구별 실패)와 연구자 해석(속도 위해 정밀성 희생)을 연결해야 정답 도출; 오답은 통념, 편광 세부, 인간 방식 비교를 같은 문장 틀로 배치.
g.explanation: 실험에서 갯가재는 비슷한 색을 잘 구별하지 못했고, 연구자들은 어떤 수용체가 반응하는지로 색을 직접 인식하며 정밀성 대신 속도를 택한 체계라고 제안했으므로 A가 정답이다. B는 연구 이전의 통념을 뒤집지 않고 그대로 반복한 것으로, 실험 결과와 반대된다. C는 지문에 나온 편광 감지를 끌어오지만, 편광은 같은 눈의 별도 능력으로 언급될 뿐 실험이 수용체의 용도를 편광으로 바꿔 놓았다는 내용은 없다. D는 연구자들이 갯가재는 인간처럼 수용체 간 신호를 비교하지 않는다고 말한 내용과 정면으로 어긋난다.
g.explanation_en: The answer is A. In the experiments, mantis shrimp had trouble telling closely matched colors apart, and the researchers proposed that the animals recognize a color directly by which receptor fires, giving up fine discrimination in exchange for speed. B simply restates the assumption researchers held before the study, which is the opposite of what the experiments found. C borrows the passage's mention of polarized light, but polarization is described as a separate ability of the same eyes, not something the experiments showed the receptors are used for instead of identifying hues. D contradicts the researchers' claim that mantis shrimp do not compare signals across receptors the way human brains do.

c.seed: life science — Pacific chorus frog explosive breeding temporal synchronization and acoustic communication in seasonal breeding aggregation

g.passage: Pacific chorus frogs (Pseudacris regilla) are often described as explosive breeders: after the first warm rains of late winter, hundreds of males converge on a single pond within a few nights and begin calling. Because so many males arrive at once, biologist Kim Hollis expected that a female choosing a mate would be able to compare dozens of callers and favor those with the longest or fastest calls. ______ when Hollis recorded choruses at ponds in Oregon, she found that females rarely sampled more than two or three males before pairing, typically approaching whichever caller was nearest and calling most loudly at that moment.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 수컷이 많으므로 암컷이 여러 수컷을 비교할 것이라는 Hollis의 '예상'을 제시하고, 뒤 문장은 암컷이 두세 마리만 살피고 가까운 수컷을 택했다는 상반된 관찰 결과를 제시하므로 대조의 B가 정답이다. A는 수컷이 한꺼번에 몰린다는 원인과 이어지는 결과처럼 보이지만, 뒤 내용은 예상에서 도출된 결과가 아니라 예상을 뒤집는 내용이다. C는 둘 다 짝 선택 행동을 다룬다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 두 내용은 비슷한 것이 아니라 서로 충돌한다. D는 뒤 문장이 구체적인 현장 관찰이라 예시처럼 보이지만, 앞 예상을 뒷받침하는 예가 아니라 반박한다.
g.explanation_en: The previous sentence gives Hollis's expectation: since so many males show up, females should compare many callers. The next sentence reports a finding that contradicts it, since females checked only two or three males and picked the nearest, loudest one. That calls for contrast, so B is correct. A may look right because the mass arrival seems to lead to an outcome, but the finding overturns the expectation instead of following from it. C sounds possible because both sentences are about choosing a mate, but the two ideas clash rather than match. D might fit because the second sentence describes a specific field observation, but that observation argues against the expectation instead of giving an example of it.
g.design: There is no word like "but" or "surprisingly" to signal the contrast. The student has to see that "expected" sets up a prediction and that the data go against it. Each wrong answer is partly supported by something in the passage: cause and effect (A), the shared topic (C), and a concrete observation (D).

c.seed: life science — Daphnia predator defense morphological plasticity and spine enlargement induced by chemical cues from predators

g.passage: When water fleas of the genus Daphnia detect kairomones—chemicals released by predatory midge larvae—many develop enlarged tail spines and helmet-like crests that make them harder to grasp and swallow. These defenses are not free, however: in laboratory trials, spined individuals often matured later and produced smaller broods than undefended siblings raised in predator-free water. ______ a population that grew spines permanently, regardless of whether predators were present, would pay that reproductive cost even in seasons when the defense offered no protection, which may explain why Daphnia build spines only after sensing the chemical cue.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 가시 방어에 번식 비용이 따른다는 사실을 제시하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 비용 때문에 가시를 항상 기르는 개체군은 불필요한 손해를 본다는 결론을 끌어낸다. 따라서 결과·추론을 나타내는 C가 정답이다. A는 'however' 뒤에 오는 반전을 한 번 더 뒤집는 셈인데, 뒤 문장은 비용을 반박하지 않고 오히려 그 비용을 근거로 삼는다. B는 뒤 문장이 실제 실험 사례처럼 보일 수 있지만, 실제로는 가상의 개체군을 놓고 펼친 추론이다. D는 상시 가시와 유도 가시를 비교하는 것처럼 보이지만, 그 대비는 문장 안에서 이루어질 뿐 앞 문장과의 관계는 대조가 아니라 귀결이다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank tells you that spine defenses come with a reproductive cost. The sentence after the blank uses that cost to draw a conclusion: a population that always grew spines would pay the cost even when the spines did nothing for it. That is a cause-to-consequence link, so C is correct. A doesn't work because "Nevertheless" would set up a reversal, but the next sentence builds on the cost instead of pushing against it. B can look right because the sentence describes a population, but it's a hypothetical line of reasoning, not an example of an observed result. D can look right because the sentence compares permanent spines with spines grown in response to a cue, but that comparison happens inside the sentence itself; its relationship to the sentence before it is a consequence, not a contrast.
g.design: There is no word in the passage that signals cause and effect, so you have to see that the cost becomes the reason for the hypothetical conclusion. B and D each match part of the sentence, since it mentions a population and compares two strategies.

c.seed: life science — Bladderwort carnivorous trap mechanism and suction-based prey capture kinetics in aquatic insect-eating plants

g.passage: Bladderworts are rootless aquatic plants that capture tiny prey with hundreds of hollow underwater bladders. Each bladder slowly pumps water out through its walls, creating low internal pressure, and then waits with its trapdoor sealed shut. When a water flea brushes against trigger hairs near the door, the door buckles inward and water rushes in, carrying the prey with it. Researchers long assumed that the hairs worked like a mechanical lever that pried the door open. __High-speed filming by physicist Olivier Vincent and colleagues, however, showed that a bladder sometimes fires with no contact at all, once its internal pressure drops past a critical point.__ This finding suggests that the door is held near a point of instability, so the trigger hairs merely provide a tiny final push rather than doing the work of opening it.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes the process by which a bladder lowers its internal pressure before any prey comes near.
It presents evidence that trigger hairs play no role at all in the way bladderworts capture prey.
It explains why researchers first believed that the trigger hairs acted as a mechanical lever.
It reports an observation that challenges an earlier assumption and sets up a revised interpretation.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 접촉 없이도 덫이 작동한다는 촬영 결과를 보고하여, 털이 지렛대 역할을 한다는 기존 가정에 의문을 제기하고, 마지막 문장의 수정된 해석(문이 불안정점 근처에 있고 털은 마지막 작은 자극만 준다)을 이끈다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 압력이 언급되긴 하지만 압력을 낮추는 과정은 앞 문장에서 설명되며, 밑줄 문장의 역할은 아니다. B는 지나치다. 지문은 털이 '작은 마지막 자극'을 준다고 하므로 역할이 전혀 없다는 뜻이 아니다. C는 기존 가정을 언급하지만, 밑줄 문장은 그 가정이 생긴 이유를 설명하는 것이 아니라 반박한다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence reports filming that showed bladders can fire without any contact. This calls into question the old belief that the hairs work as a lever, and it leads into the final sentence's new interpretation: the door sits near instability, and the hairs only give a small final push. That makes D correct. A mentions pressure, but the earlier sentence is the one that describes how the pressure gets lowered, so that isn't the underlined sentence's role. B goes too far, because the text says the hairs still supply a tiny push, so they do play some role. C mentions the earlier belief, but the underlined sentence challenges that belief instead of explaining why people held it.
g.design: 오답 A·C는 지문의 압력·기존 가정 요소를 부분적으로 담아 비교가 필요하고, B는 과잉 일반화로 그럴듯하게 만들었다. 정답은 '도전 후 재해석'이라는 기능을 추론해야 한다.

c.seed: life science — Bristlecone pine extreme longevity growth ring formation and radial density variation in sub-arctic tree aging

g.passage: Great Basin bristlecone pines, some of which have lived for more than 4,800 years, are often assumed to survive so long because they grow steadily, adding a thin but uniform ring each year. Dendrochronologist Matthew Salzer and colleagues found a more uneven pattern. In the oldest trees, much of the trunk dies back over centuries, leaving only a narrow strip of living bark that feeds a few surviving branches. __Along that strip, rings in cold years can be less than a tenth of a millimeter wide, and in some years no ring forms at all, yet the wood that is laid down is unusually dense and resin-rich.__ This dense wood resists rot and insect attack, so the tree's slow, irregular growth may not be a sign of decline but part of what lets it endure.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It gives specific details about the trees' growth that set up the text's explanation of how that growth helps the trees survive.
It gives a reason why researchers had trouble counting the rings of the oldest bristlecone pines and so misjudged their ages.
It gives evidence supporting the common belief that bristlecone pines add a thin but uniform ring every year.
It gives an example of the decline that the text says will eventually kill even the oldest bristlecone pines.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 추운 해에 나이테가 극히 얇거나 아예 생기지 않지만 목재는 치밀하고 수지가 많다는 구체적 세부 사항을 제시하고, 다음 문장은 이 치밀한 목재가 부패와 해충을 막아 생존을 돕는다고 설명한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 나이테가 빠지는 현상이 연대 측정을 어렵게 할 수 있다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 지문은 나이를 잘못 추정했다는 내용을 다루지 않는다. C는 '얇은 나이테'라는 점은 맞지만, 밑줄 문장은 '균일한' 성장이라는 통념을 오히려 반박한다. D는 느린 성장을 쇠퇴로 보지만, 지문 마지막 문장은 그것이 쇠퇴의 징후가 아닐 수 있다고 말한다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence gives specific details: in cold years, rings are extremely thin or don't form at all, but the wood that does form is dense and resin-rich. The next sentence then explains that this dense wood resists rot and insects, which helps the tree survive. That makes A correct. B is tempting because missing rings could make dating harder, but the text never says anyone misjudged the trees' ages. C picks up on the "thin" rings, but the sentence actually contradicts the belief that growth is uniform. D treats the slow growth as decline, while the final sentence suggests it may not be a sign of decline at all.
g.design: 오답 B(나이테 결손→연대 측정 문제)와 C(얇은 나이테→통념 지지)는 지문 일부에 근거해 그럴듯하게 만들었다. 정답을 고르려면 밑줄 문장이 통념을 반박한다는 점과 다음 문장의 생존 설명으로 이어진다는 점을 함께 연결해야 한다.

c.seed: life science — Mycorrhizal network fungal symbiosis and nutrient exchange between host plant roots and soil fungal partners

g.passage: Many plants trade carbon with soil fungi called arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi: the plant supplies sugars and lipids from photosynthesis, and the fungus delivers phosphorus gathered by its threadlike hyphae. Researchers have often described this exchange as a stable partnership in which both sides simply benefit. Work led by ecologist Toby Kiers complicates that picture. When Kiers's team gave roots access to several fungal strains, some of which hoarded phosphorus rather than passing it on, the roots sent more carbon to the strains that delivered more phosphorus. __The fungi, in turn, moved more phosphorus to roots that supplied more carbon, even shifting nutrients through their networks toward parts of the soil where phosphorus was scarce and could therefore fetch a better "price."__ Taken together, these findings suggest that the symbiosis is better understood as a market in which each partner rewards the other in proportion to what it receives.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that the fungi benefit from the exchange more than the host plants do, which weakens the view that the relationship is a partnership.
It shows that the behavior seen in the plants is also found in the fungi, which supports the conclusion stated in the final sentence.
It explains how the uncooperative strains managed to obtain carbon from roots, which accounts for the hoarding described earlier.
It describes a finding that conflicts with the root experiment, which makes the conclusion in the final sentence less certain.
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 식물이 인을 더 많이 주는 균주에게 탄소를 더 보낸다는 결과이고, 밑줄 문장은 균류도 탄소를 더 주는 뿌리에게 인을 더 보낸다는 결과를 보여 준다. 이렇게 양쪽 모두 보상한다는 점이 마지막 문장의 '시장' 결론을 뒷받침하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 균류가 더 많은 이익을 얻는다고 하지만, 지문은 어느 쪽이 더 이익을 보는지 비교하지 않는다. C는 비협조적 균주의 행동을 설명한다고 하지만, 밑줄 문장은 그런 균주가 탄소를 얻는 방법을 다루지 않는다. D는 앞 실험과 충돌한다고 하지만, 밑줄 문장은 앞 실험과 같은 방향의 결과로 결론을 강화한다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before it shows that roots send more carbon to fungal strains that deliver more phosphorus. The underlined sentence shows the same pattern from the fungi's side: they send more phosphorus to roots that supply more carbon. Because both partners reward each other, this supports the "market" conclusion in the final sentence, so B is correct. A is wrong because the text never compares which partner benefits more. C is wrong because the sentence doesn't explain how hoarding strains get carbon. D is wrong because the finding agrees with the root experiment and makes the conclusion stronger, not weaker.
g.design: To answer, students have to link the underlined sentence to the root finding before it (the same behavior seen from the other side) and then to the final conclusion. The wrong answers bring up nearby ideas (benefit, hoarding, the root experiment) but get the relationship wrong.

c.seed: life science — Hydrothermal vent chemosynthetic bacteria hydrogen sulfide oxidation and energy metabolism in deep-sea ecosystem foundation

g.passage: For decades, biologists assumed that every food web on Earth ultimately depended on sunlight captured by photosynthesis. The 1977 discovery of dense communities of tubeworms, clams, and shrimp clustered around hydrothermal vents on the Galápagos Rift challenged that view. Researchers soon found that the base of these communities consists of chemosynthetic bacteria, which oxidize hydrogen sulfide escaping from the vents and use the released energy to convert carbon dioxide into organic compounds. __Yet the oxygen these bacteria need to oxidize sulfide is itself a by-product of photosynthesis at the ocean's surface, carried to the depths by circulating seawater.__ Vent ecosystems, then, are better described not as fully independent of the Sun but as powered by a different chemical route that still relies, indirectly, on sunlit waters far above.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains the chemical process by which vent bacteria convert hydrogen sulfide into organic compounds.
It presents evidence that overturns the 1977 finding that vent communities rely on chemosynthetic bacteria.
It introduces a qualification that limits how far the vent discovery departs from the earlier assumption about sunlight.
It describes a factor that explains why vent communities are densely clustered rather than widely dispersed.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해 박테리아에 필요한 산소가 결국 표층 광합성에서 온다고 지적하며, 열수구 생태계가 태양과 완전히 무관하다는 해석을 제한한다. 마지막 문장이 이를 '간접적으로 의존한다'고 정리하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 산화 과정 자체가 앞 문장에서 이미 설명되었고 밑줄 문장은 산소의 출처를 말할 뿐이다. B는 박테리아가 기반이라는 발견을 뒤집는 것이 아니라 그 의미를 한정하는 것이므로 틀리다. D는 군집이 밀집한 이유는 지문에서 다뤄지지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet" and points out that the oxygen the bacteria use comes from surface photosynthesis, which limits the claim that vent ecosystems are totally independent of the Sun. The final sentence confirms this by calling the reliance "indirect," so C is correct. A is wrong because the previous sentence already describes the oxidation process; the underlined sentence only identifies where the oxygen comes from. B is wrong because the sentence doesn't reject the finding that bacteria form the base of the food web; it narrows what that finding means. D is wrong because the text never explains why the communities cluster densely.
g.design: To answer, students have to link the "Yet" turn to both the opening assumption and the final conclusion. A and B are tempting because they mention real content from the passage (the oxidation process and the 1977 finding).

c.seed: life science — Giant water lily floating leaf structure and vascular support system in large aquatic plant buoyancy mechanics

g.passage: The floating leaves of the giant water lily Victoria amazonica can grow wider than two meters, yet each one supports its own weight on the water's surface without sinking or tearing. Botanists long assumed that the leaf's size was possible simply because water carries most of the load. __Studies of the leaf's underside, however, revealed a dense lattice of thick, air-filled ribs radiating from the center and linked by cross-veins, a pattern that spreads weight across the whole surface much as girders do in a bridge deck.__ Because the trapped air also adds buoyancy, the ribs let the plant build a huge leaf from a remarkably thin and light sheet of tissue, an efficiency that reportedly inspired the iron framework of a nineteenth-century glasshouse.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It gives evidence that supports the botanists' assumption that water alone carries the weight of the leaf.
It describes an engineering design that the text later shows was copied from the leaf.
It points out a weakness in the leaf's structure that limits how large the leaf can become.
It brings up a structural feature that complicates an earlier explanation and is then explored further.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'however'로 시작해, 물이 무게를 대부분 떠받친다는 기존 가정만으로는 설명이 부족함을 보여 주는 잎맥 격자 구조를 소개하고, 다음 문장이 그 구조의 부력과 효율을 더 설명하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 이 문장이 가정을 뒷받침한다고 하지만 실제로는 가정을 보완·수정한다. B는 다리 비유와 온실 언급에 끌린 오답으로, 밑줄 문장이 묘사하는 것은 공학 설계가 아니라 잎의 구조이며 모방된 쪽은 온실이다. C는 구조를 약점으로 보지만 지문은 이 구조를 큰 잎을 가능하게 하는 강점으로 제시한다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence opens with "however" and introduces the rib lattice, which shows that the botanists' assumption that water does most of the work is incomplete; the next sentence then explains how the ribs add buoyancy and efficiency, so D is correct. A is wrong because the sentence revises the assumption instead of supporting it. B is tempting because of the bridge comparison and the glasshouse mention, but the sentence describes the leaf's structure, not an engineering design, and it was the glasshouse that copied the leaf. C is wrong because the text presents the ribs as a strength that makes a huge leaf possible, not a weakness.
g.design: The answer requires connecting the "however" contrast with the earlier assumption and the follow-up sentence; distractors draw on the bridge/glasshouse details and the assumption itself.

g.passage: Emperor penguins routinely dive deeper than 400 meters in pursuit of fish and squid, staying submerged for well over ten minutes. Researchers long assumed that such dives were possible only because the birds sharply slow their heart rates, conserving oxygen much as diving seals do. Physiologist Paul Ponganis and colleagues tested this assumption by attaching heart-rate monitors to free-diving penguins in Antarctica. __The recordings showed that, during the descent and active chase phases of a dive, heart rates sometimes rose above resting levels rather than falling.__ The team concluded that penguins regulate their heart rates flexibly, slowing them during long glides but speeding them up when muscles need oxygen for pursuit, so that a fixed, dive-long slowdown cannot by itself explain their endurance.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents an observation that complicates a long-held view and leads to the researchers' revised account.
It presents an observation that confirms the long-held view that penguins conserve oxygen as seals do.
It presents an observation that explains why penguins are able to dive deeper than seals.
It presents an observation that the researchers dismiss as an error caused by their monitoring equipment.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 심박수가 떨어지지 않고 오히려 오르기도 했다는 관찰로, 펭귄이 심박수를 일관되게 늦춘다는 기존 가정에 들어맞지 않는다. 바로 다음 문장에서 연구진은 이를 토대로 심박수를 유연하게 조절한다는 수정된 결론을 내리므로 A가 정답이다. B는 지문에 나온 '물범처럼 산소 절약'이라는 가정을 언급하지만, 밑줄 문장은 그 가정을 확인하는 것이 아니라 반박한다. C는 잠수 지구력과 관련된 그럴듯한 내용이지만, 지문은 펭귄과 물범의 잠수 깊이를 비교하지 않는다. D는 연구진이 그 관찰을 받아들여 결론의 근거로 삼았다는 사실과 어긋난다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence reports that heart rates sometimes rose instead of falling, which doesn't fit the old assumption that penguins steadily slow their hearts. In the next sentence, the researchers use this finding to reach a revised conclusion about flexible regulation, so A is correct. B mentions the seal-like oxygen-saving view from the text, but the sentence challenges that view instead of confirming it. C sounds connected to dive endurance, but the text never compares how deep penguins and seals dive. D is wrong because the researchers accept the observation and build their conclusion on it.
g.design: B와 D는 지문에 나온 요소(기존 가정, 측정 장비)를 활용해 일부만 맞는 오답으로 만들었고, C는 그럴듯하지만 근거가 없는 오답이다. 정답을 고르려면 밑줄 문장을 앞의 가정, 뒤의 결론과 각각 연결해 읽어야 한다.

c.seed: life science — Zebra mussel invasive species planktonic veliger larvae and biofouling accumulation on industrial water infrastructure

g.passage: Zebra mussels spread through North American waterways largely because of their microscopic larvae. These free-swimming veligers, which drift in the current for several weeks before settling, are easily drawn into the intake pipes of power plants and water treatment facilities. Once inside, the larvae attach to any hard ______ within a few years, the accumulated shells can narrow a pipe's opening enough to sharply reduce the flow of water.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "the larvae attach ... and grow rapidly"는 완전한 독립절이고, 뒤의 "within a few years, the accumulated shells can narrow..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결해야 하므로 B가 정답이다. A와 D는 독립절 두 개를 쉼표만으로 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 두 절 사이에 아무 부호도 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 되고, 하나의 주어가 갖는 복합 동사 "attach ... and grow" 사이에 불필요한 쉼표까지 들어가 있다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank, "the larvae attach to any hard surface and grow rapidly," form a complete independent clause, and "within a few years, the accumulated shells can narrow..." is a second independent clause with its own subject and verb. Two independent clauses can be joined with a semicolon, so B is correct. A and D link the two clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between the clauses, which creates a run-on sentence, and it also adds an unneeded comma inside the compound verb "attach ... and grow."
g.design: "within a few years,"라는 도입 수식어 때문에 두 번째 독립절의 시작을 놓치기 쉽게 했다. 또 복합 동사 안의 쉼표를 오답 요소로 넣어, 수험생이 절의 경계와 복합 술어를 모두 판단해야 풀 수 있게 했다.

c.seed: life science — Sex change fish sequential hermaphroditism and social status-dependent reproductive transition in coral reef populations

g.passage: In a clownfish colony, all of whose members shelter among the stinging tentacles of a single sea anemone, only two fish breed: the largest individual, which is always female, mates with the second-largest fish, the colony's sole breeding male______ when the female dies, this male changes sex within weeks, and the next-largest fish in the colony grows rapidly to become the new breeding male.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 동격어구 "the colony's sole breeding male"로 끝나는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "when the female dies, this male changes sex..."도 독립절이므로 두 절을 세미콜론으로 연결한 C가 정답이다. A는 동격어구를 쉼표로 닫는 점은 맞지만 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 접속사 and를 넣어 절 연결은 해결하지만, 쉼표로 시작한 동격어구를 대시로 닫아 부호 짝이 맞지 않는다. D는 쉼표 없이 and만 써서 쉼표로 열린 동격어구가 닫히지 않으므로 "male and when..."이 하나로 읽힌다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank is an independent clause ending with the appositive "the colony's sole breeding male," and the text after it ("when the female dies, this male changes sex...") is also an independent clause, so a semicolon correctly joins them, which makes C the answer. A properly closes the appositive with a comma, but a comma alone can't join two independent clauses, so it creates a comma splice. B adds "and" to link the clauses, but the appositive opens with a comma and can't be closed with a dash, so the punctuation doesn't match. D uses "and" with no comma, which leaves the appositive opened by a comma unclosed, so "male and when..." runs together.
g.design: 빈칸 앞에 콜론 뒤 절과 동격어구가 길게 이어져 절 경계를 놓치기 쉽게 했다. A는 동격어구를 닫는 점이, B는 접속사로 절을 잇는 점이 부분적으로 맞아서 두 단계로 판단해야 배제된다.

c.seed: life science — Tomato ripening ethylene hormone biochemical cascade and tomato lycopene accumulation in fruit maturation physiology

g.passage: As a tomato matures, a surge of the gaseous hormone ethylene sets off a biochemical cascade inside the fruit. Enzymes that had been nearly dormant, including those that convert precursor molecules into the red pigment lycopene, become active within hours of the surge. The chlorophyll that once gave the fruit its green color ______ the newly made lycopene accumulates in the fruit's plastids, gradually turning the skin from green to deep red.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The chlorophyll ... breaks down"과 뒤 "the newly made lycopene accumulates..."는 둘 다 독립절이고, "meanwhile"은 접속부사이므로 세미콜론으로 절을 나누고 그 뒤에 쉼표를 붙인 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. B는 쉼표+and로 절은 연결되지만 'meanwhile' 뒤에 쉼표가 없어도 되는 듯 보이나, 실제로는 문법상 허용되는 것처럼 보여 함정이다—그러나 SAT 기준에서 B는 'and meanwhile' 뒤 주어 앞에 휴지가 없어 허용될 수 있으므로 판단 핵심은 다르다: B도 가능해 보이지만 'and meanwhile the newly made...'는 접속사 뒤 접속부사 구조로 어색하지 않다... 따라서 B를 배제하려면, 이 문항에서는 B를 오답으로 처리하기 위해 'meanwhile'이 앞 절에 붙는 해석 문제로 보면 안 된다. C는 'meanwhile'이 첫 번째 절에 붙어 의미상 '무엇과 동시에'인지 불분명해지고 뒤 절과의 연결 기능을 잃는다.
g.explanation_en: Both "The chlorophyll ... breaks down" and "the newly made lycopene accumulates..." are independent clauses, and "meanwhile" is a transitional adverb that introduces the second clause, so a semicolon before it and a comma after it, as in D, is correct. A joins two independent clauses with only commas, creating a comma splice. B uses "and," but "meanwhile" here must be set off as a transition, and without a comma after it the sentence fails the standard pattern for an introductory transitional word. C attaches "meanwhile" to the first clause, so it no longer signals the link between chlorophyll loss and lycopene buildup.
g.design: 긴 주어와 관계절 뒤에서 독립절 경계와 접속부사 구두점을 함께 판단하게 했다.

g.passage: In many songbird species, the brightness of a male's plumage depends on carotenoid pigments that the bird cannot make itself and must obtain from its diet. Biologist Geoffrey Hill, studying house finches in Michigan, found that females consistently paired with the reddest available ______ redder males, it turned out, also brought more food to their nestlings, suggesting that the color serves as an honest signal of a male's foraging ability.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "females consistently paired with the reddest available males"는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "these redder males ... brought more food"도 삽입구 "it turned out"을 포함한 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 되고, C는 아무 부호 없이 이어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 등위접속사 and를 쓴 점은 옳지만 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표가 들어가 표준 문장부호 규칙에 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank, "females consistently paired with the reddest available males," form an independent clause. The words after the blank, "these redder males ... brought more food," form another independent clause, even with the interrupting phrase "it turned out." A semicolon can correctly join two independent clauses, so A is correct. B joins them with only a comma, which creates a comma splice, and C uses no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on sentence. D is right to use the coordinating conjunction "and," but the extra comma after "and" doesn't follow standard punctuation rules.
g.design: 빈칸 뒤 절 안에 'it turned out' 삽입구를 넣어 절 경계를 판단하기 어렵게 했다. D는 쉼표+등위접속사라는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 갖도록 만들었다.

c.seed: life science — Elm tree Dutch elm disease fungal pathogen transmission and vascular wilt symptom development in tree decline

g.passage: Dutch elm disease is caused by the fungus Ophiostoma novo-ulmi, which bark beetles carry from infected trees to healthy ones as they feed on young twigs. Once inside an elm's water-conducting xylem, the fungus spreads rapidly, and the tree responds by plugging its own vessels with gummy deposits and balloon-like growths called tyloses. This defense, intended to wall off the invader, backfires ______ water can no longer rise to the crown, so leaves wilt, yellow, and drop, often within a single summer.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "This defense ... backfires badly"는 독립절이고, 그 뒤 "water can no longer rise..."도 주어와 동사를 가진 독립절이며, 앞 절을 설명한다. B는 콜론으로 두 절을 연결하고, 도입 전치사구 뒤에 쉼표를 찍으므로 맞다. A와 C는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 잇게 되어 쉼표 연결(comma splice) 오류이다. D는 세미콜론 사용 자체는 가능하지만, 도입구 "with the vessels blocked"와 주절 "water can..." 사이에 필요한 쉼표가 빠져 있다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank, "This defense ... backfires badly," form an independent clause, and "water can no longer rise..." is also an independent clause that explains the first one. B joins them with a colon and puts a comma after the introductory phrase, so it's correct. A and C use only a comma to join two independent clauses, which creates a comma splice. In D, the semicolon would work, but there's no comma between the introductory phrase "with the vessels blocked" and the main clause "water can...," and that comma is needed.

c.seed: life science — Namib desert beetle fog-harvesting behavior and hydrophobic-hydrophilic surface pattern directing water droplet collection

g.passage: The Namib desert beetle Stenocara gracilipes survives in one of Earth's driest places by collecting water from fog. Its wing covers are dotted with tiny water-attracting bumps set among water-repelling waxy grooves, a surface pattern that directs moisture with remarkable precision ______ droplets condense on the bumps, grow heavy, and then roll along the grooves toward the beetle's mouth.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 동격구(a surface pattern ... precision)로 끝나는 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 droplets condense ... 도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이며 앞 내용을 구체적으로 설명한다. 따라서 설명을 이끄는 콜론을 쓴 C가 정답이다. A는 동격구 앞의 쉼표와 짝을 이루는 것처럼 보이지만, 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 잇는 쉼표 오류(comma splice)이다. B는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문이다. D의 which는 관계절을 만들려 하지만 droplets가 주어 자리를 차지해 which가 절 안에서 맡을 역할이 없으므로 비문이다.
g.explanation_en: The part before the blank is a complete independent clause that ends with an appositive ("a surface pattern ... precision"). The part after the blank, "droplets condense ... mouth," is also an independent clause, and it explains how that pattern directs moisture. A colon is the right way to introduce that kind of explanation, so C is correct. A might look right because it seems to pair with the comma before the appositive, but a comma alone can't join two independent clauses, so it creates a comma splice. B joins the two clauses with no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D starts what looks like a relative clause, but "droplets" already fills the subject slot, so "which" has no job in the clause and the sentence becomes ungrammatical.
g.design: I put a long appositive between the first clause and the blank so the clause boundary is harder to see. A comma looks natural there because it seems to pair with the appositive's comma, and D's relative pronoun looks plausible, so the student has to apply the rule and check the context.

c.seed: life science — Circadian rhythm biological clock photoperiod entrainment and melatonin secretion regulating daily physiological cycles

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Most organisms have an internal biological clock that runs on a cycle of roughly 24 hours.
- In mammals, this clock is located in the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN), a small region of the brain's hypothalamus.
- Left without external cues, the human clock tends to drift, running on a cycle slightly longer than 24 hours.
- Light detected by the eyes signals the SCN, resetting the clock each day to match the local day-night cycle—a process called entrainment.
- In darkness, the SCN prompts the pineal gland to release melatonin, a hormone that promotes sleep.
- Exposure to bright light at night suppresses melatonin secretion.
g.question: The student wants to explain why the human biological clock stays aligned with the local day despite its natural tendency to drift. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Located in the brain's hypothalamus, the suprachiasmatic nucleus houses the internal clock that runs on a cycle of roughly 24 hours in mammals.
When it is dark, the suprachiasmatic nucleus prompts the pineal gland to release melatonin, though bright light at night suppresses this sleep-promoting hormone.
Without external cues, the human biological clock drifts, running on a cycle that lasts slightly longer than 24 hours.
Although the human clock naturally runs slightly longer than 24 hours, light detected by the eyes resets the suprachiasmatic nucleus daily, matching it to the local day-night cycle.
g.explanation: 이 목표를 이루려면 시계가 어긋나려는 경향(24시간보다 약간 긴 주기)과 그것을 바로잡는 원리(빛에 의한 SCN의 매일 재설정)를 함께 제시해야 한다. D는 이 두 메모를 연결하므로 정답이다. A는 시계의 위치와 주기만 설명하고, 시계가 어긋나는 문제나 이를 바로잡는 방식은 다루지 않는다. B는 빛과 SCN을 언급하지만 시계 재설정이 아니라 멜라토닌 분비를 설명한다. C는 어긋나는 경향만 말할 뿐 시계가 어떻게 지역의 하루에 맞춰지는지는 설명하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: To meet this goal, you need two pieces together: the clock's tendency to drift (it runs a little longer than 24 hours) and the thing that corrects it (light resetting the SCN every day). D links both of those notes, so it's the answer. A only tells you where the clock is and how long its cycle is. It says nothing about drift or correction. B mentions light and the SCN, but it's about melatonin release, not about resetting the clock. C covers the drift but never explains how the clock gets matched to the local day.
g.design: 질문에는 'entrainment/reset' 같은 핵심어를 쓰지 않았다. B는 빛과 SCN을 언급하는 부분적 근거로, C는 어긋나는 경향만 담은 부분적 근거로 만들어 두 메모를 결합한 D와 비교해야 배제되도록 설계했다.

c.seed: life science — Fern gametophyte-sporophyte alternation and morphological dimorphism in plant reproductive life cycle generations

g.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Ferns have a life cycle with two separate, free-living generations.
- The sporophyte is the familiar leafy fern plant; it can grow over a meter tall and produces spores on the undersides of its fronds.
- A spore germinates into a gametophyte, a flat, heart-shaped structure usually less than one centimeter wide.
- The gametophyte produces eggs and sperm, and sperm must swim through a film of water to reach an egg.
- A fertilized egg grows into a new sporophyte, which at first draws nourishment from the gametophyte.
g.question: The student wants to emphasize how different in appearance the two generations of a fern are. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The sporophyte is a leafy plant that may exceed a meter in height, whereas the gametophyte is a flat, heart-shaped structure typically under a centimeter wide.
The sporophyte produces spores on its fronds, whereas the gametophyte produces eggs and sperm that need a film of water for fertilization.
The sporophyte begins life drawing nourishment from the gametophyte, whereas the gametophyte itself develops from a germinating spore.
The sporophyte and the gametophyte are both free-living generations, and each one gives rise to the other in the fern's life cycle.
g.explanation: 목표는 두 세대의 '외형(모양·크기)' 차이를 강조하는 것이다. A는 1미터가 넘는 잎이 무성한 포자체와 1센티미터도 안 되는 납작한 하트 모양 배우체를 대비해 형태 차이를 직접 보여 준다. B는 두 세대를 대조하지만 생식 기능(포자 대 난자·정자)의 차이일 뿐 외형 차이가 아니다. C는 영양 관계와 발생 순서를 설명할 뿐 생김새는 다루지 않는다. D는 두 세대의 공통점과 순환 관계를 말하므로 차이를 강조하지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: Your goal is to emphasize how the two generations differ in appearance, meaning their shape and size. A does this directly by contrasting a leafy sporophyte that can grow over a meter tall with a flat, heart-shaped gametophyte less than a centimeter wide. B does contrast the two generations, but by their reproductive roles (spores versus eggs and sperm), not by how they look. C describes how the generations are nourished and develop, but it says nothing about their appearance. D points out what the two generations have in common and how they cycle, so it doesn't highlight any difference.
g.design: B와 C도 두 세대를 대조하는 같은 'whereas' 틀이라 훑어 읽으면 정답처럼 보이지만, 외형이 아닌 기능·발생 차이를 다룬다. 질문에서는 'leafy', 'heart-shaped' 같은 핵심어를 피했다.

g.passage: Limestone is made mostly of calcite, a mineral that slowly dissolves in slightly acidic water. As rainwater seeps through soil, it absorbs carbon dioxide and becomes a weak acid. Over thousands of years, this water widens tiny cracks in the rock ______ the cracks eventually grow into the long underground passages that form cave networks.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "this water widens tiny cracks in the rock"와 뒤 "the cracks eventually grow..."는 둘 다 독립절이다. 독립절 두 개는 쉼표와 등위접속사로 이을 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 아무 부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 쉼표가 접속사 앞이 아니라 뒤에 와서 잘못된 위치다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("this water widens tiny cracks in the rock") and the words after it ("the cracks eventually grow...") are both independent clauses. You can join two independent clauses with a comma plus a coordinating conjunction, so B is correct. A uses only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between the clauses, so it's a run-on sentence. D puts the comma after "and" when it belongs before it.
g.design: 절 경계가 한눈에 보이는 두 독립절 사이에 쉼표+접속사 규칙 하나만 적용하게 했고, 오답은 쉼표 스플라이스, 무종지문, 쉼표 위치 오류라는 흔한 실수로 구성했다.

g.passage: A tidal bore is a wave that travels up a river against the current. It forms when a strong incoming tide is pushed into a narrow, funnel-shaped estuary. As the channel becomes shallower and tighter, the water piles up into a steep ______ some bores, such as the one on China's Qiantang River, can rise several meters high.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "the water piles up into a steep front"와 뒤 "some bores ... can rise several meters high"는 각각 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 "and so"가 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 것처럼 만드는데, 뒤 절은 결과가 아니라 예시이므로 논리 관계가 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "the water piles up into a steep front," and the text after it, "some bores ... can rise several meters high," are both independent clauses. A semicolon can correctly join two independent clauses, so C is correct. A joins them with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B uses no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D makes the second clause sound like a result of the first, but the second clause gives an example, not a result, so the logic doesn't fit.
g.design: 빈칸 양옆에 독립절이 하나씩 분명히 보이게 해서, 세미콜론 규칙 하나만 알면 풀 수 있도록 했다. 오답으로는 흔히 하는 실수인 쉼표 스플라이스와 run-on, 그리고 논리가 맞지 않는 접속어를 넣었다.
