c.seed: technology and engineering — Magnetorheological damper electromagnetic coil activation and field-dependent viscosity control in seismic building isolation engineering

g.passage: Engineers who protect buildings from earthquakes have long relied on passive dampers, devices filled with oil that resist motion by a fixed amount. Because their resistance cannot change, such dampers are tuned for an expected range of shaking and may perform poorly when an actual earthquake is stronger or weaker than predicted. Magnetorheological (MR) dampers address this limitation. They contain a fluid packed with tiny iron particles; when an electromagnetic coil inside the damper is energized, the particles align into chains along the magnetic field, and within milliseconds the fluid thickens dramatically. By adjusting the current sent to the coil, a building's control system can make the damper stiffer or softer moment by moment as sensors detect changes in ground motion. Notably, MR dampers need only about as much power as a small light bulb to operate, so they can run on backup batteries if an earthquake cuts off a building's main electricity.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Because passive dampers rely on oil, they are generally more dependable than MR dampers during earthquakes that disrupt a building's electrical supply.
Unlike passive dampers, MR dampers can vary their resistance in response to shaking as it occurs, and their low power demand helps keep them working during an earthquake.
MR dampers work by aligning iron particles into chains, a process that engineers have found takes too long to be useful during sudden ground motion.
Since MR dampers can run on backup batteries, engineers now prefer them to passive dampers mainly for their reduced energy costs in everyday building operation.
g.explanation: 지문은 저항이 고정된 수동형 댐퍼의 한계를 소개한 뒤, MR 댐퍼가 코일 전류를 조절해 실시간으로 점성을 바꿀 수 있고 저전력이라 정전 때도 작동한다는 점을 설명하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 정전을 언급하지만, 지문은 오히려 MR 댐퍼가 배터리로 계속 작동한다고 말하므로 지문과 반대된다. C는 입자 정렬 원리는 맞게 짚지만, 지문은 그 과정이 수 밀리초 안에 일어난다고 하므로 너무 느리다는 주장은 틀렸다. D는 배터리 작동을 언급하지만, 지문은 평상시 에너지 비용 절감이나 엔지니어들의 선호 이유를 다루지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The passage first describes the weakness of passive dampers, whose resistance is fixed. It then explains that MR dampers can change their viscosity moment by moment by adjusting the coil current, and that their low power needs let them keep working during a power outage, so B is correct. A mentions power loss, but the passage says the opposite: MR dampers keep running on backup batteries. C describes the particle alignment correctly, but the passage says it happens within milliseconds, so the claim that it is too slow is wrong. D mentions battery operation, but the passage never discusses everyday energy savings or why engineers prefer one damper over the other.
g.design: 정답을 고르려면 수동형 댐퍼와의 대비와 저전력이라는 장점, 두 정보를 연결해야 한다. 오답 A, C, D는 정전, 입자 정렬, 배터리처럼 지문의 실제 세부 내용을 가져오되 결론을 왜곡해서, 지문과 꼼꼼히 비교해야만 배제되도록 만들었다.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Lithium-ion battery solid electrolyte interphase formation and ionic conductivity cycling stability in electric vehicle energy storage

g.passage:
When a lithium-ion battery is charged for the first time, a small portion of its liquid electrolyte breaks down on the surface of the graphite anode, leaving behind a thin film known as the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). Engineers once treated this film mainly as a cost: forming it consumes lithium that can never again carry charge, so a new cell loses some capacity before it ever powers a vehicle. Yet the SEI also blocks further electrolyte decomposition while still letting lithium ions pass through, and without it the anode would keep eating away at the electrolyte with every cycle.

Recent work by battery researchers suggests that the way the film is first grown matters as much as whether it forms at all. Cells charged slowly at moderate temperatures during manufacturing tend to develop a thin, uniform SEI that conducts ions readily and remains stable over thousands of cycles, whereas rapidly formed films are often thick and patchy, cracking as the anode swells and shrinks. For electric vehicle makers, this means that a slower, more expensive formation step at the factory may pay off in batteries that hold their range for many more years.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Because creating the SEI permanently uses up lithium, engineers are now trying to design anodes that do not require the film at all.
Because the SEI lets lithium ions pass through, rapidly formed films perform about as well as slowly formed ones over long-term use.
Because the SEI both costs some capacity and protects the cell, the conditions under which it first develops strongly affect a battery's long-term durability.
Because fast charging at the factory saves money, electric vehicle makers have largely stopped worrying about how the SEI affects battery range.
g.explanation: 지문은 SEI가 리튬을 소모하는 비용인 동시에 보호막이라는 점을 밝힌 뒤, 초기 형성 조건(느린 충전, 적정 온도)이 수명을 좌우한다고 주장하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 리튬 소모라는 사실은 맞지만, 지문은 SEI를 없애자는 것이 아니라 SEI가 꼭 필요하다고 말한다. B는 이온 통과라는 세부 사항은 맞지만, 빠르게 형성된 막은 두껍고 고르지 않아 갈라진다는 지문 내용과 반대된다. D는 지문이 오히려 비용이 더 드는 느린 형성 단계가 이득일 수 있다고 하므로 틀렸다.
g.explanation_en: The text explains that the SEI costs some lithium but also protects the anode, and then argues that how the film first forms (slowly, at moderate temperatures) decides how long the battery lasts, so C is correct. A uses a true detail about lithium loss, but the text says the SEI is necessary, not something to get rid of. B uses a true detail about ions passing through, but it contradicts the text, which says rapidly formed films are thick, patchy, and crack. D gets it backward: the text suggests a slower, more expensive formation step may be worth paying for.
g.design: To get this right, you have to connect two ideas: the SEI's double role and the claim that formation conditions matter. Choices A and B each take a true detail and then draw a wrong conclusion from it, so they only fall apart when you read closely.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Holographic diffractive grating wavelength selectivity and coherent light reconstruction in three-dimensional medical imaging display technology

g.passage: Holographic displays being developed for surgical planning rely on diffractive gratings recorded in a photosensitive film. Because each grating is tuned to a narrow band of wavelengths, it reconstructs a three-dimensional image of an organ only when illuminated by coherent light of the matching color; light of other wavelengths passes through largely undeflected. This selectivity allows engineers to stack several gratings in a single thin layer, each one responding to its own laser without interfering with the others. ______ the very narrowness that makes stacking possible also makes the display vulnerable: if a laser's output drifts by even a few nanometers as it warms up, the corresponding image dims or blurs, which is why prototype systems require active temperature control of their light sources.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 파장 선택성이 여러 격자를 겹쳐 쌓을 수 있게 해 준다는 장점을 말하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 바로 그 좁은 선택성 때문에 레이저 파장이 조금만 바뀌어도 화질이 떨어지는 약점을 제시한다. 장점을 인정한 뒤 단점으로 방향을 바꾸므로 양보 후 반전을 나타내는 D가 정답이다. A는 선택성이 약점의 원인이라는 점에서 그럴듯해 보이지만, 뒤 문장은 '겹쳐 쌓을 수 있다'는 앞 문장의 결과가 아니라 그와 대비되는 문제점이다. B는 뒤 문장을 앞 문장의 사례로 보지만 새로운 단점을 소개할 뿐이고, C는 비슷한 내용을 덧붙이는 표현이라 장점과 단점의 대비를 나타내지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank describes an advantage: the gratings' wavelength selectivity lets engineers stack them in one layer. The sentence after it points out a drawback that comes from that same narrowness, since a small drift in a laser's wavelength dims or blurs the image. The text admits a benefit and then turns to a weakness, so the answer is D, which signals that kind of contrast. A might look right because selectivity does cause the weakness, but the weakness isn't a result of being able to stack gratings. Instead, it pushes against that point. B is wrong because the second sentence brings up a new problem rather than giving an example of the first claim, and C is wrong because it adds a similar point and misses the shift from advantage to drawback.
g.design: 이 문항은 어휘 단서 없이 장점에서 단점으로 넘어가는 양보 후 반전의 논리를 파악해야 풀 수 있게 만들었다. 같은 성질이 원인이 된다는 점 때문에 A가 그럴듯해 보이도록 했다.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Pneumatic McKibben artificial muscle nylon fiber braiding geometry and compressed air expansion force in soft robotic prosthetic limb actuation

g.passage: A McKibben artificial muscle consists of an inflatable rubber bladder wrapped in a sleeve of braided nylon fibers that cross one another at a shallow angle. When compressed air fills the bladder, the tube pushes outward, and the braid's fibers, which cannot stretch, pivot toward a steeper crossing angle to accommodate the widening tube. ______ the sleeve draws its two ends closer together, shortening along its length much as a biceps does, a motion engineers harness to bend the elbow joint of soft robotic prosthetic arms.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
g.explanation: 앞 문장은 공기가 들어가 튜브가 넓어지면서 늘어나지 않는 섬유가 더 가파른 각도로 회전한다고 설명하고, 뒤 문장은 그 결과로 슬리브가 길이 방향으로 짧아진다고 말하므로 원인-결과 관계인 A가 정답이다. B는 '넓어짐'과 '짧아짐'이 반대 방향처럼 보여 대조로 오해하기 쉽지만, 수축은 팽창과 모순되는 것이 아니라 팽창이 낳는 결과이다. C는 두 문장이 모두 변형을 다루어 유사해 보이지만, 별개의 비슷한 현상이 아니라 같은 과정의 다음 단계이다. D는 뒤 문장이 앞 문장의 일반 진술을 보여 주는 사례가 아니라 새로 생기는 결과이므로 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The first sentence explains that when air widens the tube, the fibers, which can't stretch, pivot to a steeper angle. The next sentence describes what happens because of that: the sleeve gets shorter along its length. That's a cause-and-effect relationship, so A is correct. B is tempting because widening and shortening look like opposite directions, but the shortening doesn't contradict the expansion. It comes from it. C treats the shortening as a separate, similar event, when it's actually the next step in the same process. D is wrong because the second sentence doesn't give an example of the first one. It describes a new outcome.
g.design: This item has no lexical cue. The surface contrast between widening and shortening pulls readers toward "However," but they have to follow the mechanism to see that the shortening is a result. C and D each have a partial basis: both sentences describe deformation, and the second gives specific detail.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Cryogenic liquid nitrogen thermal storage phase-change enthalpy and sensible heat recovery in grid-scale energy buffer systems

g.passage: Liquid air energy storage plants use surplus electricity to cool air until it condenses, then store the liquid in insulated tanks; when demand rises, the liquid is pumped, warmed, and expanded through turbines to generate power. Early designs wasted much of the "cold" released during warming, because the liquid's boiling and subsequent rise to ambient temperature simply dumped heat-absorbing capacity into the atmosphere. __Engineers at several pilot facilities have since begun routing that cold into packed beds of gravel, which hold it as sensible heat and return it to the liquefier during the next charging cycle.__ The change matters because liquefaction is the most energy-intensive step in the process: recycled cold reduces the electricity needed to produce each tonne of liquid air, raising round-trip efficiency from roughly 25 percent toward 50 percent or more.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces a weakness of early plant designs that the final sentence argues has not yet been overcome.
It presents a remedy for the inefficiency identified in the previous sentence, the benefit of which is then explained.
It describes a step in the basic storage cycle outlined in the first sentence, which the final sentence then measures.
It offers an alternative to liquefaction that the final sentence claims is less energy-intensive.
g.explanation: 둘째 문장은 초기 설계가 기화 과정의 '냉열'을 낭비했다는 문제를 제시하고, 밑줄 문장은 그 냉열을 자갈층에 저장해 재사용하는 해결책을 소개하며, 마지막 문장은 그 이점(효율 향상)을 설명하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 마지막 문장이 문제가 해결되고 있음을 보여 주므로 틀렸다. C는 밑줄 문장이 기본 저장 사이클의 일부가 아니라 나중에 추가된 개선책이라는 점을 놓쳤다. D는 냉열 재활용이 액화를 대체하는 것이 아니라 액화에 드는 에너지를 줄여 주는 것이므로 틀렸다.
g.explanation_en: The second sentence points out a problem: early designs wasted the "cold" released as the liquid warmed. The underlined sentence describes a fix, storing that cold in gravel beds so it can be reused, and the final sentence explains why this helps by showing how it raises efficiency. That makes B correct. A is wrong because the final sentence shows the weakness is being overcome, not that it remains. C is wrong because the cold recovery is an improvement added later, not part of the basic cycle described in the first sentence. D is wrong because recycling cold doesn't replace liquefaction; it cuts the energy liquefaction needs.
g.design: 문제-해결-이점 구조로, 오답은 각각 일부 관계(약점, 사이클, 액화 에너지)를 맞게 짚되 연결을 왜곡하도록 같은 문장 틀로 구성했다.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Tribochemical polishing abrasive particle nanoscale interaction and atomic-layer material removal in semiconductor wafer surface planarization

g.passage: Chemical mechanical planarization, the step that flattens silicon wafers between layers of circuitry, was long explained as a simple combination of two forces: a chemical slurry softens the wafer surface, and abrasive particles scrape the softened material away. Under that view, harder or larger particles should remove material faster. __Yet when engineer Mei Tanaka's team tracked individual silica particles sliding across copper films, they found that removal occurred one atomic layer at a time, and only where particle and surface briefly formed chemical bonds that tore away surface atoms as the particle moved on.__ This finding helps explain why some soft, reactive particles outperform harder ones, and it suggests that future slurries may be designed by tuning surface chemistry rather than by increasing abrasive hardness.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents an experimental observation that confirms the traditional account of how abrasive particles remove material from wafers.
It outlines a proposed method for increasing removal rates that the text later recommends adopting in manufacturing.
It reports a finding that challenges the earlier explanation and sets up the text's conclusion about how slurries might be developed.
It describes a limitation of an experiment that the text then argues makes the earlier explanation impossible to test.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해, 경도·크기로 제거율을 설명하던 기존 견해와 달리 원자층 단위의 화학결합 기반 제거를 보여 준다. 이어지는 문장은 이 발견을 근거로 부드러운 입자의 우수성을 설명하고 향후 슬러리 설계 방향을 제시하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 실험 관찰이라는 점은 맞지만 기존 설명을 확인한다고 해서 틀렸다. B는 슬러리 설계로 이어진다는 점은 비슷하지만 밑줄 문장은 방법 제안이 아니라 관찰 보고다. D는 실험의 한계나 검증 불가능성을 언급하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The underlined sentence opens with "Yet," and it shows atomic-layer removal driven by chemical bonding, which contradicts the older view that harder or larger particles remove more material. The next sentence uses this finding to explain why soft particles can work better and to suggest how slurries could be designed, so C is correct. A is right that this is an experimental observation, but it's wrong to say the observation confirms the traditional account. B links to slurry design, but the sentence reports an observation and doesn't propose a method. D is wrong because the text never mentions a limitation of the experiment or says anything can't be tested.
g.design: 오답 A·B에 부분적으로 맞는 요소(실험 관찰, 슬러리 설계로의 연결)를 넣어 두었다. 그래서 'Yet'이 만드는 반박 관계와 마지막 문장과의 연결을 둘 다 확인해야 정답을 고를 수 있다.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Perovskite halide crystal structure bandgap engineering and moisture-induced degradation pathways in thin-film photovoltaic cell reliability

g.passage: Perovskite solar cells can be tuned by swapping the halide ions in their crystal lattice, a strategy known as bandgap engineering. Yet the same ionic flexibility that makes this tuning possible also creates a weakness. When water molecules seep into the thin film, they bond with the organic cations sitting in the gaps of the lattice, gradually loosening the structure until it breaks down into yellow lead iodide ______ therefore testing water-repellent coatings that could block moisture without reducing the cells' efficiency.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 "When water molecules ... lead iodide"는 완전한 문장이고, 빈칸 뒤 "engineers are therefore testing..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이므로 두 절은 마침표로 분리해야 한다. 따라서 정답은 D이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. B는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 run-on 문장이다. C는 관계대명사 which로 시작하지만, testing의 목적어가 이미 coatings로 채워져 있어 which가 절 안에서 맡을 역할이 없으므로 비문이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank, "When water molecules ... lead iodide," make up a complete sentence, and "engineers are therefore testing..." is also an independent clause with its own subject and verb, so the two clauses have to be separated with a period. That makes D the correct answer. A joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B runs the two clauses together with no punctuation at all. C begins with the relative pronoun "which," but "testing" already has its object, "coatings," so "which" has no job to do in its clause, and the sentence is ungrammatical.
g.design: 빈칸 앞에 긴 종속절과 분사구가 있어 문장 경계가 흐려 보인다. 학생은 빈칸 뒤 독립절과 therefore를 확인해야 한다. 오답 C의 관계사절은 그럴듯해 보이지만 목적어가 이미 채워져 있어 성립하지 않는다.

g.passage: In electrospinning, a high voltage draws a charged polymer solution from a needle into a thin jet that whips chaotically before landing as fibers on a collector. Biomedical engineer Lena Okafor found that the whipping instability, long treated as a nuisance in the fabrication of tissue scaffolds, could be tuned: by raising the applied voltage in small, steady increments, her team stretched the jet more evenly during its ______ fibers thin enough to mimic the collagen strands that cells naturally cling to.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 긴 콜론 뒤 독립절 안에서 분사구 경계를 판단해야 하며, 세미콜론·마침표 오답은 앞 콜론과 독립절 구조에 끌리게 설계했다.
g.explanation: 콜론 뒤 독립절 "her team stretched the jet ... during its flight" 다음에 오는 "producing fibers ..."는 결과를 나타내는 분사구이므로 쉼표로 이어 붙이는 것이 맞고, 따라서 정답은 A이다. B는 세미콜론 뒤에 독립절이 와야 하는데 분사구만 남아 틀렸다. C는 "Producing fibers ..."를 따로 떼어 내 동사가 없는 문장 조각을 만든다. D는 "flight producing"으로 분사구가 명사를 꾸미는 것처럼 읽히게 하고, 분사와 그 목적어 "fibers" 사이를 쉼표로 잘못 끊는다.
g.explanation_en: After the colon, the independent clause "her team stretched the jet more evenly during its flight" is followed by "producing fibers...," a participial phrase that describes the result. A comma correctly attaches it, so A is the answer. B puts in a semicolon, but a semicolon has to be followed by an independent clause, and here only a phrase follows. C breaks the phrase off on its own, which leaves a fragment with no main verb. D makes "producing" look like it modifies "flight," and it also puts a comma between the participle and its object, "fibers," which is not allowed.

c.seed: technology and engineering — Osmotic power salinity gradient exploitation and membrane potential driving pressure-retarded osmosis renewable energy generation mechanisms

g.passage: Pressure-retarded osmosis, a method of generating electricity where rivers meet the sea, depends on a semipermeable membrane that lets water molecules pass but blocks dissolved salt. Fresh water naturally migrates across the membrane toward the saltier side, raising the pressure in that chamber. The pressurized brackish water, which engineers route through a turbine before releasing it into the ocean______ the process converts a difference in salinity directly into mechanical work.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: then spins the turbine's blades, in this way,
then spins the turbine's blades; in this way,
then spins the turbine's blades, in this way
then spins the turbine's blades in this way;
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞에는 주어 "The pressurized brackish water"와 비필수 관계절이 있고, 동사 "spins"가 그 주어의 서술어가 되어 첫 독립절이 끝난다. 뒤의 "the process converts..."도 독립절이므로 두 절 사이에 세미콜론이 필요하고, "in this way"는 둘째 절을 이끄는 전환 표현이라 뒤에 쉼표를 둔다. 그래서 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 결합 오류(comma splice)가 되고, C도 같은 오류에 쉼표까지 빠져 있다. D는 세미콜론으로 절을 나누기는 하지만 "in this way"를 첫 절에 붙여 의미가 어긋나고, 둘째 절은 무엇을 가리키는지 알 수 없는 채로 시작된다.
g.explanation_en: Before the blank, you have the subject "The pressurized brackish water" and a nonessential relative clause. The verb "spins" completes that subject, so the first independent clause ends there. What follows, "the process converts...," is also an independent clause, so the two clauses need a semicolon between them. "In this way" introduces the second clause and should be followed by a comma, which makes B correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice, and C has the same error plus a missing comma. D does separate the clauses with a semicolon, but it attaches "in this way" to the first clause, which garbles the meaning and leaves the second clause without the phrase that links it back.
g.design: 긴 비필수 관계절 때문에 주어와 동사 사이가 멀어져 절 경계를 놓치기 쉽게 만들었다. 또 오답 D는 세미콜론을 쓰긴 했지만 위치가 틀린 형태로 넣어, 선택지를 비교해야만 배제되도록 했다.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: technology and engineering — Shape-memory polymer cross-linked network recovery and thermal-triggered molecular chain rearrangement in self-deployable aerospace structures

g.passage: Shape-memory polymers, materials whose cross-linked molecular networks "remember" an original configuration, are increasingly used in self-deploying aerospace structures. A folded antenna boom made of such a polymer can be stowed compactly for launch______ once heated above its transition temperature in orbit, the boom's polymer chains rearrange, and the structure springs back to its programmed shape.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "A folded antenna boom ... for launch"와 뒤 "once heated ..., the boom's polymer chains rearrange..."는 각각 독립절이다. "then"은 등위접속사가 아닌 부사이므로 두 절을 잇는 데는 세미콜론이 필요하고, 그 뒤에 쉼표로 "then"을 구분하는 C가 정답이다. A와 D는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다(D는 'then' 뒤 쉼표도 없음). B는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 run-on 문장이다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("A folded antenna boom ... for launch") and the text after it ("once heated ..., the boom's polymer chains rearrange...") are both independent clauses. Since "then" is an adverb, not a coordinating conjunction, you need a semicolon to join the two clauses, with a comma after "then," which is why C is correct. A and D connect two independent clauses with only a comma, so they're comma splices (D also leaves out the comma after "then"). B joins the clauses with no punctuation at all, so it's a run-on sentence.
g.design: 중간 난이도: 긴 동격 수식어와 'once' 종속절 때문에 뒤 절이 독립절인지 판단해야 하고, 'then'이 접속사가 아님을 인식해야 한다.
